The only guard, line 11 `if (!str[i]) break;`, is wrong-target drift: it tests the byte value (NUL) and never constrains the index i, so it admits i >= 1024. A witness of 1024 consecutive non-NUL bytes admitted by every guard iteration reaches i == 1024 and performs an out-of-bounds stack write at this sink (CWE-121). The absent fix is a pre-write bound check such as `if (i >= sizeof(str) - 1) break;` to leave room for the NUL terminator; ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE at line 14 runs after the loop and provides no protection.

assumptions: `char str[1024]` declares a 1024-element stack array addressable at indices 0..1023.
`gf_bs_read_u8(bs)` returns any byte value (0-255) from the parsed file, i.e., entry-point-controlled data, since no constraint on it appears in the fragment.
Standard semantics: the loop writes the terminating NUL at the current index before breaking, so a run of 1024 non-NUL bytes writes the NUL (or the next byte) at index 1024, out of bounds.
limitations: Downstream corruption (e.g., `gf_strdup(str)` at line 16 reading an unterminated or out-of-bounds string) is not needed to confirm the flaw and is not asserted.
If the bitstream were exhausted mid-flight, `gf_bs_read_u8` behavior is not shown, but an attacker can simply supply the required non-NUL bytes, so this does not constrain the witness.

verdict.summary: dev->card_label, whose contents are never constrained, validated, or sanitized in this fragment, is passed as the format-string argument to snprintf at line 14 instead of as a '%s' argument. Any label containing '%' conversions (e.g. %n, %s) is interpreted by the kernel's vsnprintf, giving an unchecked read/write primitive. The labellen min-size computation (lines 5-7) only caps the output length and does not protect the format interpretation.

evidence.reason: Interpretive sink: dev->card_label is supplied in the format position of snprintf. Its content is unconstrained within the fragment (no validation or sanitization shown); labellen (lines 5-7) bounds bytes written, not the %-specifiers consumed, so it fails the Guard-Identity Audit (wrong-property drift, class 4). A card_label containing e.g. '%n' or '%s' is admitted on every path (no branch guards line 14) and drives a kernel format-string read/write. Absent fix: pass a literal format, snprintf(cap->card, labellen, "%s", dev->card_label). Primary mechanism: CWE-134 improperly controlled format string.

assumptions: sizeof(cap->card) and sizeof(dev->card_label) are compile-time capacities available at lines 5-7.
snprintf treats its third argument as the format string and consumes '%-specifiers it contains (standard C/library semantics).
cap is the framework-supplied output buffer and is non-NULL on this path.
limitations: The setter of dev->card_label is not shown in this fragment; it is treated as a user-configurable value whose content the fragment never constrains.
The return of video_get_drvdata(dev->vdev) (line 9) is dereferenced without a NULL check, but no shown producer can make it NULL, so that is not promoted to a finding.
Exploitation impact is not demonstrated; the verdict rests on the unvalidated attacker-controlled value reaching the interpretive sink.

verdict.summary: RTCP XR block length rb_len is read from the packet (line 25) and never validated against the remaining packet words; block pointers stored in the loop (lines 31/34/37/40) are dereferenced by fixed struct offsets after the loop (lines 139-175), so an attacker-controlled rb_len lets field reads run past the end of the received buffer: heap out-of-bounds read.

evidence.reason: rb_stats was stored at line 37 from rb_hdr (packet word 1) with no validation of the block extent rb_len (line 25, max 65535). The capacity bound is line 19-20: size/4 >= pkt_len+1, admitting a minimal 12-byte packet (pkt_len=2). The loop guard line 23 constrains only the 32-bit start word (rb_hdr < pkt+pkt_len), not the block length, and line 138 'if (rb_stats)' excludes only NULL (guard-identity drift class 3: wrong-target — start pointer bounded, fixed-offset sink unconstrained). With one BT_STATS block at word 1, rb_len=1, flags l-bit set, rb_stats->lost reads bytes 12-15, past the 12-byte buffer. Absent one-statement fix: per-block check that rb_len+1 <= (pkt_len - ((pj_int32_t*)rb_hdr - (pj_int32_t*)pkt)) before store/advance at lines 46-47. Confirmed CWE-125 out-of-bounds read.

Same unvalidated rb_len chain as line 155: with size=12, pkt_len=2 (admitted by line 19), rb_len=1 and the j-flag bit set, rb_stats->jitter_min sits at struct offset 16, i.e. absolute byte 20 of the 12-byte accepted packet, reading up to 12 bytes past the buffer end. No guard on the path (line 23 start-pointer only; line 138 NULL-only) constrains the read extent; the absent per-block bound (`rb_len+1` vs remaining packet words, to be placed before line 46-47) would exclude this witness. Confirmed CWE-125 out-of-bounds read.

assumptions: RTCP length field counts 32-bit words after the 4-byte common header, so the valid packet occupies pkt_len+1 words; this matches the check at line 19 and the buf start after common at lines 5/10-11.
Block length semantics: a block consumes rb_len+1 words (block advance at line 46-47), consistent with RFC 3611.
Field offsets used for rb_stats->lost / jitter_min follow the PJSIP pjmedia_rtcp_xr_rb_stats layout (header 4B, begin_seq 2B, end_seq 2B, lost 4B, dup 4B, jitter fields after).
limitations: Whether the receive buffer is exactly `size` bytes is caller-dependent; the fragment itself authorizes access only within the 4*(pkt_len+1)-byte packet region via line 19-20, and the witness uses the minimum allowed size, so the OOB read is real for a minimal datagram.

Pointer formation at line 46-47 with unvalidated rb_len is technically UB (out-of-bounds pointer) but is not dereferenced inside the loop, so it is folded into the same CWE-125 finding rather than a separate one.
sess is assumed non-NULL (no NULL producer shown in the fragment); no OOB write was identified because all stores target sess.

verdict.summary: FractionalAvgPoolGrad writes into the intermediate in_backprop matrix without constraining out_backprop's batch/depth dimensions against the original input shape, so an entry-point-supplied tensor with out_batch > in_batch (or out_depth > in_depth) reaches coeffRef(d, in_index) with an out-of-range index and performs a heap OOB write.

evidence.reason: Write sink: coeffRef returns a reference used for += (L133-134). Matrix capacity is rows=in_depth, cols=in_cols*in_rows*in_batch (L86-88). d is bounded only by out_depth (L128) and in_index contains b*in_rows (L126) with b bounded only by out_batch (L96). Neither out_depth nor out_batch is compared to in_depth/in_batch by any shown guard: L24-26, L38-49, L59-70, L103-106, L114-118 all pass for witness orig_input_tensor_shape=[1,1,1,1], out_backprop=[2,1,1,1], row/col_seq=[0,1] (out_batch=2>in_batch=1 gives in_index=(1*1+0)*1+0=1 >= cols=1; out_depth=2>in_depth=1 gives d=1 >= rows=1), so the write is out of bounds. Absent fix: an OP_REQUIRES constraining out_batch<=in_batch and out_depth<=in_depth (or requiring shape equality) before the write loops. Primary CWE-787 heap out-of-bounds write.

assumptions: Eigen Dynamic Matrix coeffRef performs offset-based addressing without bounds checks, so d>=in_depth or in_index>=in_cols*in_rows*in_batch is an out-of-bounds write (matrix dims at L87-88: rows=in_depth, cols=in_cols*in_rows*in_batch).
out_backprop dims at L33-36 and orig_input_tensor_shape flat values at L55-58 are entry-point tensor data; no shown statement couples them.
row/col sequence reads (L98-L111) are in bounds because L38-49 require NumElements > out_rows/out_cols.
limitations: In real TensorFlow the registered gradient typically passes shape-consistent tensors, but that invariant is not visible in this fragment and was not relied on.

The absent one-statement fix is the fail-closed form used correctly at lines 186/194: 'if (r < 0 && r != -EFAULT)'. Absent fix: 'if (r < 0 && r != -EFAULT)' fail-closed check; primary CWE-754.

assumptions: seccomp_init(SCMP_ACT_ALLOW) at line 146 makes the policy default-allow, so an uninstalled blocking rule leaves its syscall permitted.

libseccomp returns negative errno values on rule-add failure; per the in-fragment comment, -EFAULT denotes 'unknown syscall' and is the intentionally tolerated case, so all other negatives are genuine failures.

The concrete kernel exploit following an unblocked syscall is outside this fragment; the confirmed defect is the fail-open status handling itself.

assumptions: TFLITE_DCHECK_EQ at line 10 has the standard DCHECK macro semantics: it is a debug-only assertion that is compiled out under NDEBUG, so it does not constrain release-build runtime behavior.
The array_data buffer's capacity is array_size elements, as the fragment itself derives the array extent from array_size at lines 13 and 58.

verdict.summary: The RTCP XR parser contains a packet-fit sanity check and per-block-type size checks that bound every packet read to the supplied `size`; all dangerous read operations in the parse loop and payload consumption are covered, so no out-of-bounds condition is reachable from the fragment.

verdict.summary: Heap out-of-bounds write in ReadPCLImage: density and options are 1-byte allocations from AcquireString("") (lines 186-187), then unconditionally written by FormatLocaleString with a MaxTextExtent write budget (lines 188-189, 191, 196-197, 204-205, 207-209). Identical structure to the verify_certificate_hash_list_ loop: the byte count equals the element's exact in-bounds span, so no memory failure set exists for the read, and the rc==1 assertion at line 31 stops the path on failure.

Container .data()/.size() contract holds for the list elements: reading size()*sizeof(value_type) bytes is exactly in-bounds.

limitations: The element type of verify_certificate_hash_list_ and verify_certificate_spki_list_ is not shown; analysis assumes byte containers (sizeof(value_type) == 1), for which no size_t multiplication overflow is derivable for an allocated container.

verdict.summary: concat_dim is read from an attacker-controlled DT_INT64 0-D tensor with no shown constraint (lines 56-59). The guard at line 68 relies on min_rank computed at line 62 as 'concat_dim + 1' (or '-concat_dim'); for concat_dim = INT64_MAX this signed addition overflows to INT64_MIN, so WithRankAtLeast(input, min_rank) admits the value and the out-of-range axis reaches c->Dim(input, concat_dim) and c->Subshape(..., concat_dim, ...), an OOB index read (CWE-125) rooted in the overflowing bound computation (CWE-190). evidence.reason: concat_dim (int64_t) has full attacker-controlled domain from lines 56-59 with no shown constraint. Line 62 derives min_rank = concat_dim + 1 for non-negative values; at concat_dim = INT64_MAX the addition wraps to INT64_MIN, so the guard at line 68 (WithRankAtLeast(input, min_rank)) admits the value on every path, and Dim indexes the input shape's dims with INT64_MAX, out of range for any realized rank. Guard-Identity Audit fails as transformation drift (class 4): the checked quantity min_rank is an overflowing transform of the sink's value. Absent fix: a direct, overflow-free range check (reject concat_dim < -rank || concat_dim >= rank) placed before this Dim/Subshape use. Mechanism: OOB read whose root cause is the signed overflow in the bounds computation (CWE-190 secondary).

Same unconstrained concat_dim (lines 56-59) reaches this second sink inside the loop (lines 77-96). The per-iteration guard at line 88 is the same overflowed WithRankAtLeast(input, min_rank) with min_rank wrapped to INT64_MIN at concat_dim = INT64_MAX, so the value is admitted and indexes the shape out of range. The concat_dim == -1 branch at line 86 does not exclude INT64_MAX, so this else-path sink is reached. Absent fix: overflow-free rank-range validation of concat_dim before the index use.

assumptions: concat_dim_t is the 0-D concat-axis tensor and flat<int32/int64>()(0) reads its single element (lines 56-59).
WithRankAtLeast(input, min_rank) compares the input rank against min_rank and trivially succeeds when min_rank is negative (INT64_MIN after the wrap).
Two's-complement wrap semantics for INT64_MAX + 1 and -INT64_MIN on the fragment's target compilers.
limitations: Dim/Subshape bodies are not shown; if they internally bounds-check, the concrete fault downgrades to a failed shape-inference error, but the out-of-domain index itself is the demonstrated unconstrained-value failure under standard indexing semantics.
The DT_INT32 concat-axis path (line 57) is fully protected: min_rank stays within int64 range for all int32 values.
The input shape's numeric rank capacity is not separately declared in the main branch, capping the confidence of the concrete OOB at 0.65.
start_value_index/end_value_index/dim_index have no shown call site, so attacker control over loop bounds is not confirmable from the fragment.

verdict.summary: The fragment carries the protecting pre-loop bound check (lines 14-15) that ties the file-supplied entry_count to the remaining box payload using the exact per-entry byte counts (long_offsets ? 16 : 12), which match the byte consumption of each loop iteration (lines 22+25 or 22+28). Every admitted entry_count is therefore fully consumable within ptr->size, and the global-entry reads are each gated by an ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE call; no dangerous operation receives an unconstrained value.

evidence.reason: entry_count is a u32 read from the entry-point bitstream (line 13) with a residual range of 0..UINT32_MAX until this guard. The guard admits only entry_count where size / (16 or 12) >= entry_count, i.e. size >= entry_count*bytes_per_entry, and each loop iteration consumes exactly 16 bytes (lines 22+25, long_offsets) or 12 bytes (lines 22+28) — identical to the divisor — so the last read leaves >= 0 payload bytes and cannot overrun the box accounting (CWE-125). Guard-Identity Audit passes: no statement between line 14 and the loop at line 17 modifies entry_count, long_offsets, or size. Degenerate inputs are covered: entry_count=0 yields zero iterations; any count exceeding the remaining payload (e.g. size=11, long_offsets=1, count=1 -> 11/16=0 < 1) is rejected. The absent-fix question is moot because the complete bound check is present, so the failure set of the local-entry reads is empty.

assumptions: ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE is GPAC's standard check-and-decrement macro: if the remaining size is less than the requested bytes it returns GF_ISOM_INVALID_FILE, otherwise it subtracts the bytes; this is required for the per-field guards in the global-entry loop.
ptr->size tracks the unread payload bytes of this box and is decremented by each ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE, so the line 14-15 comparison accounts exactly for the bytes the local loop will consume.
gf_malloc is assumed to return NULL on allocation failure, matching the explicit checks at lines 19 and 39.
limitations: The global-entry loop (lines 37-62) lacks a count-versus-size precheck on global_entry_count; a finding is not confirmed because every global-entry read is individually gated by ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE (lines 40/43/47/52/56), which bounds each access to the remaining payload.

A large global_entry_count can cause many small allocations, but each iteration requires at least 16 payload bytes, so iterations are bounded by the box payload size; no unbounded resource exhaustion is demonstrated in-fragment.

The protective semantics of ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE are inferred from its name and uniform usage pattern; a hypothetical decrement-only variant (not GPAC semantics) would be needed to make the global loop reads unsafe.

verdict.summary: n and nrhs are extracted via input.dim_size(ndims - 1) and rhs.dim_size(ndims - 1) before the ndims >= 2 and rhs.dims() == ndims checks (lines 8-16) execute. This indexes rhs's shape with input's ndims - 1 before rhs.dims() == ndims (line 12) is checked: ndims == 0 yields index -1, and ndims == 3 with rhs rank 1 yields index 2 on a rank-1 shape, both OOB reads inside dim_size. The guard at lines 12-16 runs after the use and fails the ordering audit. Absent fix: validate rhs.dims() against ndims before this read (CWE-125).

assumptions: input.dims() and rhs.dims() return nonnegative ints; TensorShape::dim_size(d) indexes the internal dims array and performs an out-of-bounds read for d < 0 or d >= rank in release builds (DCHECKs are debug-only).
Tensor shapes passed to the kernel are attacker-controlled entry-point data; the two inputs' ranks are not pre-validated by kernel dispatch before ComputeAsync runs.
limitations: The body of dim_size is not shown in the fragment; its OOB behavior relies on standard TensorShape accessor semantics.
Loops use int batch against int64 batch_size; overflow would require batch_size > 2^31, not producible with realistic tensor sizes, so it is not counted as a finding.
Huge-shape int64 product overflow in NumElements()/shape arithmetic would require impractically large tensors and is out of scope.

verdict.summary: All entry-point-derived indices (start, delete, items, delta) are constrained by the visible clamps at L26/L32/L42 and the NJS_MAX_LENGTH guard at L47, so every memory/property operation (deletion copy, memcpy, copy_within, delete/set loops) stays within its capacity; no dangerous operation admits an unconstrained value.

evidence.reason: Decisive clamp: admits start in [0, length], excluding all negative values and values above length; every later sink index (n = start+i, memcpy destination start, copy_within to = start+items) consumes this same int64 start with no intermediate modification (no guard-identity drift).

Decisive clamp: admits delete in [0, length - start] (and the nargs==2 path sets delete = length - start at L32), so start + delete <= length on every path; this invariant bounds the L61-63 read loop and keeps both copy_within counts (L105, L124) non-negative.

Decisive guard: rejects the operation whenever length + delta exceeds NJS_MAX_LENGTH, so the post-splice length and every index <= length + delta used by the memcpy (L116-117) and the property-set loop (L139-144) stay within the permitted capacity; no shrink path can underflow because length + delta >= start >= 0.

OOB write/read sink fully protected: loop guard i < delete (L61) admits i in [0, delete) inside deleted, whose capacity is delete from the allocation at L54; read index n = start + i < start + delete <= length, inside array->start (fast-array buffer length >= array->length); no residual-range value exceeds either capacity.

memcpy sink fully protected: destination [start, start+items) ends at start+items = start+delete+delta <= length+delta <= NJS_MAX_LENGTH (L26/L42/L47); when delta > 0, njs_array_expand (L98) grows capacity to at least length+delta; when delta <= 0, start+items <= start+delete <= length inside the existing fast-array buffer; source args[3..nargs-1] is exactly items = nargs-3 values. No admitted value violates a capacity.

assumptions: njs_is_fast_array/njs_array imply a contiguous start buffer holding array->length elements with capacity >= length.
njs_array_alloc(vm, 0, delete, 0) returns an array capable of holding delete elements.
njs_array_expand(vm, array, 0, delta) grows capacity to at least length + delta on success.
njs_object_length returns the array's length such that length == array->length for fast arrays.
Helper return semantics follow their checked NJS_OK / NJS_ERROR contract as used in the fragment.
limitations: Helper bodies (njs_array_alloc, njs_array_expand, njs_array_copy_within, njs_object_length) are not shown; the safe conclusion relies on their standard njs semantics together with the in-fragment clamps, not on unshown invariants.
Safety of args[3] assumes the VM passes exactly nargs values in args, per the standard call contract; a caller violating that is outside the fragment's derivable trust.
The TODO stubs (ArraySpeciesCreate/CreateDataPropertyOrThrow) are ECMAScript spec-compliance items, not memory-safety sinks.
No dangerous operation failed confirmation, so the verdict rests on the complete guarded inventory rather than any uncovered flaw.

verdict.summary: Heap out-of-bounds write in GetEXIFProperty's all-tags mode: key is allocated with exactly strlen(property)+1 bytes (line 761), then FormatLocaleString(key,MaxTextExtent,"%s",description) (lines 783-784) writes a description of up to 36 bytes into it. limitations: No call site for GetEXIFProperty is shown; property provenance is derived wholly in-fragment (line 447 admits length-6 strings and line 453 selects the all-mode). Standard ImageMagick callers request all tags with "exif:*", which is exactly the failing witness.
Not assessed: OOM-induced NULL from NewSplayTree/AcquireQuantumMemory is not attacker-controllable here and is not a finding.

verdict.summary: Attacker-controlled 4-bit size fields (offset_size/length_size at lines 7-8, unconstrained 0..15) allow the extent loop (line 53) to run up to 65535 iterations per item while consuming 0 box bytes (line 66 decrements offset_size+length_size=0), and with version<2 item_count=65535 (line 17) a ~393 KB iloc box drives ~4.29e9 allocations at line 55 -> OOM (CWE-770). GF_SAFEALLOC is zero-initializing and may return NULL on allocation failure (checked at lines 26 and 56).
gf_list_new()/gf_list_add() are malloc-backed and may fail/OOM.
The box byte accounting at lines 43, 60, and 66 exactly matches the bytes consumed by the corresponding bit reads.
limitations: Bit widths up to 8*15=120 bits at lines 45, 61, 68-69 exceed typical 64-bit gf_bs_read_int limits, but because the byte accounting keeps every read inside the box, any harm depends on callee-internal behavior and is not confirmable from the fragment.
The CWE-476 NULL deref requires an allocation failure (OOM), which depends on system memory; it is independently enabled by the confirmed CWE-770 amplification.
Termination is guaranteed by the fixed 16/32-bit loop counters even in the amplification path; the failure is memory blow-up, not non-termination.
The resource-amplification finding rests on an exotic but reachable configuration (version<2, offset_size=length_size=base_offset_size=0) that the fragment never excludes.

verdict.summary: flatpak_dir_ensure_bundle_remote silently succeeds with *out_metadata = NULL when a bundle's header lacks metadata: a crafted bundle yields fp_metadata == NULL (L30) and the caller (bundle-install transaction) is not given the permission metadata it requested, so the requested permissions are not presented/verified (fail-open). assumptions: flatpak_bundle_load may succeed while leaving out-parameter fp_metadata NULL when the bundle header has no metadata entry; no visible constraint in the fragment bounds it (the absence of that constraint is the vulnerability's root).

limitations: The downstream user-visible impact (permission prompt skipped in the transaction caller) lives in unshown callers; the finding rests on the in-fragment fail-open success return with NULL metadata.

verdict.summary: Integer overflow in the constant-size limit check at L29-30: out_shape.num_elements() (int64_t, fully defined but unbounded in magnitude) is multiplied by DataTypeSize(n->output_type(i)) (size_t); the product wraps, so an oversized fully-defined shape (e.g., 2^61 elements of an 8-byte type) passes the `> max_constant_size_in_bytes` test, the node is declared constant-foldable, and a cap-bypassing constant materialization (OOM/DoS) is admitted.

Phase 1 residual range: num_elements() is int64_t and is only gated by out_shape.IsFullyDefined() (L28), which bounds definiteness, not magnitude; DataTypeSize returns size_t. The product is evaluated in unsigned 64-bit, so num_elements()=2^61 with an 8-byte output type wraps to 0 and fails to exceed max_constant_size_in_bytes, skipping `return false` (L31) and labeling an actually 2^64-byte constant as foldable. Guards on the path (L22, L25, L28) do not constrain the operand magnitude; the absent fix is a division-based comparison (num_elements() > max_constant_size_in_bytes / DataTypeSize(...)) or an explicit pre-multiply overflow check. Primary CWE-190 (wraparound root cause); secondary CWE-770 as the cap bypass admits unbounded constant allocation.

assumptions: IsFullyDefined() implies num_elements() >= 0 and returns the exact product of the shape's dimensions, but imposes no upper magnitude bound within the fragment.
DataTypeSize() follows standard semantics: returns a positive byte size (size_t) for the node's output type.
shape_map, consider, and shape_replacement_map are the fragment's only external data sources; their contents are consumed without further shown validation.
limitations: Potential OOB read of n->output_type(i) (i derived from the shape-vector length) is not confirmable: the node's output-count capacity is not declared or computed in the fragment.

The downstream constant materialization/allocation is not shown; the resource-exhaustion consequence (CWE-770) is inferred from the gate's role, while the overflow itself is fully confirmed inside the fragment.
NULL-deref analysis for n is out of scope: no statement in the fragment can produce a NULL n.

verdict.summary: The size_t addition `length += dir->length` at line 12 can wrap, and the `length > NJS_MAX_PATH` guard at line 25 tests only the wrapped sum, so a wrapped-small length is admitted while `njs_cpymem` at line 39 (and line 32) copies the untruncated operand lengths (e.g., SIZE_MAX-scale) into the stack buffer `src[NJS_MAX_PATH + 1]` (line 6), producing an out-of-bounds write. njs_cpymem copies n bytes and returns dst+n, per its standard memcpy-style semantics.
njs_slow_path is only a branch-prediction hint; the guarded condition executes normally.
src capacity is exactly NJS_MAX_PATH + 1 as declared at line 6; the straggler NUL write at line 40 is the reason the +1 exists.
limitations: dir and info are helper parameters with no shown call site, so attacker control of their lengths is not directly evidenced inside the fragment (category (c) analysis); the overflow witness therefore relies on degenerate, near-SIZE_MAX operand lengths.

Line 18's `dir->start[dir->length - 1]` read with `dir->length == 0` (index SIZE_MAX) is admitted by the line 14 guard when `info->name.length > 0`, but dir->start's capacity is not shown, so the CWE-125 capacity requirement is not met; kept as a candidate only.

The decisive finding is a defensible-hardening-adjacent extreme boundary (wrap), though the mechanism (guard testing a wrapped value while the sink consumes raw operands) is fully demonstrated in-fragment.

Whether the scanner helpers guarantee forward progress between delimiters (e.g., whitespace between attributes) is not shown; that path is not used as a witness — the EOF/terminator-suppression witnesses stand on the shown control flow alone.

verdict.summary: The only dangerous arithmetic in the fragment is num_filters % rank (L28) and num_filters / rank (L29), whose entire failure set {rank == 0} is excluded by the verbatim guard TF_LITE_ENSURE(context, rank != 0) at L27, evaluated before both uses on every path. evidence.reason: Sink reads byte offset 12 (p = hdr + sizeof(*hdr), line 28) and requires length >= 13. The capacity line is line 12 ('length >= sizeof(pjmedia_rtcp_fb_common)'), admitting exactly 12 bytes, and line 25 ('if (length < rpsi_len + 12)') admits length == 12 when rpsi_len == 0. rpsi_len == 0 is reachable because line 18 guards the raw host-order member ('hdr->rtcp_common.length < 3'), not the pj_ntohs-converted value used at line 24 (guard-identity drift class: type/precision/byte order), so network length 2 is admitted on little-endian hosts. The absent one-statement fix is an ntohs-based reject (e.g., 'if (pj_ntohs((pj_uint16_t)hdr->rtcp_common.length) < 3) return PJ_ETOOSMALL;') or 'if (length < rpsi_len + 13)' before this read; without it an attacker-controlled 12-byte datagram triggers a 1-byte out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

assumptions: sizeof(pjmedia_rtcp_fb_common) == 12, matching the capacity enforced at line 12.
hdr->rtcp_common.length is a 16-bit field in network byte order, evidenced by pj_ntohs() at line 24.
length is the size of the externally supplied RTCP datagram (entry-point input), so a 12-byte attacker datagram yields length == 12.
limitations: The over-read requires a little-endian host; on big-endian hosts line 18 rejects network length 2, so the witness is platform-dependent.
Only the single-byte read at line 29 is confirmed out of bounds; the pt read (line 43) and pj_strset range (line 45) remain within the admitted buffer on all reaching paths.
Callers are not shown; the length == 12, rpsi_len == 0 combination is derived from an attacker-crafted 12-byte RTCP PSFB packet, not from any caller-visible API contract.

verdict.summary: The only NULL-producing call (vim_strsave at line 33) is fully guarded: the `if (p != NULL)` check at line 34 excludes the entire NULL failure set from ml_append (line 36) and vim_free (line 37), with no intervening mutation (guard-identity audit passes). u_save's FAIL status is checked fail-closed at line 25. The corrupted ref is consumed only by a later, unshown operation, so this does not confirm an in-fragment OOB write/read and is recorded as a robustness/logic concern.

verdict.summary: ReadCINImage copies a file-controlled row size into a fixed-size quantum buffer: image->depth is an unvalidated 0..255 byte (lines 134/340), so length=GetBytesPerRow(...) (lines 379/383) can exceed the pixels buffer extent computed at line 377 and discarded at line 378, and ReadBlobStream at line 395 heap-overflows pixels. The columns*rows/8-vs-blobsize check at line 348 bounds total data, not per-row length vs buffer capacity.

evidence.reason: Heap overflow (CWE-787): length is derived from attacker-controlled image->depth (channel[0].bits_per_pixel, a 0..255 byte read at line 134, assigned unvalidated at line 340) via GetBytesPerRow(image->columns,3,image->depth,MagickTrue) at line 379 (or 1 sample at line 383), while pixels is the GetQuantumPixels buffer whose capacity is the extent computed at line 377 (GetQuantumExtent with quantum depth 32 = 12*columns RGB / 4*columns Gray) and thrown away at line 378. Witness depth=33, columns=1000, rows=1, number_channels=3: length=(1000*3*33+7)/8=12375 padded to 12376 > extent=12000, so ReadBlobStream writes 12376 bytes into a 12000-byte buffer. The only nearby check, line 348 (columns*rows/8 <= GetBlobSize), constrains total pixel data vs file size, not per-row length vs buffer capacity (wrong-target drift), and admits this witness (125 <= blobsize for a ~15KB file); guard 396 (count != length) runs after the write and protects nothing. Absent fix: 'if (length > extent) ThrowReaderException(...)' or a bound on image->depth (e.g., 'image->depth > 32') placed between lines 379/383 and 395.

assumptions: GetQuantumExtent (line 377) returns the per-row bytes needed for the chosen quantum_type at the 32-bit quantum depth set at line 374, i.e., 12*columns for RGBQuantum and 4*columns for GrayQuantum.

GetQuantumPixels (line 386) returns the quantum buffer allocated to that extent; ReadBlobStream (line 395) writes up to length bytes into it; GetBytesPerRow (lines 379/383) computes padded ceil(columns*samples*depth/8).
ReadBlobLong returns a 32-bit unsigned value, so columns/rows are <= 2^32-1; bits_per_pixel is an unsigned byte 0..255 with no shown cap.
cin is zero-initialized at line 71, so partially-read header fields are not uninitialized.
limitations: The exact allocation size of pixels rests on standard API semantics of GetQuantumExtent/GetQuantumPixels since their bodies are not shown; the fragment itself computes and then discards the relevant extent at lines 377-378.
A crafted depth=33 file overflows by ~376 bytes per row; downstream crash/exploitation is not demonstrated, so severity is high (direct memory corruption) rather than critical.
The line-348 check does bound total pixel extent, so a separate huge columns*rows allocation/DoS via SetImageExtent (line 361) is demoted.
The user-data read (lines 322-339) is properly guarded by the GetBlobSize check at line 330 and is not part of this finding.

verdict.summary: In dynamicGetbuf, the guard `if (remain >= len)` (line 11) only bounds rlen from above and never excludes a negative `len`, so on the then-path `rlen = len` can be negative. The negative int is converted to a huge size_t in `memcpy` (line 20), producing an out-of-bounds write to `buf` and read from `dp->data + dp->pos` (heap buffer overflow). The missing fix is a `len <= 0` (or `rlen < 0`) guard before the copy.

A negative int for rlen promotes to a huge unsigned size_t (CWE-195 signed-to-unsigned negative size), and memcpy then performs an out-of-bounds write/read (CWE-787); the buffer capacities are the caller-supplied len-bytes regions, and the copy size exceeds any such region. The else-branch EOF check (lines 14-16) only protects the rlen=remain path, not this one. Absent protective statement: `if (len <= 0) return EOF;` before the length decision.

assumptions: memcpy's size parameter is size_t, so a negative int rlen promotes to a huge unsigned length (standard C semantics).
int is signed and at least 32-bit, so -1 and INT_MIN are representable values of len.
limitations: No call site of dynamicGetbuf is shown, so the negative-len caller is not demonstrated in the fragment; the finding rests on the fully visible missing lower-bound check feeding the visible memcpy sink.

Derived capacities of buf and dp->data are not declared in the fragment; the failure is shown via the negative-size-to-huge-size_t conversion rather than a numeric comparison against a declared capacity.
No NULL producer for ctx, dctx->dp, or buf exists in the fragment, so NULL-dereference candidates were not confirmed.

verdict.summary: njs_function_frame_save() copies the entire active frame into the saved (awaited) frame at line 8 without re-initializing the spare-memory management fields native.size, native.free and native.free_size. The saved frame therefore retains pointers to memory owned by the transient active frame; the standard njs fix initializes those fields to 0/NULL (ad48705), and its absence lets a later njs_function_frame_alloc() on the restored frame reuse already-freed spare memory, causing use-after-free.

evidence.reason: Line 8 unconditionally copies every field of vm->active_frame into the persistent saved frame, including the spare-memory fields native.size, native.free and native.free_size (standard njs frame-allocator semantics). No statement in the fragment re-initializes or clears these fields: lines 9-27 overwrite only previous_active_frame, arguments, arguments_offset, local, temp and pc, so the residual range of the copied spare-memory pointers is unconstrained and equals the active frame's live pointers. The absent protective statement is the initialization 'native->size = 0; native->free = NULL; native->free_size = 0;' right after 'native = &frame->native;' (line 11) — this is the verbatim fix of njs commit ad48705. When the saved await frame is restored and passed to njs_function_frame_alloc(), the stale free/free_size/size fields select spare memory that may already be freed, yielding a use-after-free (CWE-416). Guard-identity audit: no guard exists on this path, so every admitted value reaches the copy unconstrained.

assumptions: njs_native_frame_t contains the spare-memory fields size/free/free_size; their meaning follows the njs frame allocator (njs_function_frame_alloc/njs_function_frame_free), and line 8 propagates them by whole-struct copy.

njs_function_frame_value_count()/njs_function_frame_values() return the active frame's value count and value extent, which bound the first copy loop; the pointer-array capacity computed at lines 19-20 (value_count + function->u.lambda->temp) is visible in the fragment.
limitations: The actual dereference of the stale spare-memory pointers happens in the unshown restore/allocation path (njs_function_frame_alloc), so the fragment itself only persists the dangling pointers; the CWE-416 mechanism is confirmed by the missing initialization that the real fix (ad48705) adds to this exact function.

Line 24 ('value + (function->args_offset - 1)') could underflow if args_offset == 0, but no in-fragment producer guarantees args_offset == 0 and the resulting pointer is only stored, not dereferenced in the fragment; demoted.

The second loop (lines 42-48) writes args_count pointers starting at new[args_count(active)+args_offset]; an OOB would require active locals+temporaries smaller than args_offset+args_count, contradicting the standard njs frame layout derivable from the helper names; no in-fragment derivation exceeds capacity, so it is not a confirmed finding.

verdict.summary: getInfoForId dereferences the map iterator it->second even when find() returned end(): the only guard (line 3) logs via STFATAL but does not terminate the path, so a missing id drives a past-the-end iterator dereference at line 6. The absent fix is a return/abort after the fatal log or an it != end() guard before the use.

Dereferencing a past-the-end iterator is undefined behavior; the fragment lacks the protective return/abort after STFATAL or an it != end() check before the use. Primary CWE-476: unchecked lookup failure leads to an invalid dereference.

assumptions: idInfoMap is a standard associative container whose find() returns end() on a missing key (only semantics needed; no capacity or trust invariant assumed).
STFATAL does not provably terminate execution — no abort()/exit()/noreturn behavior is visible in the fragment.
limitations: If STFATAL is in fact a terminating abort-style macro in the real program, the dereference would be unreachable; that property is not derivable from the shown code.
Provenance of id from callers is unshown but irrelevant: any missing-key lookup admitted by the fragment is a valid witness.

verdict.summary: In QPaintEngineEx::stroke, the element-walk loops advance 'points' by 6 qreals for a QPainterPath::CurveToElement while the only guard, 'while (points < lastPoint)' (lines 111 and 167), only ensures 2 qreals remain. The curve arms read points[0..5] (line 124-126) and points[0..2] as QPointF (line 184-187) past the capacity computed at line 88, 'points + (pointCount<<1)', when the unvalidated element stream from path.elements() places a CurveToElement with fewer than 3 points remaining, causing an out-of-bounds heap read.

evidence.reason: Sink reads points[0..5] (6 qreals) with no check that 6 qreals remain. Capacity is points + (pointCount<<1) (line 88). The loop guard 'while (points < lastPoint)' (line 111) admits lastPoint - points == 2 or 4 (points advances by 2, so the parity is even), so with elements = {MoveToElement, CurveToElement} and pointCount == 2, the second iteration enters case CurveToElement (line 123) and reads indices pointCount*2 .. pointCount*2+3, up to 4 qreals past the array end. The element-type stream from path.elements() (line 84) is never validated; no statement such as 'if (points + 6 > lastPoint) break;' appears before the cubicTo call. Confirmed CWE-125 out-of-bounds read.

Cosmetic-pen branch repeats the same unprotected curve read: QPointF[0..2] dereferences 6 qreals from the points buffer whose bound is points + (pointCount<<1) (line 88), guarded only by 'while (points < lastPoint)' (line 167), which admits a 2- or 4-qreal remainder. A CurveToElement admitted by every guard with points == lastPoint - 2 reads up to 4 qreals out of bounds (CWE-125); the missing bound check (e.g., 'if (points + 6 > lastPoint) break;') is absent on this path as well.

QVectorPath::isEmpty() (line 9) is interpreted as elementCount() == 0 per standard Qt semantics, excluding the zero-element reads.
points advances in steps of 2, so lastPoint - points is always even, making the admitted remainder exactly 2 or 4 for the degenerate curve case.
limitations: path is an internal-helper parameter with no shown call site; a well-formed element stream (CurveToElement always followed by two CurveToDataElement) would keep the curve reads in bounds, but that invariant is not derivable from the fragment and is not credited.

Unsupported element values reaching the switch hit the default arms (lines 131-132, 193-194), which advance neither points nor types, causing non-termination of the while loops (CWE-835 candidate); it shares the same unvalidated element-stream root cause and is not counted as a separate primary finding.
StrokeHandler capacity (line 13) and the stroker/dasher writes into it are not shown and were not assessed.

STFATAL has no shown termination semantics (no exit/throw/return visible in the fragment), so control is analyzed as continuing to line 7.
limitations: If the unshown definition of STFATAL aborts the process (e.g., a glog-style FATAL), the dereference at line 7 is unreachable; that invariant is not derivable from the shown code and was not assumed.
The log statement at line 5 uses a string literal, so no log-injection (CWE-117) finding applies.

verdict.summary: ReadCINImage bounds the attacker-controlled user_length against GetBlobSize before allocating/reading the user profile (line 332), NULL-checks profile/quantum_info/q (335/374/395), requires a full row read (count == length) before importing pixels (398), and fail-closes on SetImageExtent failure (364). The pixel-buffer capacity is not shown in the fragment, so no OOB can be confirmed; every dangerous operation with a visible failure set is protected.

The protective bound at line 332 ('if (cin.file.user_length > GetBlobSize(image))') throws before the allocation, admitting only user_length in [1, GetBlobSize] (0 excluded by the enclosing condition at line 324); the NULL-return check at lines 335-336 also precedes use. Guard identity holds: no shown statement between lines 332 and 334 alters user_length, so the unbounded-allocation failure set is fully excluded.

Row read of length=GetBytesPerRow(image->columns,channels,image->depth) into the GetQuantumPixels() buffer. Partial/EOF reads are excluded by the equality check at line 398 ('if (count != (ssize_t) length) break;') before ImportQuantumPixels at line 400 consumes the buffer, so the short-read failure set is fully constrained on every path of the row loop (line 389); length cannot wrap the (ssize_t) cast (max about 4.1e11). The pixel buffer's capacity is not declared in the fragment, so the complementary large-length OOB-write hypothesis fails the in-fragment capacity requirement and is recorded in limitations.

Extent allocation driven by entry-point columns/rows (lines 343-344); each is at most 2^32-1 from ReadBlobLong, so columns*rows fits without wrapping 64-bit arithmetic (also used at line 350). Failure is fail-closed: line 364 checks status==MagickFalse and returns with the exception propagated (lines 366-367), so the allocation-failure set cannot reach an unguarded use.

Cache-write handle is checked for NULL at line 395 before ImportQuantumPixels/SyncAuthenticPixels at lines 400/402, and y is bounded by the loop condition at line 389 (y < (ssize_t) image->rows). The NULL-deref failure set is excluded on every iteration of the row loop.

ReadBlob/ReadBlobStream never write more bytes than the requested length or than remain in the file (standard ImageMagick blob semantics), and GetBlobSize(image) is the total file size.

CopyMagickString(property, field, sizeof(field)) and the fixed-size ReadBlob(...sizeof(field)...) calls copy at most sizeof(field) bytes, so no header-field string/property operation can overflow its fixed buffer.
limitations: The capacity of the quantum pixel buffer returned by GetQuantumPixels (line 388) is not declared or computed in the fragment, so a heap overflow via ReadBlobStream (line 397) if length exceeded that buffer can neither be confirmed nor refuted from the shown statements; it would require AcquireQuantumInfo/GetQuantumExtent internals.

The heuristic at line 350 (columns*rows/8 <= blob size) does not bound a single row, but per-row reads are EOF-bounded by ReadBlobStream and rejected at line 398 before reaching ImportQuantumPixels at line 400.
Consequences of degenerate image->depth (bits_per_pixel of 0 or above the supported quantum depths, line 342) inside ImportQuantumPixels are callee-internal and not derivable from the fragment.
The 64-bit ~0UL sentinel comparisons against 32-bit film fields (e.g., line 291) and the film/user-block condition gated on user_length (lines 263, 324) are correctness quirks, not security sinks.

verdict.summary: No dangerous operation admits an unconstrained value. The only entry-point-derived scalar k is range-checked to [1, n-1] at lines 23-25 before any use in regularize_k, EccPoint_mult, or modInv, and all failure paths (RNG, r==0, oversize s) fail closed with return 0. All stack and signature writes are sized by curve constants against the declared uECC_MAX_WORDS capacities with no in-fragment derivation that can exceed them.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective guard on the entry-point scalar k: isZero over num_words excludes k == 0 and cmp(curve->n, k, num_n_words) != 1 excludes k >= n, admitting exactly [1, n-1]. Checked before k is consumed by regularize_k (L27), EccPoint_mult (L36) and the modMult/modInv chain (L52-54), and k is unmodified between check and use, so no guard-identity drift; the k == 0 failure set of modInv is fully excluded.

Fail-closed status check: an all-zero point result (r == 0) is rejected before the r value is emitted into signature at L57/L77, so the degenerate ECDSA r == 0 case cannot produce a signature; the call returns failure instead.

Fail-closed RNG status handling and initialization: the no-RNG path pins the blinding multiplier tmp to 1 (so k' = k cannot become 0 before modInv at L53), and the RNG path returns 0 on generation failure instead of continuing with uninitialized or partial data.

Top-word initialization for s before the num_n_words-wide vli_modMult at L68: when num_n_words exceeds num_words (e.g., a 160-bit field with a 161-bit order), uECC_vli_set at L67 fills only num_words words and this statement zeroes the remaining word, preventing uninitialized stack data from entering the modular arithmetic chain; the index is bounded by the curve-fixed word count which no shown statement can drive out of [1, uECC_MAX_WORDS].

assumptions: All in-fragment writes into tmp/s/p are sized by curve->num_words / num_n_words, which for the library's fixed curve family stay within the declared uECC_MAX_WORDS capacities; the fragment itself never mutates these fields.
The signature buffer is caller-provided at 2 * curve->num_bytes: r occupies the first num_bytes (via p/nativeToBytes), s the second (L77/L79).
limitations: hash_size is not capped inside this fragment before bits2int at L70; its safety depends on the unshown bits2int capping the hash to BITS_TO_BYTES(curve->num_n_bits), which is standard uECC semantics but not visible here - demoted rather than confirmed.

An explicit num_words <= uECC_MAX_WORDS (or num_n_words <= uECC_MAX_WORDS) bound is absent, so a hypothetical out-of-family curve could overflow the stack buffers; no shown producer can derive such a value, so this is an unconfirmed, caller/environment-dependent concern.
NULL for private_key/message_hash/signature would only arise from an unshown caller violating the documented buffer contract; no shown statement can produce NULL.

If the RNG path's uECC_generate_random_int could return 0 for tmp, the later modInv(0) at L53 would be undefined; the standard helper semantics retry to a nonzero value, and the helper body is not shown - demoted.

verdict.summary: Unbounded strcpy of the endpoint-derived pipe path into the fixed-size sun_path array of sockaddr_un overflows the stack when pipePath is at least sizeof(local.sun_path) bytes; no length check precedes the copy.

evidence.reason: pipePath (std::string from endpoint.name(), line 4) retains its full declared length domain when it reaches line 15; sockaddr_un::sun_path is a fixed-size array (capacity per OS ABI, e.g., 108 bytes), so strcpy writes strlen(pipePath)+1 bytes and overflows for any pipePath.size() >= sizeof(local.sun_path). The only prior guard (lines 5-7) checks map membership, not length, so its admitted set still includes overflowing paths (wrong-target drift). The absent one-statement fix is a length check such as 'if (pipePath.size() >= sizeof(local.sun_path)) throw/return' (or a bounded copy like strncpy) before line 15; the surviving witness is a path of capacity length with no embedded NUL, admitted on every path. Primary CWE-121 stack-based buffer overflow (unchecked unbounded copy).

assumptions: sockaddr_un::sun_path is a fixed-size array whose capacity is defined by the OS ABI (e.g., 108 bytes on Linux).
strcpy copies the entire source string plus the NUL terminator.
limitations: ::listen(fd, 5) at line 19 discards its return value; treated as a status-handling note, not the confirmed mechanism.
endpoint.name() has no shown call site, so provenance is internal-helper; the finding rests on the unconstrained string reaching strcpy in-fragment.
chmod/security-context behavior under #ifndef WIN32 is out of scope for this verdict.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation is protected: the entry assert bounds off <= len (line 5), the gate at lines 16-17 plus the per-state '++p == pe' guards (e.g., lines 42-43) exclude p >= pe before every dereference, the in-place snake_upcase_char writes occur only at p < pe, and all callback ranges (PTR_TO/LEN, header_done) are derived from marks inside [buffer+off, buffer+len). No unconstrained value reaches an unprotected sink.

evidence.reason: First buffer read sink (case 1). Protected by line 5 'assert(off <= len ...)' which bounds p = buffer+off to <= pe, and by line 16 'if ( p == pe ) goto _test_eof;' which excludes p == pe; combined with monotonic guarded increments, the admitted set is p in [buffer+off, buffer+len-1], whose intersection with the failure set (p >= buffer+len) is empty. Guard-Identity audit: same p, same type, no intervening assignment (pass).

In-place write at p. Reached only from state 15 whose dereference was preceded by 'if ( ++p == pe ) goto _test_eof15;' (lines 254-255), so p < pe and the written byte index is at most len-1, inside the len-byte capacity defined by pe = buffer+len (line 8). No type/precision or check-then-use drift: same p, immediately after the guard.

Range-consuming callback. Fires only from case 16 after dereferencing p at line 285, so p < pe; therefore p+1 <= pe = buffer+len and pe-p-1 >= 0, delivering the range [p+1, pe] strictly inside the len-byte buffer. body_start = p - buffer + 1 (line 291) is likewise in [1, len]. Both the pointer arithmetic and the length cannot underflow or exceed the capacity.

assumptions: pe = buffer + len (line 8) is the exclusive end of a len-byte readable/writable region, so [buffer+off, buffer+len-1] is the valid index range.
assert() statements (lines 5, 11, 953-958) are treated as active checks, as in Puma's default extension build; line 5 bounds the otherwise-unconstrained off parameter.
Callback bodies consume exactly the pointer and length passed by the parser.
limitations: off > len is excluded only by assert (line 5); in a hypothetical NDEBUG build with an out-of-contract caller, the line 21 deref could read past pe. off has no shown producer, so per provenance rules this is not a confirmed finding.
snake_upcase_char casts away const on buffer (lines 306, 310); a read-only backing store would fault, which is a caller-contract concern, not an in-fragment defect.
The unshown callback bodies could in principle mishandle their ranges; standard semantics (consume exactly the named pointer/length) are assumed.
parser->nread overflow would require more than SIZE_MAX total bytes across calls, not derivable from a realistic buffered request.

verdict.summary: The socket path from endpoint.name() is copied into the fixed-size sun_path buffer with strncpy without a length check or explicit terminator, so a path of >= sizeof(local.sun_path) bytes leaves sun_path unterminated; unlink() and chmod() then treat it as a C string and read past the 108-byte buffer (CWE-125) and may act on an unintended path, caused by improper null termination (CWE-170).

The residual flags value is the full prior unsigned int of the recycled slot: the fragment overwrites ops/page/offset/len but never flags, so PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE set by a prior normal pipe write survives. No guard anywhere in the fragment constrains buf->flags, so the admitted value set at the sink includes CAN_MERGE. Absent one-statement fix: buf->flags = 0; before get_page(page) (between lines 35 and 36). With the stale flag, a subsequent write() merges user data into the page-cache page backing buf->page, enabling writes to read-only file cache (CWE-281, CVE-2022-0847).

assumptions: Pipe ring slots are reused: i_head is advanced (line 29) and pipe->head updated (line 41), and the fragment re-fetches the slot with pipe->bufs[i_head & p_mask] (line 30).

Standard kernel pipe semantics: pipe_write sets PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE on newly created pipe buffers; a buffer retaining CAN_MERGE and referencing a page-cache page allows subsequent merge writes into that page.
limitations: pipe->ring_size - 1 at line 7 assumes ring_size >= 1; the kernel allocates a power-of-two ring, but that invariant is not visible in this fragment, so it is not used as a finding.
sanity(i) body is not shown; it is treated only as the entry gate it appears to be, with no effect on buf->flags.
The upstream fix also covers the parallel path in fs/splice.c (push_pipe), but only this fragment is analyzed.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation in uECC_sign_with_k carries a protective statement that fully excludes its failure set: the k-range guard (L22-24) admits only 1 <= k < n before k reaches EccPoint_mult and the blinding modInv chain; the isZero(p) guard (L28-30) rejects r == 0; the RNG branch (L34-39) initializes tmp on both paths and checks uECC_generate_random_int's status; and the bit-length guard (L64-66) admits only numBits(s) <= num_bytes*8 immediately before s is written to the signature buffer at L68/70, with no intervening mutation of s. All remaining memory operations depend on caller-provided curve properties and buffer sizes that no shown statement constrains, so no unconstrained value reaches an unprotected sink.

evidence.reason: Protective statement for the s store at L68/70. s is produced by modMult reduction mod curve->n (L63), and the guard admits only numBits(s) <= num_bytes*8, excluding every value not representable in the num_bytes-byte store (failure set: numBits(s) > num_bytes*8). Guard-Identity Audit passes: the guard tests the same value s at the same precision (bitcount vs num_bytes*8) at a control point immediately before the sink, with no assignment between L66 and L68/70. This is the decisive protective statement for the verdict.

Protective range guard for the nonce k before it is consumed by EccPoint_mult (L27) and by the blinding modMult/modInv chain (L43-45). Admitted set is 1 <= k < curve->n; k == 0 is rejected by isZero and k >= n is rejected by cmp(curve->n, k, num_n_words) != 1. No statement between L24 and L27 mutates k (L26 only reads it), so the guard still constrains the exact value consumed; eliminates modInv(0) and invalid-scalar cases.

Protective status guard rejecting the ECDSA-invalid case r == 0 before p is used as r (stored at L48, consumed at L58-59 for s = r*d). Admitted set is p != 0, excluding the failure set {r == 0}; the check runs immediately after EccPoint_mult and before any use of p, so it constrains the exact value reaching the downstream arithmetic.

Protective initialization/status handling for tmp before it is consumed at L43-45 (blinding multiply/invert/multiply). Both branches initialize tmp (clear+set to 1, or RNG output), and the RNG failure return is checked, so tmp is never uninitialized and no failed RNG status is discarded (no CWE-457/CWE-754 failure set survives).

assumptions: curve is a well-formed uECC curve: num_n_bits > 0, num_words <= uECC_MAX_WORDS, num_bytes <= uECC_MAX_WORDS*sizeof(uECC_word_t), so stack arrays tmp/s indexed at num_n_words-1 and the num_bytes-byte stores remain in-bounds (invariants not derivable inside the fragment, relied on in the direction favorable to safety).
signature buffer holds at least 2*curve->num_bytes and message_hash holds hash_size bytes (caller contract, not shown).

uECC_generate_random_int returns a value in [1, n-1] on success or is retried by callers for zero (zero result would make k' = 0, giving s = 0 with probability ~2^-256; not derivable from shown code).

The two little-endian bcopy calls (L52, L68) follow the fragment's destination-first argument convention, consistent with their sibling calls uECC_vli_bytesToNative/nativeToBytes (L54, L70); buffer sizes are unshown either way.
limitations: EccPoint_mult (L27), uECC_vli_set (L58), nativeToBytes (L48/L70), bits2int (L61), and modInv (L44) bodies are not shown, so potential out-of-bounds behavior inside them (e.g., reading word num_n_words when num_n_bits is a multiple of the word size) cannot be confirmed from the fragment and is not counted as a finding.

Any memory-safety failure at L52/L54/L57/L58/L70 would require caller-supplied degenerate curve parameters or undersized buffers (e.g., num_n_bits == 0 making s[-1] at L57), which no shown statement produces.

hash_size is not validated against the curve byte size before bits2int (L61); an oversized/lying hash_size could over-read message_hash only inside the unshown helper, so it is demoted to a robustness concern.

A hypothetical RNG returning exactly 0 would yield s = 0 via the blinding path and would not be re-rejected by the L64-66 check; probability ~2^-256 and dependent on unshown caller/RNG behavior, so not a confirmed vulnerability.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective guard for the dangling-binding-chain failure set: it excludes {desc carries NFT_DATA_DESC_SETELEM} and {chain is NFT_CHAIN_BINDING} before the chain reference is stored at lines 56-57. The admitted set after this guard contains no binding chain for set-element verdicts, and no statement between line 54 and the assignment at line 57 can change chain or desc->flags, so the Guard-Identity Audit passes.

Protects every dereference of chain (lines 50, 53, 56-57): the first lookup branch (lines 36-38) is covered by this shared check, and the byid branch is additionally covered by the same-value check at lines 42-43. An ERR_PTR lookup result is excluded before nft_is_base_chain(chain) dereferences it; the guard constrains the same pointer value at the same precision with no intervening assignment.

Return-status check on nft_chain_lookup_byid (lines 40-41) executed before the pointer can be reused or dereferenced; together with the shared IS_ERR check at lines 48-49 it makes the error-pointer failure set empty on every path reaching the sink.
Required-attribute validation before reading the entry-point verdict code at line 16; an absent CODE attribute is excluded, so nla_get_be32 is never called on a NULL attribute pointer.

Whitelist validation of the attacker-controlled verdict code: any value whose masked low byte is not NF_ACCEPT/NF_DROP/NF_QUEUE and any value not exactly NFT_CONTINUE/NFT_BREAK/NFT_RETURN/NFT_JUMP/NFT_GOTO is rejected (line 26), so an unconstrained code never proceeds to the chain-lookup and assignment logic.

assumptions: nft_chain_lookup and nft_chain_lookup_byid return ERR_PTR (never NULL) on failure per kernel convention, which is exactly the error class the IS_ERR checks at lines 42-43 and 48-49 filter.

nla_parse_nested_deprecated returns negative on error and, on success, fills tb[] only for validated attributes; the host array capacity NFTA_VERDICT_MAX + 1 (line 5) matches the maximum index used at line 9.
ctx, data, and desc are valid kernel-internal objects supplied by the nf_tables API callers.
limitations: Upper bits of ACCEPT/DROP/QUEUE verdict codes are admitted as long as the low byte is valid; their downstream packet-path interpretation is outside this fragment and was not assessed.
Helper bodies (nft_chain_lookup, nft_chain_lookup_byid, nft_is_base_chain) are not shown; their standard ERR_PTR/non-NULL-on-success semantics are assumed, per the rules for unshown callees.
The fragment is the fixed form: the NFT_DATA_DESC_SETELEM + NFT_CHAIN_BINDING rejection (lines 52-54) is present verbatim, so a vulnerable pairing that omits that check is not what is displayed.

verdict.summary: All dangerous operations are protected by in-fragment statements: the header sanitize (lines 45-49) excludes zero, oversized, and invalid width/height/bytes values and any product exceeding G_MAXSIZE before any allocation; the name path requires a full read and a NUL byte at temp[bn_size-1] (lines 97-98) before gimp_any_to_utf8(temp, -1); every read is checked against its exact count (lines 29, 97, 123, 167), and the pattern/case-2 loops index only within the declared allocations.

evidence.snippet:
if ((bh.width == 0) || (bh.width > GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE) ||
      (bh.height == 0) || (bh.height > GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE) ||
      ((bh.bytes != 1) && (bh.bytes != 2) && (bh.bytes != 4) &&

evidence.reason: Protective guard for every allocation/size derived from the entry-point header: it excludes width==0, height==0, width/height above GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE, bytes outside {1,2,4,18}, and any width*height*bytes product above G_MAXSIZE; lines 120-123 and 163 then operate only on the admitted range, so the failure set (zero, degenerate, or overflowing sizes reaching g_new/g_malloc/read) is empty.

Protective guard for the gimp_any_to_utf8(temp, -1) strlen-style consumer at line 108: bn_size>0 (line 93) makes temp[bn_size-1] in-bounds, the full-read check excludes short reads, and the NUL check guarantees termination, so no unterminated or partially initialized buffer reaches the length-intolerant conversion on any path.

assumptions: GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE is a named compile-time cap referenced but not valued in the fragment; the sanitize at lines 45-49 still excludes zero widths/heights and bounds the product against G_MAXSIZE.

GLib g_new/g_malloc abort on allocation failure and never return NULL (standard semantics), so an unusually large bn_size (line 95) is at most an OOM/robustness concern, not an in-fragment memory-safety failure.
The only reassignment of a guarded header field is bh.bytes (lines 72, 162, 207) before its consumers; width and height are never rewritten after line 49.
limitations: The multiplications at lines 120 (bh.width*bh.height*bh.bytes) and 163 (4*bh.width*bh.height) are computed in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic; wrapping would require width*height*bytes >= 2^32, i.e., GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE >= 32768, whose value is not shown in the fragment, so no in-fragment witness is derivable.

gimp_any_to_utf8 could return NULL on conversion failure, which would make strlen(name) at line 245 a NULL deref, but NULL-on-failure is unshown callee behavior and no fragment statement produces or checks it.

bh.header_size is not upper-bounded (only > sizeof(BrushHeader) at line 84), so bn_size can request up to ~2GB via g_new(line 95); the full-read check and glib abort semantics leave this as a resource/hardening concern rather than a confirmed memory-safety or injection flaw.

verdict.summary: gdImageFillToBorder validates only the upper bound of the fill coordinates (x >= im->sx, y >= im->sy at lines 13-18) but never rejects or clamps negative y, so a caller-supplied y = -1 reaches gdImageGetPixel/gdImageSetPixel as a row index outside [0, im->sy), causing an out-of-bounds read and write. The missing one-statement fix is a lower-bound check such as 'if (x < 0 || y < 0) return;' before the seek loops.

evidence.reason: y is an int parameter whose residual range after the shown constraints (lines 13-18 clamp only y >= im->sy) still includes every negative value; the row domain implied by im->sy is [0, im->sy) as used at lines 16/41/56, and nothing in the fragment bounds y below. Witness y = -1 with x >= 0 is admitted by the line 16-18 guard (admitted set (-inf, sy-1]) and reaches this sink on the first iteration of the left loop (line 20, i = x), writing at image row -1. No lower-bound validation (e.g. 'if (x < 0 || y < 0) return;' or 'if (y < 0) y = 0;') precedes the use; guard at line 41 is evaluated after this sink and is false for y < 0, guard at line 56 is true for y < 0 but cannot protect an earlier write. Missing fix: lower-bound check on y; primary CWE-787 out-of-bounds write.

The same unconstrained negative y read from the same source (guard at line 16-18 admits all y < 0) is passed as the row argument to gdImageGetPixel on every left-loop iteration before any y > 0 / y < im->sy - 1 guard (lines 41, 56) is evaluated. Witness y = -1 reaches this read at i = x and reads image row -1, outside the [0, im->sy) row domain the fragment itself uses at lines 16, 41 and 56. Missing fix: lower-bound validation of y before the seek loops; secondary CWE-125 out-of-bounds read.

assumptions: im->sx and im->sy are the image width and height, and the valid coordinate domain is x in [0, im->sx), y in [0, im->sy) — the fragment itself treats these as the bounds at lines 13-18, 41 and 56.

Full int domain for x and y because no shown caller or other fragment statement constrains their lower bound; the fragment's own upper clamps prove that out-of-domain parameters are expected to be handled here.
limitations: Exact memory-corruption impact depends on whether the unshown helper bodies gdImageGetPixel/gdImageSetPixel bounds-check internally; if they do, the demonstrated failure reduces to an out-of-domain argument (input-validation flaw) rather than a confirmed crash.
x < 0 alone is not a finding: the left loop is skipped and leftLimit == -1 triggers the return at lines 27-28.
