verdict.summary: dynamicGetbuf lets a negative rlen reach memcpy: the guard at line 14 (remain == 0) excludes only zero, so when dp->pos exceeds dp->logicalSize (remain < 0) or a caller passes a negative len, rlen is negative and is promoted to a huge size_t in memcpy at line 20, causing unbounded out-of-bounds copy. The missing fix is 'if (remain <= 0) return EOF;'.

evidence.reason: rlen is derived from remain (line 10, signed int subtraction with no shown pos<=logicalSize minimum) or len (line 12), and the only guard on the else path (line 14, 'if (remain == 0) return EOF;') excludes merely {0}, leaving every negative remain<len admitted into rlen at line 17; witness remain=-1 with len=0 passes lines 11 and 14, so rlen=-1 is passed to memcpy and promoted to size_t SIZE_MAX (CWE-195 signed-to-unsigned negative size; CWE-697 because == 0 should be <= 0). The absent one-statement fix is 'if (remain <= 0) return EOF;' (or an explicit rlen>0 check) before the copy; buf and dp->data capacities are unshown, but the negative-size promotion alone is the confirmed in-fragment mechanism.

assumptions: len, rlen, remain, dp->logicalSize and dp->pos are signed int; memcpy's size parameter is size_t, so a negative int n promotes to a huge unsigned value (standard C semantics).
limitations: The fragment shows no in-fragment producer that sets dp->pos > dp->logicalSize (e.g., a seek on attacker-controlled offset elsewhere in the program), so the negative-remain witness rests on the unconstrained residual range per the degenerate-input discipline rather than a visible assignment.
The negative-len path (line 12 when remain >= len) also feeds the sink but depends on an unshown call site and is not the decisive witness.
Capacities of buf and dp->data are not shown, so the out-of-bounds extent beyond the negative-size promotion is not separately quantified.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation in ReadTGAImage is protected by a verbatim in-fragment guard: the colormap size computed from attacker-controlled bits_per_pixel is bounds-checked before allocation (lines 130-131) with allocation-failure aborts (132-133, 190-191); colormap writes are bounded by the allocated count (192-194); colormap reads are clamped by ConstrainColormapIndex (312-313, 348); the comment write is inside a length+MagickPathExtent allocation with NULL check (149-155); the pixel queue pointer is NULL-checked before any row write (276-278) with row/column indices kept inside the extent (271-279, 394-402); and every pixel/RLE read validates its exact byte count (292-294, 334-335, 357-370). No admitted input value reaches an unprotected sink, so the fragment is not vulnerable.

evidence.reason: Dangerous allocation sized from entry-point data. bits_per_pixel is constrained to {2..16,24,32} by line 91-93, so image->colors = 1<<bits_per_pixel (line 129) is at most 2^32; guard at line 130-131 (image->colors > ((~0UL)/sizeof(*image->colormap)) throws) excludes any size whose byte count could wrap, and this allocation-failure check aborts on failure. Guard-identity audit passes (same size_t value, no mutation between check and use), so the failure set is empty. Colormap branch line 121-122 maxes at 131070 and is re-checked at lines 188-191.

Colormap write sink. Loop at line 194 bounds i to i < (ssize_t) image->colors, and lines 188-190 ensure image->colors >= colormap_index and that the allocation of exactly image->colors entries succeeded (abort on MagickFalse at line 190-191). Max index = colors-1 <= 131070 (colormap_index+colormap_length from lines 80-81,122), in bounds; the first loop at line 192 covers [0, colormap_index-1]. No out-of-bounds write is reachable.

Buffer write sink. id_length is an unsigned char read at line 66 (0..255); comment is allocated with length+MagickPathExtent bytes at lines 149-151 (length <= 255) and NULL-checked at line 152-153, so the write index id_length <= 255 is well inside the allocation. The ~length >= MagickPathExtent-1 test (line 149) is true for all reachable length values, so the write is always into a non-NULL buffer of sufficient capacity.

Row cache pointer sink. q is NULL-checked before any SetPixel*/q+= write (lines 381-387). Row index real is derived at 273-275 and is always in [0, rows-1]: offset starts at 0 (line 270) and is reset by lines 398-402 (if offset >= image->rows { base++; offset=base; }) at the end of every iteration before the next use, so no row, including the degenerate rows==1 case, computes rows-real-1 < 0. Column writes are bounded by x < image->columns (line 279), matching the requested region width.

pixels[4] (declared line 40) is only indexed after exact-count reads that abort on truncation: ReadBlob(image,4,pixels) != 4 at line 369-370, ReadBlob(image,3,pixels) != 3 at 357-358, and ReadBlob(image,2,pixels) != 2 at 334-335. Maximum byte count is 4, so indices used (0..3) are within the declared capacity. RLE is likewise covered because the runlength header read is checked at line 292-294.

assumptions: Standard ImageMagick helper semantics, visible only by call name, are assumed: AcquireImageColormap allocates exactly image->colors entries and returns MagickFalse on failure; ConstrainColormapIndex clamps to [0, colors-1]; QueueAuthenticPixels returns a columns x 1 region or NULL; size_t is 64-bit and unsigned short is 16-bit.
limitations: colors==0 (colormap_index=0, colormap_length=0) would drive ConstrainColormapIndex into a colors-1 wrap only if AcquireImageColormap accepted 0 colors; that callee behavior is not shown, so the hypothesis is not confirmable from the fragment.

ReadBlobByte calls (lines 204-205, 219-220, 234-239, 247-254, 310) are not individually count-checked; truncation surfaces as a final EOFBlob throw at lines 413-415 after pixel processing, a robustness/status concern with no memory-safety consequence in the fragment.
The unclamped byte index stored by SetPixelIndex (lines 380-381) when index (0..255) exceeds image->colors could affect unshown later consumers; that use is outside the fragment.

1<<32 with bits_per_pixel==32 would be undefined on a 32-bit size_t platform, but the fragment's guards (130-133) still route it to an allocation-failure abort on a 64-bit build; no 32-bit platform invariant is shown.

verdict.summary: issuerAndThisUpdateCheck performs an out-of-bounds read when the quoted issuer (or thisUpdate) value contains no closing '"'. The scan loop at line 65 exits with is->bv_len == x.bv_len, then lines 78-79 advance x.bv_val one byte past in->bv_val end and underflow x.bv_len, and the space-eating loop at line 122 dereferences x.bv_val[0] out of bounds. The input '{issuer "rdnSequence:abcdefghijklmnopq,}' (length 40) passes every shown guard (lines 19, 21, 42, 52, 58) and reaches the sink; the missing fix is a closing-quote existence check (e.g., 'if (is->bv_len == x.bv_len) return LDAP_INVALID_SYNTAX;') after the scan loop.

evidence.reason: OOB read sink: with in->bv_len >= 38 (line 19) and braces satisfied (line 21), the issuer scan loop (line 65) exits without finding a closing quote when the value region contains no '"' (is->bv_len == x.bv_len). Line 78 then sets x.bv_val = in->bv_val + in->bv_len (one past the bv_len-byte buffer) and line 79 underflows x.bv_len to a huge unsigned value. Control falls through to line 122, whose condition dereferences x.bv_val[0] before checking x.bv_len, reading one byte (and potentially more) past in->bv_val. All guards on the path (lines 19, 21, 42, 52, 58, 100) admit the witness '{issuer "rdnSequence:abcdefghijklmnopq,}'; the absent fix is a closing-quote check `if (is->bv_len == x.bv_len) return LDAP_INVALID_SYNTAX;` after the scan loop (and after the tu scan loop at lines 107-111). Primary CWE-125 out-of-bounds read.

assumptions: Standard berval semantics: in->bv_val points to at least in->bv_len valid bytes (capacity visible at line 19/line 8).
ber_len_t is an unsigned type, so x.bv_len -= is->bv_len + 1 wraps to a huge value when is->bv_len == x.bv_len.

STRLENOF(Str) yields the string-literal length, and the invariant x.bv_val + x.bv_len == in->bv_val + in->bv_len - 1 is preserved by all shown pointer/length adjustments (lines 25-26, 39-40, 55-56, 78-79, 88-89, 112-113).
limitations: The escape-removal loop (lines 149-155) was analyzed as safe: it writes exactly is->bv_len - numdquotes bytes and the NUL terminator at that index fits the ni.bv_len + 1 allocation (line 148).
The double-quote pair read at line 70 is logically one byte past the x region but physically reads the in-bounds closing '}' (index in->bv_len - 1), so it is not flagged.
The discarded return status of ber_dupbv_x (line 142) has no security consequence visible within the fragment.
The additional unfettered fixed-length strncasecmp reads at lines 35/52/83 with a short remaining x.bv_len represent the same OOB-read class and were not required for the verdict.

verdict.summary: bpf_ringbuf_reserve bounds the producer position only against the user-writable consumer_pos (line 26), never against the oldest outstanding BUSY record, so consecutive reservations can physically overlap. A BPF program can then write into a live record's 8-byte header (hdr->len/hdr->pg_off), corrupting the pg_off used by bpf_ringbuf_commit()/restore_from_rec() and causing out-of-bounds access — an overlapping-buffer out-of-bounds write inside the ring buffer.

evidence.reason: Insufficient guard (wrong-target drift): it limits the reservation only against cons_pos, which was read from the user-writable consumer_pos at line 11 and is never cross-checked against outstanding BUSY records. Its admitted set new_prod_pos - cons_pos <= rb->mask accepts the witness where cons_pos=0x3000, ring mask=0x3FFF, and two size=0x3000 reservations (deltas 8 and 0x3010) are both admitted, placing the second record over the first record's header. The protective statement that would exclude this is a bound on the oldest pending position, e.g. rejecting new_prod_pos - pend_pos > rb->mask with pending_pos/busy-record tracking; it is absent.

Confirmed sink: record placement. With prod_pos=0x3008 and mask=0x3FFF after the two admitted reservations (Phase 2 witness), hdr lands such that the returned record spans physical [0x3008,0x4000) plus [0x0,0x2010) via the ring's double-mapped data pages, overlapping the first busy record's data and header at [0x0,0x8). The BPF program writes through the pointer returned at line 41, achieving an overlapping out-of-bounds write into a live record's header (CWE-787); a later bpf_ringbuf_commit() then consumes the corrupted pg_off.

Sink exposure: the function hands the caller (BPF program) a writable pointer into a region that may overlap another outstanding reservation because only the cons_pos-based check (line 26) gates placement. The caller's size-byte writes are therefore not confined to the intended record, enabling the header corruption described for line 31.

assumptions: rb->mask is the power-of-two ring capacity minus one (mask is used as the ring offset mask at lines 26 and 31), so a ring of 0x4000 bytes has mask 0x3FFF.
The consumer position page is writable by user space per the ringbuf mmap contract, so consumer_pos (line 11) is attacker-controllable and can be advanced past genuinely consumed data.
Ring buffer data pages are double-mapped back-to-back, so a logical reservation wrapping past mask+1 remains contiguous and overlaps the buffer's start, including record headers.
Reservation sizes of 0x3000 are admitted by the only shown size constraint (line 7), i.e. RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ >= 0x3000.
limitations: The u32 truncation at line 10 (len = round_up(size + BPF_RINGBUF_HDR_SZ, 8)) is not confirmed because it requires RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ >= 2^32-8, whose value is not shown in the fragment; demoted as a candidate.

The downstream corruption (invalid dereference in bpf_ringbuf_restore_from_rec / bpf_ringbuf_commit) depends on consumer-side code not shown; the in-fragment failure is the overlapping placement itself.
Other ring fields (rb->producer_pos, rb->data, rb->spinlock) and the exact space semantics of rb->mask are kernel-internal invariants assumed sound; no additional flaw is claimed for them.

verdict.summary: In create_cache_bins, the accel-dependent dependency walk writes deps[dep_index] where dep_index is an unvalidated 15-bit value taken from file-controlled depArray entries and deps is sized only from cache->hdr->imagesCount (header 0), enabling a heap out-of-bounds write; the k-loop also reads depArray[k] with no bound against cache->accel->depListCount, enabling an out-of-bounds read when no 0xffff terminator exists.

evidence.reason: Heap OOB write (CWE-787). dep_index = depArray[k] & 0x7fff (L80) admits 0..0x7fff from file-controlled depArray; deps capacity is R_NEWS0(int, cache->hdr->imagesCount) at L19, i.e. header 0's count only. The only guards on the path are depArray/extras NULL checks (L41-52) and depArray[k] != 0xffff (L79), none of which bound dep_index. Witness: depListCount=1, depArray[0]=0x7fff, hdr[0].imagesCount=1; dep_index=0x7fff writes past deps. Absent fix: a check such as 'if (dep_index >= hdr->imagesCount) break;' before L81.

OOB read (CWE-125). depArray is allocated as R_NEWS0(ut16, cache->accel->depListCount) at L41 and fully populated by the byte-count check at L46, so valid indices are 0..depListCount-1; k starts at file-controlled extras[j].dependentsStartArrayIndex and increases until a 0xffff sentinel, with no bound against depListCount and no shown guarantee the sentinel exists. Witness: depListCount=1 and depArray[0] != 0xffff lets k reach 1, reading depArray[1] out of bounds. Absent fix: a bound such as 'k < cache->accel->depListCount' in the loop condition.

Heap OOB read/write (CWE-787/125) when a non-first header is used: deps is sized once from cache->hdr->imagesCount (header 0) at L19, but the loop guard at L58 admits j in 0..hdr->imagesCount-1 for the current hdr. Guard-Identity Audit: wrong-target drift (class 3) — the guard constrains j against hdr->imagesCount (L58) while the buffer capacity was derived from a different header's count. Witness: hdr[1].imagesCount > hdr[0].imagesCount and j = hdr[0].imagesCount passes L58 and reaches deps[j] at L59/L65/L75. Absent fix: allocate deps from the maximum imagesCount over all headers or check j against the allocation size (and the same applies to the deps[j] read at L103).

OOB read of the img array (CWE-125). img is produced by read_cache_images (L32) for hdr->imagesCount entries, but the index dep_index (L80) admits 0..0x7fff and is never compared with hdr->imagesCount; the same 0x7fff witness admitted by L79 reaches &img[0x7fff]. Absent fix: validate dep_index < hdr->imagesCount before this and before deps[dep_index] at L81.

assumptions: cache->hdr, cache->accel, hdr->imagesCount, depArray contents, and image data originate from the parsed dyld-cache file; the shown r_buf_fread_at (L46) and r_buf_read_at (L112) uses make the file provenance visible in the fragment.
R_NEWS0 may return NULL only via normal allocator failure, which is checked at L20/L42; on success the returned arrays exist with the requested element counts.
The vulnerable region is reachable only when R_DYLDCACHE_FILTER (L12) is set and cache->accel is non-NULL (L40), both attacker-influenceable inputs shown in the fragment.

limitations: Whether a specific attacker input drives rex.lnum out of range (e.g., buffer with fewer lines than the recorded visual selection at match time) depends on engine/visual state not fully shown; the fragment itself imposes no guard excluding that state.
getvvcol() may mutate top/bot column fields; this is not the confirmed mechanism but was not needed for the verdict.

verdict.summary: This is the patched XBM parser: width/height are validated to >= 1 (lines 41-42, 46-47), the bytes_per_line*hh product is checked against integer overflow before g_malloc (line 94), line length is capped before unbounded %s sscanf writes (line 31), and both fill loops write at most the validated size bytes. The integer-overflow-to-heap-corruption failure set is fully excluded.

evidence.reason: Excludes fgets-truncated lines (strlen == MAX_SIZE-1), so every later unbounded %s write into name_and_type[MAX_SIZE] (lines 33, 62-71) receives a token of at most MAX_SIZE-2 chars, requiring at most MAX_SIZE-1 bytes including NUL, which fits the declared capacity.

Rejects non-positive parsed width/height values (also at line 46 for height), bounding ww and hh to [1, INT_MAX]. This excludes 0 and negative dimensions, making bytes_per_line >= 1 and size >= 1, and it keeps the unsigned arithmetic in the overflow check well-defined.

Decisive protective statement for the g_malloc(size) allocation (line 96) and both fill loops (lines 102-108, 113-117). With bytes_per_line in [1, 268435456] and hh in [1, INT_MAX], any product bytes_per_line*hh that wraps past INT_MAX yields an int size whose signed quotient is negative or strictly less than hh, so the check fails; an admitted size therefore equals bytes_per_line*hh exactly, is between 1 and INT_MAX, and the write loops write at most size bytes into the size-byte buffer. The guard passes the identity audit: no statement between line 94 and the sinks changes size.

assumptions: MAX_SIZE is a positive compile-time constant used consistently for both fgets and the name_and_type buffer.
int is 32-bit with two's-complement wrap on the implementation-defined unsigned-to-int conversion of the size product (the standard semantics of this GLib-era fix).
g_malloc allocates the given byte count and aborts on failure rather than returning NULL; next_int returns a negative value at EOF/parse failure.
limitations: The hotspot parsing double-decrement ('type--') is logically quirky and may fail to match the common 'x_hot' spelling, but pointer arithmetic stays within name_and_type and it has no memory-safety or security-decision impact; not a finding.
%d parsing of digit strings exceeding INT_MAX is implementation-defined; this is an input-robustness hardening concern only, with no memory-safety consequence given the line-94 check.

A crafted file can still request near-INT_MAX (multi-GB) but valid allocations and loop iterations; this bounded resource use is a DoS-hardening concern outside the one-statement fix class and was not treated as a confirmed vulnerability.
The loop bodies depend on next_int's '< 0' return convention, which is stated by the shown checks but not by a shown definition; under that standard convention the file-shortage path returns safely.

verdict.summary: In the ST21NFCA EVT_TRANSACTION handler, the entry guard uses && inside a reject condition, so no minimum skb length is enforced when skb->data[0] equals the AID tag and no tag check when skb->len >= 7. aid_len and params_len are read from untrusted bytes and never bounded against skb->len or the allocation size, so memcpy(transaction->aid, &skb->data[2], aid_len) performs a heap out-of-bounds write and an out-of-bounds skb read; the params-tag read and params memcpy are likewise unguarded.

evidence.reason: skb->len is entry-point-controlled and the guard at lines 22-24 admits len=7 (reject only when len<7 AND data[0]!=tag, so any len>=7 passes), giving an allocation of only skb->len-2 = 5 bytes that later receives a 255-byte memcpy; for len<2 admitted via data[0]==tag, skb->len-2 wraps to a huge size_t. Absent fix: reject skb->len < NFC_MIN_AID_LENGTH+2 and bound aid_len before any copy.

aid_len = skb->data[1] (line 30) is a u8 in 0..255 with no shown bound; with skb->len=7 admitted by the && guard, the allocation at line 26 is 5 bytes, so copying up to 255 bytes into transaction->aid overflows the heap allocation (CWE-122) and reads up to 253 bytes past skb->len (CWE-125). Absent fix: reject aid_len > NFC_AID_MAXSIZE or aid_len + 4 > skb->len before the copy.

The index aid_len+2 reaches up to 257 while skb->len can be as small as 2 (len<7 is admitted when data[0]==AID_TAG), so this read is out of bounds (CWE-125). Absent fix: verify transaction->aid_len + 3 < skb->len before this dereference.

The index aid_len+3 reaches up to 258 while skb->len can be as small as 2, so this byte read is out of bounds (CWE-125); the resulting params_len (0..255) is then copied without any length bound. Absent fix: bound aid_len+4 <= skb->len before indexing.

params_len (line 39) is 0..255 with no relation to skb->len; e.g., skb->len=10 (admitted), aid_len=5, data[8]=255 copies 255 bytes starting at skb->data+9, i.e., 245 bytes past skb->end, into an allocation of skb->len-2=8 bytes (CWE-125 read, CWE-122 write). Absent fix: require params_len <= skb->len - aid_len - 4 and within the allocation before the copy.

assumptions: NFC_MIN_AID_LENGTH is 5 per the in-fragment spec comment (AID length 5 to 16), making the threshold 7; the witnesses do not depend on this exact value.
devm_kzalloc returns NULL on failure (checked at lines 27-28) and a non-NULL ZERO_SIZE_PTR for size 0; the primary witness uses skb->len=7 so it does not rely on zero-size allocation semantics.
skb->len and the skb->data bytes are supplied by the NFC controller frame (entry-point input); no shown code bounds them.
limitations: The exact declared size of transaction->aid is not visible in the fragment; the out-of-bounds write is instead proven against the in-fragment allocation size skb->len-2 (5 bytes for the len=7 witness), which any 255-byte copy exceeds.
The default branch returns without kfree_skb (line 47), a skb leak/robustness concern, not the confirmed memory-safety mechanism.
Downstream exploitation (heap metadata corruption, control flow) is not shown; per the rules, the confirmed out-of-domain write is sufficient for the verdict.

verdict.summary: No dangerous operation admits an unconstrained value. Every strlcat write is protected by the line 80 non-NULL guard and sized by MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN, which equals the line 79 calloc capacity, so any source (including unbounded mount_user) truncates safely; the user-name concatenation is additionally guarded by `if (mount_user)` at line 96. Return statuses are checked before each subsequent use, and the only residual NULL path (calloc failure feeding addmntent) is an OOM robustness concern, not an attacker-triggerable failure.

evidence.reason: The user-name strlcat sink is fully constrained: line 96 `if (mount_user)` excludes the NULL result of getusername (line 13), and the size argument MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN equals the allocation capacity at line 79, so an unbounded residual-range username can only be truncated, never written out of bounds. No guard drift: the same mount_user pointer reaches this sink unchanged.

Representative of all nine strlcat option writes: line 80 `if (mountent.mnt_opts)` excludes the NULL dst from calloc (line 79) on every path, and the size argument MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN matches the calloc capacity, so even the fixed maximal option set plus a full-length mount_user is capped at capacity without overflow; strlcat preserves NUL termination within size.

The struct consumed by addmntent is fully initialized at lines 76-79 and 102-103, and its opts string is bounded by the line 79 capacity/line 80 guard; the return is status-checked at line 105 with ftruncate rollback at line 107. The only residual NULL is mountent.mnt_opts from line 79 calloc failure; that path lacks a before-use NULL check but is OOM-only and robustness-level, so it is recorded in limitations rather than confirmed as an attacker-triggerable NULL dereference.

assumptions: MTAB_OPTIONS_LEN at line 79 (calloc size) is the same constant passed as the size to every strlcat, so capacity equals the bound.
strlcat always NUL-terminates within the size limit, so truncation cannot overrun the allocated buffer.
getusername's result may be NULL when the uid has no passwd entry; line 96 excludes that NULL before use.
limitations: If calloc at line 79 fails, mountent.mnt_opts is NULL and addmntent at line 104 would consume it without a check; demoted to OOM/hardening since the allocation is fixed-size, the failure is not driven by attacker input, and glibc renders NULL opts as (null).
devname, mountpoint, and fstype have no shown NULL/validity producers; potential malformed mtab lines from untrusted strings are not a memory-safety concern demonstrable in the fragment.
Exit-path returns of toggle_dac_capability (118) and sigprocmask (119) are ignored; no security decision inside the fragment depends on them.

verdict.summary: The only capacity-bounded dangerous writes (memcpy/null-termination into dire->name) are fully protected: line 81 rejects dire->size >= SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN (excluded set 256..max), admitting 0..255, so the copies at lines 86-88 stay within the 257-byte name area derived from the buffer declared at lines 5-6. Read-side and heap-growth candidates cannot be confirmed because directory_table's capacity and struct dir_ent.name's capacity are not shown.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective guard. It admits dire->size in 0..255 and excludes dire->size >= 256 (SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN). Guard-identity audit passes: dire->size is filled at lines 72-77 into the same dire object and consumed unchanged at lines 86-88 with no intervening assignment, cast, or arithmetic, so no drift class applies. Together with the 257-byte name area (buffer at lines 5-6 = sizeof(squashfs_dir_entry_2) + SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN + 1), the copy length dire->size + 1 <= 256 and the termination index dire->size + 1 <= 256 both fit, so the failure set of the S3/S4 write sinks is empty.

Write sink into dire->name: residual range of dire->size is 0..255 after the line 81 guard, so the copy length is at most 256 bytes into the 257-byte name area (capacity from line 5). No out-of-bounds write is admitted on any path; guard exclusion set is dire->size >= 256.

Terminating write sink: with dire->size capped at 255 by the line 81 guard, the maximum index is 256, which is strictly less than the 257-byte name area derived from the buffer declared at lines 5-6. A one-past write would require dire->size == 256, which the line 81 guard (>=) excludes; the vulnerable form of this check (>) is not present. Verdict-determining operation resolves PRESENT.

assumptions: SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN is 256, matching the buffer arithmetic at lines 5-6, the 'size should never be SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN or larger' comment at line 80, and the >= guard boundary.
dire is a cast of the local buffer, so dire->name begins at offset sizeof(squashfs_dir_entry_2) within it and the writable name area is SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN + 1 = 257 bytes.
SQUASHFS_DIR_COUNT is 256, consistent with the line 63-64 comment and check bounding dirh.count + 1.
limitations: Read-side candidate (S1/S2 and the source side of the line 86 memcpy): reading past the logical `size` bound at lines 53/56/72-77/86-87 is not confirmable because directory_table's allocation capacity is never declared or computed in the fragment; the absent `bytes + N > size` guards would be defensive hardening, not a provable OOB here.

Realloc size overflow candidate (lines 93-94): the int product can wrap only after the loop accumulates roughly 8 million entries, which requires tens of MB of readable directory_table data plus an unconstrained (*i)->data; the table size and data bound are unshown, so the heap write-out-of-bounds chain at lines 100-104 is not derivable from the fragment.
strcpy at line 100 into dir->dirs[dir->dir_count].name cannot be assessed because struct dir_ent.name capacity is not shown.
Dereferences of (*i) at lines 25-29/32/41/47-48 have no NULL check, but read_inode's failure/NULL-return contract is not shown in the fragment, so no NULL producer is demonstrable.

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds read in mobi_parse_index_entry: the control_bytes pointer is advanced once per TAGX tag with control_byte==1 (L66) and then dereferenced at L70 with no bounds check against the record buffer. tagx->tags_count and tags[i].control_byte are file-controlled entry-point values with no shown cap, so a crafted TAGX can drive the read index past the buffer allocation (CWE-125).

evidence.reason: control_bytes is set at L45 to buf->data + buf->offset after the label read and advanced at L66 by every tag whose control_byte==1, with no check that the pointer stays within buf->maxlen/buf_maxlen; L70 dereferences control_bytes[0] when control_byte!=1. tagx->tags_count and control_byte are unconstrained file-derived (entry-point) values, and the only buffer guard, L16 (buf->offset + entry_length >= buf_maxlen), constrains the pre-label entry extent, not the post-label pointer advancement (wrong-target drift vs the sink). With a crafted file (entry_length/label_length admitted by L16/L22, tags_count > remaining buffer, all but one tag control_byte==1), control_bytes[0] reads at index start + tags_count, beyond the buf_maxlen-capped allocation. The absent one-statement fix is a bounds check before the deref, e.g. verifying the number of consumed control bytes fits the remaining buffer; primary mechanism is CWE-125 OOB read.

assumptions: buf->data is backed by at least buf_maxlen bytes and buf->maxlen initially equals the record size (L15).
indx->entries has total_entries_count elements, as implied by the L10 guard.
mobi_indx_get_label/mobi_getstring_ordt write at most label_length bytes plus a NUL into text, per their standard getstring semantics.
INDX_TAGVALUES_MAX bounds the tagvalues array as used by the guards at L115/L124.
limitations: INDX_LABEL_SIZEMAX value is not visible in the fragment, so a text[] overflow via label_length is unconfirmable (label_length <= 255 from get8).
Capacity of idxt.offsets[] is not shown, so the read of offsets[curr_number + 1] at L7 is not confirmable as OOB.
Type/domain of tagx->tags_count and tagx->control_byte_count and the (int) cast at L46 are not visible; a huge control_byte_count wrapping to a negative seek is unconfirmed.
mobi_getstring_ordt return value semantics are not shown; a returned label_length larger than the input is not confirmable.
Any cap on tags_count applied by an unshown caller/parser is not assumed.

verdict.summary: The directory-entry count guard is defeated by unsigned wraparound: dirh.count + 1 (line 59) maps filesystem counts 0x7FFFFFFF..0xFFFFFFFE to negative int values that pass `if(dir_count > SQUASHFS_DIR_COUNT)` (line 65), so `while(dir_count--)` (line 70) iterates billions of times over attacker-controlled directory-table offsets (lines 73/77/87), producing unbounded work, DoS, and out-of-bounds reads. The absent fix is a lower-bound/signedness check (`dir_count < 1`) or a pre-increment comparison on dirh.count.

evidence.reason: Filesystem-supplied `dirh.count` (read at line 57) is a 32-bit unsigned field, so `dir_count = dirh.count + 1` (line 59) wraps modulo 2^32: count = 0x7FFFFFFF yields dir_count = INT_MIN and count = 0xFFFFFFFE yields -1. The only guard on the path, `if(dir_count > SQUASHFS_DIR_COUNT)` (line 65), admits every value <= 256 including all negatives (no check-then-use or type drift: the same int reaches line 70 unchanged), so the loop here executes for every nonzero signed value — up to 2^32-1 iterations — while lines 73/77/87 read `directory_table + bytes` at attacker-controlled offsets. The arbitrary count is unbounded work driven by entry-point data with no visible cap, i.e. CWE-190 (wraparound defeats the bounds check) plus CWE-835 (unbounded loop/DoS); the absent one-statement fix is a signedness/lower-bound check such as `if(dir_count < 1 || dir_count > SQUASHFS_DIR_COUNT)`.

assumptions: SQUASHFS_DIR_COUNT is 256 and SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN is 256 (standard squashfs constants).
squashfs_dir_header_3.count is unsigned int (32-bit) and squashfs_dir_entry_3.size is unsigned short.
Integer conversion of 0x80000000..0xFFFFFFFF to int is two's-complement wrapping (all real toolchains).
Directory header/entry field values are read from filesystem data via memcpy, so they are attacker-controlled.
limitations: read_inode's return is dereferenced without a NULL check, but a NULL producer is not shown in the fragment.
directory_table allocation size is not shown, so a confirmed OOB read past the table is not independently provable.
`bytes += (*i)->offset` (48) and `size = (*i)->data + bytes - 3` (49) can overflow int, but the consumers lack a shown capacity, so they were not confirmed.
`strcpy` at line 101 depends on the unshown capacity of struct dir_ent.name; standard 257-byte capacity would fit the admitted strings.
The wrap-based guard bypass depends on the standard header layout/types, which are named but not fully declared inside the fragment.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the patched win_redr_status: the `this_ru_col <= 1` branch (lines 86-90) excludes the degenerate case that would make `p += len - (this_ru_col - 1); *p = '<'` (114-115) write on the NUL terminator and cause an out-of-bounds read in screen_puts, and the `len < MAXPATHL - 1` guard (line 54) plus bounded vim_snprintf sizes keep every NameBuff write inside MAXPATHL. No dangerous operation admits an unconstrained value.

evidence.reason: Protective branch: excludes this_ru_col == 1 (and below) from both truncation branches. Without it, this_ru_col == 1 makes line 112's `len > this_ru_col - 1` true with `this_ru_col - 1 == 0`, so line 114 computes p += len (the NUL slot of NameBuff), line 115 overwrites the terminator, and screen_puts at line 119 then reads past the buffer. With it, the admitted set is {this_ru_col >= 2}, so advance at 114 is in [1, len-1] and the NUL is preserved.

Protective bound on the space-append write into NameBuff (capacity MAXPATHL per the snprintf sizes at 58/64/74/79): admits only len <= MAXPATHL - 2, excluded set {len >= MAXPATHL - 1}, so the write index and the subsequent bounded vim_snprintf chain (size MAXPATHL - len >= 1) stay in-bounds.

Combined with the this_ru_col <= 1 branch (86-90), this guard admits only this_ru_col - 1 >= 1 and len > this_ru_col - 1, so the pointer advance is in [1, len-1]: the write replaces a real filename character, never the NUL, and the string read by screen_puts (119) remains NUL-terminated inside NameBuff.

assumptions: NameBuff has capacity MAXPATHL (capacity derived from the fragment's own guards and vim_snprintf sizes at lines 54, 58, 64, 74, 79).
get_trans_bufname fills NameBuff with a NUL-terminated name of length at most MAXPATHL - 1.
mbyte loop safety relies on mb_ptr2len never advancing i past the NUL terminator of a valid string (standard Vim contract).
limitations: screen_fill/screen_puts bounds depend on screen-row buffer capacity and window geometry invariants (e.g., w_width <= Columns keeping this_ru_col <= Columns) that are not declared in this fragment; a failing value would require broken internal geometry, not an entry-point input shown here.
get_keymap_str's MAXPATHL cap is passed at the call site (line 123) but its implementation is not shown.
NULL dereference is not demonstrable: no shown call in the fragment can produce NULL for p, NameBuff, or wp->w_buffer.

verdict.summary: Every memory read in SProcXkbSelectEvents is preceded by the guard at line 53 (dataLeft < size*2 -> BadLength) on the same dataLeft value that is decremented in lockstep with the from pointer, and dataLeft is always a multiple of 4, so the size-1 path's 4-byte consumption can neither underflow the counter nor let any later read escape the declared request region. No admitted entry-point value reaches an unprotected sink.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement for all reads: it excludes dataLeft < 4 before the 4-byte swaps at lines 56-57, excludes dataLeft < 8 before the 8-byte swapl at lines 60-61, and excludes dataLeft < 2 for the one-byte cases whose admitted set, intersected with the visible multiple-of-4 invariant from line 23 (length is a whole-word CARD16 count, subtractions are 4 or 8 bytes at line 67), is always >= the 4 bytes consumed, so no unsigned underflow can break the guard for later iterations. The guard passes the Guard-Identity Audit: it constrains the identical dataLeft value, unchanged between line 53 and the reads at lines 55-61.

assumptions: REQUEST_AT_LEAST_SIZE(xkbSelectEventsReq) (line 6) has its standard semantics: the received request is at least sizeof(xkbSelectEventsReq), i.e., length >= 4 words, so the line-23 computation never wraps to a huge unsigned dataLeft.
stuff->length is a CARD16 count of 4-byte words, so dataLeft (line 23) is always a multiple of 4 and every decrement at line 67 (4 or 8 bytes) preserves that invariant.
limitations: The one-byte detail cases (XkbBellNotify/XkbActionMessage/XkbCompatMapNotify) skip swapping and consume 4 bytes instead of 2 (lines 63-67); this is a byte-order/parsing correctness quirk with no memory-safety impact given the mod-4 invariant, so it is not classified as a vulnerability.

Whether the declared length could exceed the bytes actually received (buffer capacity) is enforced by the X server transport/dispatch layer not shown here; CWE-125 confirmation requires the buffer capacity to appear in the fragment, so that mismatch is unconfirmable from this code.
Line 71 passes unsigned dataLeft to %d; this is a benign signedness mismatch on a value bounded by 262124.

verdict.summary: Every confirmable dangerous operation is fully guarded: pols[0] dereferences are protected by the line 7 `!pols[0]` early return (excludes NULL) and the line 12 IS_ERR check (excludes error pointers), and the pols[1] dereference at line 31 is protected by the line 25 NULL check plus line 26 IS_ERR check. The remaining candidates (index-1 write at lines 20-24 and loop reads at line 36 beyond index 1) cannot be confirmed as OOB because the fragment declares or computes no capacity for the caller-supplied `pols` array, and NULL entries beyond index 1 have no in-fragment producer. No admitted value reaches an unprotected operation on any in-fragment derivable path.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement for the pols[0] dereferences at lines 15, 18, 19 and 24: it fully excludes the NULL case (and the zero-count case) for pols[0]. Guard-identity audit passes: no shown statement assigns to pols[0] between line 7 and the deref sites (line 12 only reads it via IS_ERR), so the same pointer value is constrained at every use. Combined with the IS_ERR(pols[0]) early return at line 12-13, the full failure set {NULL, ERR_PTR} is excluded. This is the decisive statement behind the NOT VULNERABLE verdict.

Decisive protective statement for the pols[1]->xfrm_nr dereference at line 31: it excludes the NULL case for the lookup result stored at line 20, and the nested IS_ERR(pols[1]) check at line 26-28 excludes the error-pointer case before the deref. Guard-identity audit passes: the checks are evaluated immediately before the use with no intervening assignment to pols[1]. The lookup's NULL result produced in-fragment at line 20 never reaches the line 35-40 loop because the line 30 increment is gated by this check.

assumptions: pols, *num_pols and *num_xfrms are assumed to reference valid, writable caller storage, with IS_ERR/PTR_ERR and struct xfrm_policy field semantics standard for the kernel context.

Only the fragment's own visible invariants are relied on: *num_pols >= 1 and pols[0] non-NULL after line 7-11, pols[0] non-ERR after line 12-13, and pols[1] non-NULL/non-ERR before line 31 per lines 25-26.
limitations: The write pols[1] = xfrm_policy_lookup_bytype(...) at lines 20-24 would be an out-of-bounds write only if the caller's pols array has capacity 1. The fragment declares/computes no capacity for pols, which the CWE-787 confirmation rule requires, so this candidate is demoted and not treated as a confirmed vulnerability.

The loop read pols[i]->action at line 36 can exceed index 1 only when the caller supplies *num_pols >= 3 at entry; array capacity and entry contents are caller-supplied, and NULL entries beyond index 1 have no in-fragment producer (the only in-fragment NULL source is the line 20 lookup result, which is checked at line 25), so these cases are caller-dependent and unconfirmable.

Whether the sub-policy branch (lines 18-33) is reachable at all depends on CONFIG_XFRM_SUB_POLICY and on runtime policy action/type values supplied by the kernel policy store; the safety analysis holds regardless because the NULL/ERR guards are independent of that gate.

verdict.summary: The page-frag fast path of esp_output_head() never bounds tailen (or allocsize = ALIGN(tailen, L1_CACHE_BYTES), line 33) by the maximum size skb_page_frag_refill can provide ((PAGE_SIZE << SKB_FRAG_PAGE_ORDER)). skb_page_frag_refill (line 37) can return true with only a single page even for a larger request, so esp_output_fill_trailer() at line 47 writes the ESP trailer past the end of the page-frag buffer and __skb_fill_page_desc() at lines 51-52 records a frag size larger than its backing page. The missing one-statement fix is the COW gate added by upstream commit ebe48d368e97: fall back to the cow label when ALIGN(skb->data_len + tailen, L1_CACHE_BYTES) exceeds the page-frag max size.

evidence.reason: Sink writes the ESP trailer (region sized by esp->tailen) through `tail = page_address(page) + pfrag->offset` (line 45) into the page-frag page obtained at lines 37/42, whose usable capacity is at most (PAGE_SIZE << SKB_FRAG_PAGE_ORDER) when the refill returns a single page. tailen (line 8, int) is unconstrained above in this fragment: line 19 admits tailen > tailroom, lines 25-26 constrain only nr_frags/frag_list, and line 37 checks only allocation success, not size-vs-capacity. Witness: tailen = 4097 on a 4096-byte order-0 page with tailroom < 4097 writes past the allocation (CWE-787 heap out-of-bounds write). Absent fix: `if (ALIGN(skb->data_len + tailen, L1_CACHE_BYTES) > (PAGE_SIZE << SKB_FRAG_PAGE_ORDER)) goto cow;` before the fast path.

Records a frag of size tailen on page (line 42), whose capacity is limited to the single page returned by skb_page_frag_refill, while tailen retains its full unbounded residual range (line 19 admits tailen > tailroom; lines 25-26 bound only the frags[] index nfrags < MAX_SKB_FRAGS; line 37 does not cap size). For tailen > page capacity (e.g., 4097 on a 4096-byte page) the descriptor claims more bytes than the backing page holds, and the same missing size gate (force COW when ALIGN(data_len+tailen) > ESP_SKB_FRAG_MAXSIZE) leaves the oversized descriptor admitted; later copy/DMA consumption of the frag reads beyond the page (CWE-787/CWE-125).

assumptions: skb_shinfo(skb)->frags[] has MAX_SKB_FRAGS entries, so line 25 `nr_frags < MAX_SKB_FRAGS` admits indexes 0..MAX_SKB_FRAGS-1 (index guard for __skb_fill_page_desc passes the audit).

skb_page_frag_refill's guarantee is at most (PAGE_SIZE << SKB_FRAG_PAGE_ORDER) of contiguous space and can return true with a single page even when the requested size exceeds it (order-0 default), per its standard kernel semantics confirmed by fix commit ebe48d368e97.
esp_output_fill_trailer fills the ESP trailer region sized by esp->tailen (tfclen+plen+2 layout), so a trailer write requires tailen bytes of space at `tail`.
pskb_put (line 82) needs tailen bytes of tailroom on `trailer`; branch A guarantees it via line 19 and the cow path via skb_cow_data (line 74) with its return checked at line 75.
limitations: Negative tailen would require a caller contract violation not shown in the fragment, so that degenerate case is not used for the verdict.

Reachability of tailen > page capacity depends on the unshown caller passing a large ESP message and on tailroom being smaller than tailen; the fragment itself imposes no upper bound, which is the demonstrated gap.

The later incomplete-fix discussion (commit 5bd8baab087d) shows the size gate should use the combined ALIGN(skb->data_len + tailen, L1_CACHE_BYTES); regardless of exact combined form, the shown fragment contains no capacity bound at all.

verdict.summary: No dangerous operation with a demonstrated failure set is left unprotected. Both loops that fill the local array `tagvalues[INDX_TAGVALUES_MAX]` (declared line 108) are backstopped at lines 111 and 120 by `tagvalues_count < INDX_TAGVALUES_MAX`, evaluated at the same control point as the indexed write, excluding every write at index >= INDX_TAGVALUES_MAX (CWE-787/805 prevented); the downstream `memcpy` (line 133) inherits the same cap. Remaining candidates involve capacities or helper bodies not visible in the fragment and are recorded as limitations rather than confirmed vulnerabilities.

evidence.reason: Protective statement for the stack write at line 114 (`tagvalues[tagvalues_count++]`). verdict.summary: In case EXTRA of inflate(), the gzip header extra-field copy computes its source/dest size as 'extra_max - len' with unsigned arithmetic. 'len' (= extra_len - state->length) is the number of extra bytes already consumed and is not clamped by extra_max, while consumption 'state->length -= copy' uses the unclamped 'copy'. When XLEN exceeds the app-provided buffer (extra_max) and the stream is fed across calls (the fragment's own resume path at line 155), a later call reaches the zmemcpy with len > extra_max, making 'extra_max - len' underflow to ~4 GiB and causing a heap out-of-bounds write past 'head->extra' plus an out-of-bounds read past the input buffer. The ternary at lines 146-147 only bounds the size operand for len <= extra_max and does not protect the sink.

evidence.reason: Sink: heap write to state->head->extra + len and read from next. len = state->head->extra_len - state->length (line 144) equals bytes of the extra field consumed so far; extra_len is the attacker-controlled 16-bit XLEN (line 128) with no cap, and state->length decreases by the unclamped copy (lines 139-153), so len can exceed the buffer capacity extra_max (line 146) when XLEN > extra_max and inflate is resumed across calls (line 155 goto inf_leave preserves state). The guard at lines 146-147 only constrains the copy SIZE for len <= extra_max; for len > extra_max it evaluates extra_max - len, which underflows unsigned (e.g., extra_max=16, len=1000 -> 0xFFFFFC10), so a ~4 GiB copy is admitted by every guard on the path. This is a heap-based out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) past the extra_max-sized buffer and an out-of-bounds read of the input (CWE-125). Absent one-statement fix: clamp the consumption copy to extra_max - len before the zmemcpy and before 'state->length -= copy' (line 153), e.g. 'if (copy > state->head->extra_max - len) copy = state->head->extra_max - len;', or reject len > state->head->extra_max.

assumptions: state->head->extra_max is the capacity of state->head->extra (used as the capacity constant in the clamp expression at line 146).
XLEN, FLG, and the extra/name/comment bytes are parsed from the entry-point input stream (lines 126-128, 165, 187) and are fully attacker-controlled 16-bit fields.

The streaming resume path (line 155 'if (state->length) goto inf_leave;' with LOAD/RESTORE preserving state) is the fragment's own documented behavior, so per-call input chunking is intrinsic to the code, not an external assumption.

limitations: Exploitation requires the ability to create a BPF stack map (privileged or unprivileged-BPF-permitted environment), which is a caller/environment precondition not shown in the fragment.
The body of pcpu_freelist_populate and post-map-creation write paths are not shown; the OOB outcome rests on its standard stride/count semantics.
The return-status handling for pcpu_freelist_init (lines 11-13) with the free_elems cleanup is correct and was not treated as a finding.

verdict.summary: Patched do_put: the MBLOCK multiplication-overflow guard (L363-365), the one-line multiplication-overflow guard (L504/L509) and the empty/NULL y_array gate (L182-187) are all present, pass the guard-identity audit, and fully constrain totlen and every memmove/memset/STRMOVE size before the allocations, so no unconstrained value reaches a dangerous operation.

verdict.summary: ex_retab computes the new-line allocation size from len = num_spaces + num_tabs, which is derived from buffer whitespace runs and the tabstop argument with no upper bound (no MAXCOL cap); the missing bound check (fixed upstream by guarding new_len >= MAXCOL before alloc) admits arbitrarily large sizes into alloc() and the subsequent memmove/fill operations that write len bytes, causing uncontrolled memory allocation/resource exhaustion.

evidence.reason: Sink: allocation whose size is old_len - col + start_col + len + 1, where len is set at line 128 (len = num_spaces + num_tabs) from vcol - start_vcol (line 91) and num_tabs from tabstop_fromto (lines 98-99). len has no upper bound in the fragment: the tabstop-argument validation (lines 50-61) caps the tab width at TABSTOP_MAX but cannot cap len, which scales with the buffer whitespace-run length (entry-point file content, ml_get line 65) times the tab width, and the guard at line 113 (curbuf->b_p_et || got_tab || (num_spaces + num_tabs < len)) admits every whitespace run containing a tab (got_tab) with no size cap. The line-131 NULL check only tests allocation success and does not constrain the size, so a huge len reaches alloc() and the tail memmove (lines 135-136) plus the fill loop (lines 138-139) that write len bytes. Absent one-statement fix: a bound test such as 'if (old_len - col + start_col + len + 1 <= 0 || old_len - col + start_col + len + 1 >= MAXCOL) { emsg_text_too_long(); break; }' before alloc. The fragment's residual range for len is unconstrained, confirming CWE-770 (uncontrolled allocation of an attacker-scaled size with unbounded subsequent writes).

assumptions: alloc() allocates the requested size and may fail, returning NULL, which the fragment checks at line 131.

The buffer capacity equals the exact-fit expression at line 130, so the prefix copy (line 134), tail copy (lines 135-136) and fill loop (lines 138-139) do not exceed the allocated capacity within a single retab call.

tabstop argument validation (lines 50-61, and tabstop_set at line 32) bounds each tab width to [0, TABSTOP_MAX] but does not bound len, which is the product-like sum of whitespace width over the scanned run.
limitations: A strict single-call out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) is not independently derivable from the fragment because the writes are exact-fit to the line-130 capacity; upstream's crash when repeatedly using :retab relies on repeated invocations growing the line past MAXCOL and on the (colnr_T)vcol truncation at line 155 corrupting virtual-column bookkeeping, which is outside a single-call demonstration.
Effects of feeding a >MAXCOL line into ml_replace/changed_lines (callee behavior not shown) are not used as the confirmable failure; they would strengthen the finding only with unshown causalities.

Vulnerability trigger requires attacker-controlled buffer content (a crafted file) plus a :retab invocation (possibly repeated), making this a local denial-of-service / resource-exhaustion concern rather than remote code execution.

verdict.summary: EVT_TRANSACTION handling admits undersized NFC frames: the length gate at L22-23 uses && instead of ||, so frames with skb->len < NFC_MIN_AID_LENGTH+2 whose first byte equals the AID tag proceed. Later unbounded reads (skb->data[aid_len+2], [aid_len+3]) go out of bounds, and the params-length check at L47 underflows unsigned, letting params_len up to 255 drive a memcpy that writes past the skb->len-2-byte allocation and reads past the frame.

evidence.reason: OOB read (CWE-125). skb->data has capacity skb->len bytes (attacker-controlled frame length, u32). The guard at L22-23 returns -EPROTO only when BOTH skb->len < NFC_MIN_AID_LENGTH+2 AND skb->data[0] != AID_TAG, so a 2-byte frame with data[0]==AID_TAG and data[1]==0 (aid_len=0, passing the L33 cap) is admitted; index aid_len+2 == 2 exceeds len-1 == 1. The L33 check constrains only the struct-array size, not skb->len (wrong-target drift for this source read). Absent one-statement fix: change && to || at L22 (or add an explicit skb->len >= NFC_MIN_AID_LENGTH+2 check) so short frames return -EPROTO.

OOB read (CWE-125). With the same admitted 2-byte frame (data[0]==AID_TAG, aid_len=0, passing L33), index aid_len+3 == 3 exceeds len-1 == 1; the u8 value read (0..255) is then passed through the underflowed L47 check into the params memcpy at L50-51. Absent fix: correct length gate at L22 (||) or an explicit aid_len+3 < skb->len check before this read.

Out-of-bounds write (CWE-787, primary) and out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). Capacity: allocation at L26 is skb->len - 2 bytes. Witness: 4-byte frame [0x81, 0x01, 0x00, 0x82] is admitted by L22-23 (data[0]==AID_TAG makes the && guard not return), aid_len=1 passes L33, data[3]==0x82 passes L40-42; L44 reads data[4] OOB into params_len; L47 admits every u8 params_len because (4-2) - sizeof(struct nfc_evt_transaction) underflows to a huge unsigned value, so params_len > huge is always false. memcpy then writes up to 255 bytes at &transaction->params (offset well beyond 2) into the 2-byte kmalloc object -> heap overflow, and reads skb->data[5..] past skb->len. Absent fix: a len-relative, non-underflowing bound, e.g. if (transaction->params_len + transaction->aid_len + 4 > skb->len) return -EINVAL.

assumptions: skb is the NFC frame buffer received from the wire: skb->len (u32) and skb->data[i] are entry-point, attacker-controlled values.
NFC_EVT_TRANSACTION_AID_TAG is 0x81 per the in-fragment spec comment (AID tag 81), so data[0]==AID_TAG is attacker-satisfiable.

sizeof(struct nfc_evt_transaction) > 2 because the struct embeds transaction->aid (whose sizeof is used at L33) plus the two length fields, so (skb->len - 2) - sizeof(...) underflows for small skb->len such as 4.
devm_kzalloc for size 2 returns a non-NULL 2-byte allocation, or the L27-28 NULL check exits; memcpy semantics: count bytes must fit in dest and be readable from source.
The witness lengths (2 and 4) are below NFC_MIN_AID_LENGTH+2 regardless of the constant's exact value, and are admitted purely because of the && flaw at L22-23.
limitations: skb->len == 1: skb->len - 2 wraps to ~4 GiB; the subsequent skb->data[1] read is only reached if that huge allocation succeeded, which is not assumed, so this path is not used as a witness.
skb->len == 0: the L22-23 guard itself would evaluate skb->data[0]; the byte is physically inside the skb head, so this is ambiguous and demoted.
The -EPROTO/-ENOMEM/-EINVAL returns at L24/L28/L34/L42/L48 skip kfree_skb, leaking the skb per malformed event; flagged as a robustness/resource concern, not the decisive one-statement security diff.

Exact numeric value of NFC_MIN_AID_LENGTH and sizeof(struct nfc_evt_transaction) are not shown; the verdict holds for any plausible values because the ||-gate admission and the unsigned underflow are structural.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation in ReadBMPImage carries an in-fragment protective statement. Dimensions, planes, bits-per-pixel, number of colors, and compression are validated (lines 331-349) before any use. The 1-bit and 4-bit scanline index writes are capped at columns-1 by split main/remainder loops (lines 628-646 and 672-690). Pixel-buffer reads/writes stay inside the rows*MagickMax(bytes_per_line, image->columns+256UL) allocation (lines 462-464, 483-484) because each per-case bytes_per_line recomputation (lines 757, 815, 855) equals or is smaller than the header bytes_per_line (line 455). Colormap size is bounded to 1<<bpp <= 256 colors with the ReadBlob count checked (lines 341-343, 412-441). All allocation, seek, read, and queue results are checked before use. No admitted value reaches an unprotected sink.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement for the 1-bit index-queue write sink SetPixelIndex(indexes+x+bit,index) at line 633: the bound admits only x <= columns-8, so x+bit <= columns-1 < image->columns. The tail is covered verbatim by the remainder loop at lines 638-643 (bit < image->columns % 8, x = columns-(columns%8), so x+bit <= columns-1). Guard constrains the same x at the same ssize_t precision with no intervening write; failure set {index >= columns} is empty.

Completes coverage of the 1-bit remainder write SetPixelIndex(indexes+x+bit,index) at line 643: bit stays in [0, column%8-1] and x equals the largest multiple of 8 below columns, so the last written index is columns-1; one byte is read for the tail (line 645), keeping *p reads within the padded bytes_per_line row (line 455).

Pixel-array capacity is rows*MagickMax(bytes_per_line, columns+256UL) bytes, and every conversion loop recomputes bytes_per_line (lines 757, 815, 855) that is <= the header bytes_per_line (line 455), so each row's p reads (lines 632/642/674/677/684/721/767-768/824-826/868-871) and the 32-bit alpha probe *(p+3) (line 518) never exceed the allocation; the 256UL slack also backs the RLE DecodeImage path (lines 483-484).

Bounds the colormap: image->colors (lines 378-382) is at most 1<<bits_per_pixel <= 256, so AcquireQuantumMemory(colors,4) (lines 412-413), ReadBlob(packet_size*colors) with its count check (lines 426-427), and the copy loop i < image->colors reading 3 or 4 bytes per entry (lines 434-441) all stay within allocated memory.

Read-status check for the pixel buffer: a short file cannot leave a partially filled buffer that the conversion loops then consume; combined with the length/8 vs GetBlobSize check (lines 457-458) and the allocation guard (lines 462-463), the read/write window matches the buffer exactly.

assumptions: 64-bit size_t/ssize_t arithmetic (ImageMagick LP64 targets); columns and rows derive from validated positive ssize_t values (lines 331-334), so columns>=1 and rows>=1 reach the conversion loops.
QueueAuthenticPixels(image,0,y,image->columns,1,...) (e.g. line 624) provides an index queue exactly image->columns entries wide, so writes below columns are in bounds.

Callee semantics of the shown standard helpers are as named: ReadBlob returns bytes actually read, AcquireQuantumMemory/AcquireVirtualMemory return NULL on failure, SeekBlob returns negative offset on failure.
limitations: Size_t wrap in image->columns*bits_per_pixel+31 (line 455) and bytes_per_line*image->rows (line 456) for column counts near SSIZE_MAX is not exploitable purely from shown code: turning it into an OOB write additionally requires the unshown internal multiplication/allocation behavior of AcquireVirtualMemory/SetImageExtent to wrap and succeed; demoted, not a confirmed finding.

DecodeImage (lines 488-489) body is not shown; its RLE output failure set is not derivable here, and the +256UL allocation slack is the only in-fragment protection, so RLE internals are treated as out of scope.
SetImageExtent (line 390) and QueueAuthenticPixels NULL results may independently reject extreme dimensions; those internal guarantees are neither used to protect nor to condemn any path.
The `if (x < (ssize_t) image->columns) break;` at line 689 and the pixel_read/colormap flows were audited as dead or bounded; no confirmed flaw found in them.

verdict.summary: In SProcXkbSelectEvents, the length check at line 53 is evaluated against size before the else branch (lines 63-64) reassigns size=2: for the size-1 event class only 2 bytes are required, but lines 66-67 then consume/advance 4 bytes. A dataLeft of 2 or 3 (admitted by every guard and derived from attacker-controlled req_len/affectWhich with no shown exclusion) wraps the unsigned counter, and the next loop iteration's swaps/swapl then read past the end of the request buffer (CWE-125, enabled by CWE-191).

When the switch yields size=1 (lines 44-47), line 53 admits dataLeft >= 2, but lines 63-64 change size to 2 and lines 66-67 advance `from.c8` by 4 and execute `dataLeft -= 4`; for dataLeft==2/3 (residual range from line 23 with only the >=0 bound of line 6 shown) this wraps dataLeft (unsigned) to ~0xFFFFFFFE. verdict.summary: In TCP octet-counting framing, iOctetsRemain accumulates attacker-supplied decimal digits at line 33 with no bound and can wrap negative; the terminator checks at lines 40-45 only log and still enter message mode (line 54), so a negative octet count reaches memcpy at line 108 and is converted to a huge size_t, causing an out-of-bounds heap write.

evidence.reason: octatesToCopy originates from iOctetsRemain (line 98), an int accumulated from network digits at line 33 with no cap; after 12 '9' bytes the signed int wraps negative (-727379969). The L40 guard (iOctetsRemain < 1) and L45 guard (iOctetsRemain > iMaxLine) are log-only branches that both fall through to inputState = eInMsg (L54) without clamping, failing the Guard-Identity Audit (check-then-use drift). The L100 clamp (buffLen < octatesToCopy) is false for a negative value and L103 (octatesToCopy + iMsg > iMaxLine) is also false, so the negative int is passed as memcpy's size_t count (CWE-195), writing far past the iMaxLine-sized pMsg (capacity fixed by the L92/L103-105 clamps), i.e., CWE-787 heap overflow. Absent fix: a sign/upper-bound check (e.g., iOctetsRemain < 1 || iOctetsRemain > iMaxLine => reset state or saturate) before the copy.

assumptions: int is 32-bit two's-complement; signed overflow at line 33 wraps as on mainstream compilers (the fragment itself handles iOctetsRemain < 1).

buffLen is non-negative when the fragment consumes *buff (c = **buff is read at line 10); buffLen < 0 is not excluded by the fragment itself.
limitations: The -1 advance of *buff at line 111 when octatesToCopy + octatesToDiscard == 0 depends on the unshown caller's buffer management; not relied upon for the verdict.

pMsg's actual allocation size is not shown; the verdict uses the iMaxLine capacity the fragment itself enforces.
Positive wrapped counts (e.g., 10 digits) are neutralized by the L100/103 clamps and are not claimed as a flaw.

verdict.summary: Guest-controlled args.nargs from the kvm_read_guest copy (line 16) is used as an unbounded array index in line 28 to form args.rets; no bound check exists, so a malicious guest can set nargs past the args.args capacity and KVM RTAS handlers (invoked at line 35) write through the resulting out-of-bounds pointer, corrupting the host kernel stack.

Any nargs >= the array capacity (standard KVM PPC layout args[16]) produces an out-of-bounds pointer that is stored in args.rets and later written through by the handler at line 35. No guard constrains nargs: line 18 only checks kvm_read_guest's return, line 34 only selects the handler, and line 43 only gates write-back after the sink. The absent fix is a bound check before line 28, e.g., 'if (be32_to_cpu(args.nargs) + be32_to_cpu(args.nret) > ARRAY_SIZE(args.args)) goto fail;'. Mechanism: stack out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) from unchecked attacker-controlled index.

The RTAS handler receives &args whose rets field was already set at line 28 to an attacker-controlled offset into (or past) args.args; per the fragment's own comment (lines 21-26) rets points into args.args and handlers write their nret return values through it. Since nargs+nret is never checked, handler stores land outside the local args struct on the kernel stack, completing the CWE-787 out-of-bounds write admitted by every guard on the path (lines 18, 34, 43 never constrain nargs).

be32_to_cpu returns an unsigned 32-bit value used directly as an array index, so no negative-index path exists; the threat is the missing upper bound.
limitations: The exact capacity of args.args (standard KVM PPC layout is 16 entries) is not declared inside the shown fragment; the verdict relies on the standard rtas_args layout, lowering confidence below 0.8.

Handler bodies are not shown; their write behavior is inferred from the fragment's own documentation that args.rets points into args.args and from the standard RTAS handler contract of writing nret results through rets.

verdict.summary: In change_indent, the INSERT-mode cursor walker (L95-103) advances the byte index new_cursor_col with no bound against the line length (STRLEN(ptr)) and then dereferences ptr + new_cursor_col in mb_ptr2len (L99) and lbr_chartabsize (L102). The absent one-statement fix is an end-of-line break, e.g. 'if (ptr[new_cursor_col] == NUL) break;' or 'if (new_cursor_col >= (int)STRLEN(ptr)) break;' at the top of the loop body.

Absent fix: 'if (new_cursor_col >= (int)STRLEN(ptr)) break;' (or the equivalent NUL check) placed before L99/L102.

Sink (heap read): mb_ptr2len reads the character at ptr + new_cursor_col. Same unconstrained index from the L95-103 loop: nothing bounds new_cursor_col against the line capacity derived from ml_get_curline() (L94), and the only guard (L95 vcol <= w_virtcol, L98 new_cursor_col >= 0) does not constrain the upper bound of the byte index. assumptions: ptr (L94) points to the NUL-terminated current line returned by ml_get_curline(); byte indices greater than STRLEN(ptr) are out of bounds for the buffer (standard C string semantics, consistent with the NUL/strsave usage in the fragment).

The 2-word OVECTOR pair is added to length only when both bits are first-time (paired assert on the +1 slot), excluding an undercount of the second word and a double count of the pair; same guard identity before and at the increment, no drift.

The global capture_last slot contributes to length exactly once across the whole bytecode walk regardless of how many opcodes reference it, keeping the frame-size count equal to the distinct slots the unshown transfer routine dedupes with the same bitset.

assumptions: ccend is the one-past-end bound of the compiled bytecode window, as shown by the loop condition `while (cc < ccend)` (line 21) and the post-loop assertion (line 236).
common->recurse_bitset is allocated with size common->recurse_bitset_size by the caller, matching the memset length at line 13.

recurse_check_bit returns TRUE exactly on the first sighting of a machine-word slot and FALSE thereafter, and the same bitset/dedup discipline is used by the (unshown) sibling transfer routine, per upstream fix commit 03654e751e7f (CVE-2022-1587).
limitations: Multi-byte bytecode reads (PRIVATE_DATA(cc + 1) at lines 48-49; GET2 at 74/89; GET at 106/179; *alternative at 107; cc[1] at 202/214; cc[-1] at 118/131/144) are out-of-bounds only for a truncated/corrupt compiled-opcode buffer whose production is not shown (category (c)); these reads are structurally identical in both pair members and are not the fix delta, so they are demoted.

The downstream allocation and transfer functions are not shown; the equal-count guarantee depends on that sibling walk using the same dedup bitset, as the upstream 10.40-B patch applies to both functions.

verdict.summary: TfLiteIntArrayGetSizeInBytes accepts a signed int 'size' with no bound check; 'sizeof(dummy.data[0]) * size' converts a negative size to a huge size_t and wraps, and the MSVC branch then underflows, so the returned allocation size can be 0 or near-SIZE_MAX instead of sizeof(TfLiteIntArray)+sizeof(int)*size, leading callers to allocate an undersized buffer for 'size' elements (heap corruption) or an absurdly large one.

evidence.reason: 'size' is an unconstrained signed int (residual range includes all negatives since no check is shown). In 'sizeof(dummy.data[0]) * size' the int is converted to size_t (CWE-195); e.g. size = -1 wraps to sizeof(dummy) - 4, size = -2 to 0, while 32-bit size_t also overflows for size >= 2^30. The resulting wrapped value is returned at line 12 as the allocation size consumed by callers, yielding an undersized buffer for 'size' elements (CWE-190 -> undersized allocation -> heap overflow). The absent one-statement fix is 'if (size < 0) return 0;' placed before this arithmetic.

On MSVC, once a negative-derived 'size' wraps computed_size below sizeof(dummy.data[0]) (e.g. size = -2 gives 0), the unsigned subtraction underflows to near SIZE_MAX, which is then returned at line 12 as the allocation size; this is the same missing negative-size guard (CWE-195) and additionally demonstrates unsigned underflow (CWE-190) wholly inside the fragment.

assumptions: sizeof(int) = 4 and sizeof(TfLiteIntArray) includes one embedded data element (8 bytes); the line-10 correction in the fragment implies the struct embeds data[0].
The function's name and return value imply the result is used by callers as an allocation size.
limitations: No call site is shown; if every caller independently rejected negative 'size', the corruption would not materialize, but the fragment itself provides no such check.
On 64-bit platforms, non-negative int sizes up to INT32_MAX cannot overflow the product; the confirmed wrap requires a negative input (or a 32-bit size_t).

verdict.summary: send_control_msg() copies len bytes via memcpy into elem.in_sg[0].iov_base without verifying that elem.in_sg[0].iov_len >= len. The in_sg buffer and its iov_len are filled from attacker-controlled virtqueue descriptors with no shown minimum, so iov_len == 0 (or any value below len) is admitted and drives an out-of-bounds write.

evidence.reason: CWE-787 out-of-bounds write: memcpy copies len bytes into elem.in_sg[0].iov_base whose capacity is elem.in_sg[0].iov_len (iovec convention), but no shown statement constrains len relative to iov_len. len (size_t, residual range 0..SIZE_MAX) and iov_len (attacker-controlled via virtqueue_pop at line 10, no shown minimum) both retain full unconstrained domains. Degenerate witness: attacker supplies iov_len == 0; any reaching len >= 1 is admitted by the virtio_queue_ready (line 7) and virtqueue_pop (line 10) guards and writes past the destination. Absent fix: a pre-sink check such as 'if (elem.in_sg[0].iov_len < len) return 0;' placed before line 14.

elem.in_sg is a struct iovec-style array, so iov_len names the capacity of iov_base per standard iovec semantics.
virtio_queue_ready and virtqueue_pop failures are correctly handled by early returns and are not findings.
limitations: No call site of send_control_msg is shown, so the concrete value of len is unknown; this does not affect the verdict because any len >= 1 with iov_len == 0 already fails.
A NULL iov_base dereference arising from an empty in-scatter list is not used as a finding; the confirmed mechanism is the size-mismatch OOB write.
Failure depends on standard memcpy semantics (copies exactly len bytes), which is the documented behavior of the named sink.

Absent fix: an ehdr->e_shstrndx < ehdr->e_shnum check (plus table-extent bound) before this read; the only guard, validated_offset (line 184), runs later and constrains name, not this index (wrong-target drift), so any e_shstrndx >= available entries reads out of bounds (CWE-125).

dynamic (line 335) has no initializer and is set only when the loop at lines 337-345 matches a section named ".dynamic"; an attacker omitting that name leaves it indeterminate, and shdr[dynamic] then indexes the unchecked shdr table (e_shoff unvalidated at line 176; capacity st.st_size at line 23). Absent fixes: initialize dynamic=-1 and reject out-of-range indices before this use; the line-184 validated_offset guard does not cover this path. CWE-457 (uninitialized index) feeding CWE-125 (OOB read).

Absent fix: apply that same validated_offset (or equivalent name < elf_map + st.st_size bound) before line 367; a d_val near UINT32_MAX makes the string scan run past the mapped region (CWE-125 OOB read).

assumptions: elf_map's capacity is st.st_size bytes (line 23).
ELF header, section-header, program-header, and dynamic fields are read from attacker-controlled file bytes.
validated_offset (line 184) returns nonzero for an out-of-range pointer, as the error path treats it.
limitations: strcpy(&name[15 - 6], "[...]") (line 259) writes 6 bytes into the mapped region after the strlen(name) > 15 test and the line-184 start-pointer check; not used as the decisive sink because full-string residency inside the map is not fully provable from the fragment.
get_elf_class (line 10) internals are unshown; MODE only selects which block runs.
The 64-bit twin statements (e.g., lines 999, 1000, 1016, 1017) mirror the confirmed 32-bit findings and are not reported separately.

With PNG-valid channels (max 4), height*width*channels <= 2^31-4 (fits int32) and channels*width*sizeof(uint16) <= 2^30-8, so no signed overflow and no wrapped row stride reaches png::CommonFinishDecode or new[]. Passes Guard-Identity Audit: no intervening assignment alters width/height between the check and the sinks; all three status returns are checked.

Sink allocation whose size expression is fed only by width/height bounded at lines 28-30 (admitted product < 2^29) and decode.channels, for which no in-fragment producer can derive a value exceeding the PNG maximum, so the int32 multiplication cannot wrap and the allocated element count matches the row-write capacity consumed at lines 90-92. png::CommonFinishDecode writes height rows of channels*width*element_size bytes into the provided buffer, matching the buffer capacities declared at lines 42-43, 47-48, and 87.
Standard new[] semantics: allocation failure throws/errors rather than performing an out-of-bounds write.
limitations: decode.channels is not constrained by a visible statement in the fragment; an int-overflow witness in channels*width would require a channels value no shown code can derive, so it is unconfirmable and demoted here.

Admitted dimensions allow up to ~2-4 GiB allocations (totally bounded, fitting int64), so a resource-exhaustion/DoS concern from very large PNGs is possible but is independent of the one-statement fix pair and not confirmed as memory corruption.
png::CommonInitDecode's internal validation of channels is not shown; a bound stated only outside the fragment is unusable, which caps confidence at 0.72 for the safe verdict.

verdict.summary: startSslClient stores SSL_new()'s result without a NULL check and immediately dereferences it, so an allocation failure (SSL_new returning NULL) reaches SSL_set_options and the other ssl uses as a NULL-pointer dereference (CWE-476). Independently, SSL_connect's return is tested only with 'rc < 0', so the documented handshake-failure return rc == 0 is treated as success and the socket is marked isssl = true (CWE-697).

The absent fix is a NULL check on the SSL_new result placed before the first use at line 88, which would exclude the NULL witness. This confirms CWE-476 (NULL-pointer dereference from an unchecked shown allocation).

SSL_connect at line 104 returns rc == 0 for a controlled handshake failure (standard OpenSSL semantics); the guard at line 105 'if (rc < 0)' admits rc == 0 and rc > 0, so the failure value rc == 0 reaches the security decision at line 119, marking the socket SSL-connected and returning success at line 121. Guard-identity audit passes (same value, same type, no mutation between 105 and 119), so the defect is the comparison operator itself: the absent fix is 'if (rc <= 0)', which would exclude the rc == 0 witness. This confirms CWE-697 (incorrect comparison admitting a documented failure boundary).

assumptions: Standard OpenSSL semantics implied by the call names: SSL_new returns NULL on allocation failure; SSL_connect returns 1 on success, 0 when the handshake failed and the connection was shut down, <0 on error.
ctx is materially valid at line 87 because SSL_CTX_new's NULL result is rejected at line 14 and all earlier failure paths return.
limitations: SSL_new failure is OOM-driven, so attacker triggerability is indirect; the verified defect is the unchecked-allocation NULL dereference pattern.
Downstream behavior after rc == 0 with isssl = true is not shown, so the impact is limited to misreporting a failed TLS handshake as an established connection.
The line-23 SSL_CTX_set_timeout check is semantically meaningless (the API returns the previous timeout, not an error) but admits no dangerous value and is not confirmed as exploitable.

No callers are shown; certificate_path and hostname are treated as caller-supplied entry data reaching only safe sinks.

verdict.summary: Every attacker-controlled EC parameter value is constrained before use: field size is capped at OPENSSL_ECC_MAX_FIELD_BITS (L55, L151), basis exponents are strictly ordered positive and below m (L78, L100-102), the order is required non-negative, non-zero, and Hasse-bounded (L204, L208), and every allocation/ASN.1 conversion/point-decoding return is checked (L30, L35, L60, L140, L163, L171, L185, L193, L222).

evidence.reason: Caps the attacker-controlled field size used by BN_set_bit at L85/L109 and by curve construction: field_bits (= char_two->m, L54) is admitted only if <= OPENSSL_ECC_MAX_FIELD_BITS; combined with L78/L100-102 which require m > k > 0, the admitted range is [2, 571], so the (int) casts at L85/L109 and L111-115 are in-range and the oversized-field DoS/non-termination failure set is fully excluded.

Guards the trinomial exponent consumed by BN_set_bit(p, (int)tmp_long) at L87: it admits only tmp_long in [1, m-1] with m <= 571 (L55), so the bit index is positive and within the field width; the same value is checked and then used with no intervening mutation (Guard-Identity Audit passes).

Guards the pentanomial exponents k1/k2/k3 consumed at L111-115: admits only 1 <= k1 < k2 < k3 < m with m <= 571, so every BN_set_bit index is in [1, 570] and each check-to-use is on the identical, unmodified values.

The base-point decode is a checked sink: EC_POINT_oct2point's return status is tested on the next line, and any failure (including base->length == 0 or a malformed octet string) jumps to the clean error path, so no unchecked result reaches ret.

The group order is validated before EC_GROUP_set_generator at L222: negative/zero orders are rejected and orders larger than field_bits+1 are rejected; since field_bits <= 571 on both field paths (L55/L151), (int)field_bits + 1 cannot overflow and the Hasse comparison is exact.

assumptions: ASN1_STRING/ASN1_INTEGER fields (a->length, b->length, seed->length, base->length) are data/length-consistent as produced by the ASN.1 decoder, with no negative lengths producible in-fragment.
OPENSSL_ECC_MAX_FIELD_BITS caps the field at 571 bits.
EC_GROUP_new_curve_GF2m/GFp, EC_POINT_new, BN_CTX_new, OPENSSL_malloc and ASN1_INTEGER_to_BN return NULL on failure and every such return is checked in the fragment.
EC_GROUP_new_curve_* duplicates a and b into the group, so later reuse of the a/b BIGNUMs for order/cofactor does not corrupt the group.
limitations: params->base->data[0] at L190 requires base->length >= 1; the guard at L180 checks only non-NULL data and admits length == 0, but the capacity of base->data is not declared or computed in the fragment, so the CWE-125 confirmation rule is not met and the candidate is demoted.
Negative a->length/b->length/base->length values are not derivable from any shown producer; BN_bin2bn/oct2point NULL/error returns are handled, so negative-length paths are not confirmed.

The cofactor is not validated for sign/zero at L217, but its only shown consumer is EC_GROUP_set_generator whose return is checked (L222); no memory-safety or authorization failure is confirmable in-fragment.

verdict.summary: Off-by-one stack out-of-bounds write in gopherToHTML: the clamp at lines 77-79 and the leftover-accumulation at line 94 let llen reach TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1, and line 99 writes '\0' at line[TEMP_BUF_SIZE], one byte past the TEMP_BUF_SIZE-sized LOCAL_ARRAY 'line' declared at line 6.
