The guard at line 77 clamps llen to TEMP_BUF_SIZE - gopherState->len - 1 (line 79), but line 94 then executes llen += gopherState->len, producing exactly llen == TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1; guard 77 tests the pre-increment value, so it fails the Guard-Identity Audit by transformation drift and never excludes llen == TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1 at the sink. line's capacity TEMP_BUF_SIZE is declared at line 6 (valid indices 0..TEMP_BUF_SIZE-1), so the write at index TEMP_BUF_SIZE is one byte past the end (CWE-787, stack OOB write). TEMP_BUF_SIZE likewise bounds tmpbuf (line 7); snprintf calls into tmpbuf are length-capped by the n argument.

inbuf/len are treated as entry-point data (gopher reply contents) with no shown size cap besides the loop guard at line 67.
limitations: The capacity of gopherState->buf is not declared in the fragment, so memcpy at line 86 into gopherState->buf + gopherState->len cannot be independently confirmed; it is bounded to len + llen <= TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1 only under the unshown buf-capacity invariant.
The CSO branch (strtok/atoi on line) has no shown memory-safety sink; html_quote/rfc1738_escape outputs are consumed by bounded snprintf into tmpbuf.
No caller of gopherToHTML is shown; the fragment itself demonstrates an admitted llen == TEMP_BUF_SIZE - 1 reaching the terminator write, so no caller invariant is needed for the verdict.

verdict.summary: TfLiteIntArrayGetSizeInBytes computes sizeof(dummy) + sizeof(dummy.data[0]) * size with no check on the int parameter size. Any size >= 536870911 (4-byte int) or any negative size makes the sum exceed the int capacity of computed_size; the assignment wraps (size=INT_MAX yields 0, size=-1 yields 0 via unsigned wraparound), so the returned byte size under-sizes the storage a caller allocates for size elements and enables heap overflow when data[] is filled. The MSVC-only subtraction is compile-time, post-wrap, and never bounds size.

evidence.reason: size is int with unconstrained domain INT_MIN..INT_MAX (no guard before this statement). The product is computed in size_t (negative size becomes huge unsigned), then the sum is assigned to int computed_size: with size=INT_MAX, 4 + 4*2147483647 = 8589934592 which exceeds the int capacity INT_MAX and wraps to 0; with size=-1 the unsigned arithmetic wraps to 0. The value returned at line 9 is therefore a truncated/zero byte size, under-sizing any allocation sized from it and allowing OOB writes into data[size]. The only conditional (#if defined(_MSC_VER), lines 5-8) subtracts one element after the wrap and constrains the derived result, not size - wrong-target/transformation drift; it protects nothing. Absent fix: a bound check before line 4 rejecting size < 0 or size > (INT_MAX - (int)sizeof(dummy)) / (int)sizeof(dummy.data[0]). Primary mechanism CWE-190 integer overflow in the size calculation.

assumptions: TfLiteIntArray is laid out as { int size; int data[]; }, so sizeof(dummy) is 4 and sizeof(dummy.data[0]) is 4 with int as 32-bit two's complement (INT_MAX = 2147483647); boundary size = (2147483647 - 4) / 4 = 536870910, so the failure set starts at size = 536870911.
The function's evident contract is to return the byte size of a TfLiteIntArray holding size elements, so a wrapped return value would under-size a caller's allocation for data[size].
limitations: No call site is shown, so the downstream malloc/fill (e.g., TfLiteIntArrayCreate writing data[]) is not confirmed in-fragment; the demonstrated failure is the integer wraparound of the size computation and the return of a corrupted byte size.

Truncation of an out-of-range value to int is implementation-defined, but GCC/Clang/MSVC wrap modulo 2^32 in practice, and the negative-size path already yields a well-defined unsigned wraparound to 0.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the patched form of ImmutableExecutorState::Initialize. Absent fix: cap decode.channels or compute the product in int64 before the call. CWE-787 with CWE-190 as root cause.

assumptions: decode.width/decode.height/decode.channels are 32-bit fields; decode.channels participates in the shown int32 arithmetic.

verdict.summary: The SSL_connect status check at line 101 uses `rc < 0`, which admits the documented failure value rc==0 (handshake shut down / not successful) onto the success path, so the function sets isssl=true and returns 0 with no TLS session established (fail-open CWE-754). Independently, the CTX is never given an explicit verify mode, so OpenSSL's default SSL_VERIFY_NONE leaves the peer certificate unvalidated when the handshake succeeds (CWE-295).

evidence.reason: rc comes from SSL_connect at line 100; with the blocking socket mode the fragment itself documents (BIO_set_nbio commented out at lines 97-98), OpenSSL returns 1 on success, 0 when the handshake failed via controlled shutdown, and <0 on fatal error. The guard at line 101 admits rc==0 (its admitted set on the success path is {0, 1}) so the failure value 0 falls through to `isssl = true; return 0;` at lines 115-117, failing open on TLS establishment. The absent one-statement fix is `if (rc != 1)` (or `rc <= 0`), which would exclude the entire failure set {0}; an attacker-controlled server that closes the connection mid-handshake drives rc==0. Guard-identity audit passes (no intervening assignment between line 100 and the use at line 115), so the predicate is insufficient, not drifted. Primary CWE-754 (improper exceptional-condition check / fail-open).

The SSL_CTX created at line 11 (TLS_client_method) is used with no call to SSL_CTX_set_verify anywhere in the fragment, leaving OpenSSL's default SSL_VERIFY_NONE; the CA loading at lines 31-32 and 42 and the TRUSTED_FIRST flag at line 66 only configure the trust store without enabling peer verification. Consequently the handshake at line 100 completes (rc==1) with any attacker-supplied certificate and the fragment marks the connection secure (isssl=true, return 0 at lines 115-117), giving a MITM-capable authentication bypass. The absent one-statement fix is `SSL_CTX_set_verify(ctx, SSL_VERIFY_PEER, NULL)` (plus a verify-result check before returning success). Secondary CWE-295.

assumptions: Blocking socket mode: the BIO_set_nbio calls at lines 97-98 are commented out, so SSL_connect does not return WANT_* pseudo-failures.
OpenSSL documented semantics: SSL_connect returns 1 on success, 0 on failed/closed handshake, <0 on fatal error; SSL_CTX_new without SSL_CTX_set_verify defaults to SSL_VERIFY_NONE.
log_ssl_errors is a printf-style logger and every call uses a literal format with matching %s arguments, so no format-string injection occurs.

The rogue-server requirement of CWE-295 assumes the caller connects to an attacker-influenced endpoint; the in-fragment proof that no verify mode is set is the absence of SSL_CTX_set_verify / SSL_set_verify combined with the default SSL_VERIFY_NONE.

Hostname/certificate_path content is only used as %s log arguments and as a CA-directory input; no injection sink (shell, format, SQL, header) consumes either value, and no length-derived capacity exists in the fragment, so no OOB candidate is derivable.

all_nodes_[apply_gradient_node_name] (lines 62-63) cannot default-insert nullptr because every apply-gradient node name is inserted at lines 39-43 in the same loop.
gradient_pos (lines 50-60) contains an entry for every op in apply_gradients_ops (lines 27-37), so the map lookups at lines 67/70 never default-insert.
limitations: Lines 67/70: apply_gradients_node->input()/mutable_input() indexed by gradient_pos[op] (fixed values 2..9) could exceed the node's actual input count, but the fragment never declares or computes input_size() or any other capacity for that repeated field, so the OOB class confirmation (capacity visible in fragment) fails; recorded as a hardening concern only.

Lines 24/97 (var->name()), 48-49 (div_const_node->name()), and 81 (IsDequeueOp(*train_node)): potential null derefs would require callers or helpers to place NULL entries in item.MainVariables(), AddNodeDivConst output, or ComputeTransitiveFanin output; no NULL producer is shown in the fragment, so not confirmable.
A malicious graph could influence node names, ops, and input lists, but no in-fragment constraint violation with a named capacity was demonstrable.

verdict.summary: In php_wddx_pop_element, the EL_BINARY branch stores the result of php_base64_decode into ent1->data via ZVAL_STR without a NULL check. Malformed base64 content in a <binary> element (e.g. "A=") makes php_base64_decode return NULL, so ent1->data becomes an IS_STRING zval whose zend_string pointer is NULL; that zval is then consumed by zend_hash_next_index_insert (line 110) or zend_symtable_str_update (line 106), whose refcount handling dereferences NULL and crashes the process. The fix present in later upstream versions (if (new_str) { ZVAL_STR(...); } else { ZVAL_EMPTY_STRING(...); }) is absent.

evidence.reason: The EL_BINARY branch (line 32) decodes attacker-controlled base64 text from ent1->data at lines 33-34 via php_base64_decode, whose standard PHP-7 semantics include a NULL failure set (verified: malformed padding such as "A=" returns NULL). No protective NULL check on new_str appears between line 33 and this line 36 store, so the NULL result is installed as an IS_STRING zval with value.str == NULL; the admitted failing value is the decode result of any invalid <binary> payload (e.g. <binary>A=</binary>). The absent fix is: if (new_str) { ZVAL_STR(&ent1->data, new_str); } else { ZVAL_EMPTY_STRING(&ent1->data); }. Downstream refcount dereference of the NULL string pointer (lines 106/110/57) yields CWE-476.

For <array><binary>INVALID</binary></array>, after the unguarded line 36 stores the NULL-str zval into ent1->data, ent2 is the array (line 62, HASH_OF at line 63), ent1->varname is NULL (line 65 false), so this line inserts the IS_STRING zval whose value.str == NULL; zend_hash_next_index_insert refcount-addrefs the string pointer, dereferencing NULL and crashing. The store at line 36 is the only guard point that could exclude this, and that check is absent; primary CWE-476 (NULL-pointer dereference), reachable purely from the fragment's binary-decode path.

assumptions: php_base64_decode returning NULL on malformed base64 is standard PHP-7 API semantics (confirmed in ext/standard/base64.c, e.g. pad encountered at i%%4==1 with witness input "A=").
Inserting or destroying an IS_STRING zval dereferences the zend_string pointer (refcount addref/release) under standard Zend semantics.

<binary> element character data is accumulated into ent1->data as a string by the WDDX character-data handler (php_wddx_process_data, not shown), so Z_STRVAL/Z_STRLEN at lines 33-34 read the attacker-supplied text.

stack->top is non-negative under the WDDX stack discipline (wddx_stack_init sets 0; all in-fragment decrements at lines 24, 52, 124 are guarded), making the line 11 `top == 0` guard sufficient for the wddx_stack_top calls.
limitations: A negative stack->top, which the `== 0` guard (line 11) would admit (a `<= 0` fix would exclude it), is not derivable from the shown fragment, so that separate underflow hypothesis is not confirmed.

NUL-termination of ent1->varname consumed by strlen at line 106, and the element-type invariants of pushed entries, depend on unshown producers and are not independently confirmable from the fragment.
Object-injection behavior via __wakeup (line 45) and class-table lookup hardening (lines 73-75) are intended deserialization semantics, not part of this finding.

verdict.summary: All dangerous operations are protected: base64 output is capped by the explicit outSize argument 2000 into buf64[5000], the terminator writes buf64[size64]=0 use size64 in [0,2000], the sdpLine sprintf consumes at most ~2052 bytes of a 5100-byte buffer, and strcpy targets are allocated exactly strlen(sdpLine)+1. No unconstrained value reaches a memory-safety sink.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement: the explicit outSize argument 2000 caps gf_base64_encode output under standard outSize semantics, so the residual range of its return value is [0,2000]. This bounds the L81 terminator write buf64[size64]=0 to indices well inside buf64[5000] (declared L9) — the excluded set is every index >= 5000 — and bounds the L82 %s read of buf64 (<=2037 bytes) inside sdpLine[5100] (L9).

Same outSize cap 2000 for the scene-sample base64 encode; size64 is confined to [0,2000], so the L118 terminator write and the L119 sprintf %s read stay within buf64[5000]/sdpLine[5100] (L9). No admitted index exceeds 2000, excluding any OOB write/read.

The serialized-IOD encode is also capped at 2000 bytes (largest potential input in the fragment), so size64 in [0,2000]; the L172 terminator write and L175 sprintf into sdpLine (prefix 51 + 2000 + 1 = 2052 < 5100, L9) cannot overflow. This is the least-protected of the three encode paths and is still fully bounded.

Copy target esd->URLString is allocated exactly as sizeof(char) * size64 with size64 = strlen(sdpLine)+1 (L89-90), so the strcpy failure set (source longer than target) is excluded by construction; sdpLine is always NUL-terminated by the L82 sprintf.
Same exact-size protection: allocation is sizeof(char) * (strlen(sdpLine)+1) at L126, fully excluding an out-of-bounds copy for the scene branch.
NULL deref protection for all later iod dereferences (L57/L102/L137/L167-168): gf_isom_get_root_od return is checked before any use, excluding NULL on every reaching path.

assumptions: gf_base64_encode(in, inSize, out, outSize) follows the standard outSize-cap semantics implied by its named size parameter at L80/L117/L171, returning bytes written <= 2000 (analogous to pstrcpy capping at its named size).
buf64 and sdpLine capacities are 5000 and 5100 bytes per L9; all computed worst-case rendered lengths (<=2052) stay below these.
gf_isom_get_esd succeeds for tracks already enumerated by gf_isom_get_track_count/media-type checks; sceneT >= 1 is enforced at L47 before its esd is used.
limitations: esd at L66/L105 is dereferenced at L98-99/L134-135 without a NULL check, but the fragment shows no producer that can make it NULL (track existence and sceneT>=1 are enforced), so a NULL-deref finding is unconfirmable and was not elevated.
Whether gf_isom_get_esd returns fresh copies vs shared pointers (which could make the L154 del and L168 iod del a double-free) is not derivable from the shown fragment.
gf_odf_desc_write's return status at L167 is discarded; no memory-safety consequence is derivable from the fragment if it fails.
L15's %d with a u32 argument is technically a format mismatch but cannot overflow buf64 (max ~11 characters), so it is a hardening note at most.

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds read of flat_segment_id in the join loop: the inner loop at line 56 admits i in [0, relative_offset_set.size()) and reads flat_segment_id(i) at line 57, while the segment_id tensor's capacity is flat_segment_id.size() (line 37) and no shown statement relates relative_offset_set.size() to it. The value-range check at lines 40-47 guards a different index range and cannot protect this read.

evidence.reason: The index i is admitted by the loop bound relative_offset_set.size() (line 56), a helper-returned size with no in-fragment constraint, while the read target's capacity is flat_segment_id.size() (the flat view of segment_id created at line 37 and used to bound the validation loop at line 40). The guard at lines 40-47 only validates values for i < flat_segment_id.size() and does not constrain the sink loop's index, so any i in [flat_segment_id.size(), relative_offset_set.size()) performs an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The absent fix is a loop bound of flat_segment_id.size() or an explicit equality/size check on relative_offset_set before the sink loop.

assumptions: flat_segment_id.size() equals segment_id.num_elements() and is the in-bounds index capacity of the flat segment_id view consumed at line 57.
The value-range validation at lines 40-47 applies only to indices below flat_segment_id.size() and constrains values only, not the sink loop's index range.
limitations: The size of relative_offset_set and the stride values come from unshown helpers GetStrides/GetFlattenedRelativeOffsets; the verdict does not assume their exact semantics, only that the fragment shows no constraint relating relative_offset_set.size() to flat_segment_id.size().

Bounds of output_flat(output_index) at lines 57-61 and of flat_input(offset) at line 61 depend on unshown GetOutputShape/GetStrides semantics, so those writes/reads are not independently confirmed and are not used for the verdict.

verdict.summary: FractionalAvgPoolGrad backpropagation writes through an index built from unvalidated row_seq/col_seq values. A negative sequence entry (e.g. -1) is admitted by the count guards and end-clamps, making the in_r/in_c loops start below zero so in_index becomes negative and coeffRef performs an out-of-bounds heap write.

evidence.reason: in_index (L103) = (b*in_rows + in_r)*in_cols + in_c derives from attacker-controlled row_seq_tensor_flat(r) (L86) and col_seq_tensor_flat(c) (L91), whose values are never validated: guards at L38/L44 bound only the tensors' element counts, and the clamps at L89/L94 bound only the loop ends. A witness with row_seq=[-1,0], col_seq=[0,1], in_rows=in_cols=100, out_backprop=[1,1,1,1] passes L38/L44 (2>1) and yields in_row_start=-1, in_row_end=0, so loop L101 starts at in_r=-1 giving in_index=(0*100-1)*100+0=-100, outside the matrix capacity in_cols*in_rows*in_batch=10000 (L74-76). coeffRef at L109 then writes before the allocated buffer (CWE-787 heap OOB write). Absent fix: clamp/validate in_row_start and in_col_start to [0, in_rows-1]/[0, in_cols-1] before use, or reject negative/oversized sequence entries.

assumptions: Eigen Matrix::coeffRef uses linear (column-major) indexing into the mapped data pointer, so a negative in_index addresses memory before the buffer (L74-76 capacity).
OP_REQUIRES/OP_REQUIRES_OK abort and return on failure; passing the checks in the shown fragment is sufficient to reach the write sink.
Tensor inputs (out_backprop, row_seq_tensor, col_seq_tensor, orig_input_tensor_shape) are externally supplied via context->input, i.e., entry-point data.
limitations: Division by zero at L110-111 requires an int64 wrap of an unbounded start/end range (e.g. INT64_MIN..INT64_MAX); in that regime the coeffRef access already faults first, so CWE-369 is not independently confirmed.

Negative values in orig_input_tensor_shape passed to in_shape.AddDim (L64) would trip TensorShape dimension checks before the write sink; this is a separate CHECK-failure/DoS concern, not the confirmed write.

If the caller only ever supplied well-formed pooling sequences generated by FractionalAvgPool forward, the negative-start path would not fire, but no such invariant is visible in the fragment, and the op accepts attacker-supplied tensors.

verdict.summary: In ReadOneMNGImage, the DEFI chunk handler derives object_id from two attacker-controlled bytes (line 375) and guards it with `if (object_id > MNG_MAX_OBJECTS)` (line 382), clamping larger values to `object_id=MNG_MAX_OBJECTS` (line 390). The operator is off by one: object_id == MNG_MAX_OBJECTS passes unmodified, and every larger value is clamped to that same out-of-range index. The fragment's own conventions fix the valid index domain to [0, MNG_MAX_OBJECTS): initialization loops (lines 114-118, 326-327) write indices 0..MNG_MAX_OBJECTS-1 and the CLIP/MOVE guards (lines 813, 895) skip i >= MNG_MAX_OBJECTS. The admitted value reaches OOB member accesses such as `mng_info->exists[object_id]=MagickTrue;` (line 404) and reads at lines 393-394 — a heap out-of-bounds write/read (CWE-787). The absent fix is `object_id >= MNG_MAX_OBJECTS` with clamp `object_id=MNG_MAX_OBJECTS-1`.

evidence.reason: Sink: write to mng_info->exists[object_id]. object_id derives from entry-controlled chunk bytes at line 375 (16-bit, [0,65535]). The only guard, `if (object_id > MNG_MAX_OBJECTS)` (line 382), admits object_id == MNG_MAX_OBJECTS unchanged and clamps every larger value to MNG_MAX_OBJECTS at line 390, so the residual range at the sink is [0, MNG_MAX_OBJECTS] with MNG_MAX_OBJECTS included. The fragment fixes the valid index domain to [0, MNG_MAX_OBJECTS): loops at lines 114-118 and 326-327 write object_clip[0..MNG_MAX_OBJECTS-1], and guards at lines 813 and 895 treat i >= MNG_MAX_OBJECTS as invalid. Witness: a DEFI chunk with 16-bit value MNG_MAX_OBJECTS (e.g., bytes 0x01,0x00 for 256), length >= 2, passes line 368 and line 382 and reaches line 404 as index MNG_MAX_OBJECTS — one past the declared capacity — a heap OOB write (CWE-787). Guard-Identity Audit: same value, no modification between line 390 and the sink, so identity passes but coverage fails; absent fix is `object_id >= MNG_MAX_OBJECTS` with clamp `object_id=MNG_MAX_OBJECTS-1`.

Sink: OOB reads of mng_info->exists[object_id] and mng_info->frozen[object_id] on the same path as the line-404 write, sharing the same admitted object_id == MNG_MAX_OBJECTS produced by guard line 382 (`>`) and clamp line 390. Valid domain is [0, MNG_MAX_OBJECTS) per init loops (lines 114-118, 326-327) and exclusion guards (lines 813, 895); index MNG_MAX_OBJECTS is one past the arrays, causing an OOB read (CWE-125, secondary to the same root cause as the CWE-787 write). Same absent fix as the write sink; both resolved ABSENT.

assumptions: MNG_MAX_OBJECTS equals the element count of the exists/frozen/invisible/x_off/y_off/object_clip arrays (valid indices [0, MNG_MAX_OBJECTS)); shown by in-fragment init loops (lines 114-118, 326-327) and CLIP/MOVE exclusion guards (lines 813, 895).
MNG_MAX_OBJECTS lies within the 16-bit object-id domain so object_id == MNG_MAX_OBJECTS is constructible from the two chunk bytes at line 375 (upstream value 256 = 0x0100).

Standard semantics: AcquireQuantumMemory returns NULL and is checked (line 188); ReadBlob/ReadBlobByte may short-read, leaving the tail of the length+MagickPathExtent allocation uninitialized but in bounds.
limitations: The MngInfo structure definition is not shown, so sizes of loop_active/loop_jump/loop_count/loop_iteration are unknown; un-guarded loop_level indexing in LOOP/ENDL (lines 926, 973, 1007) is not confirmable as OOB.

MNG_LOOSE-only global_plte/global_trns paths (lines 499-518, 534-541) can dereference unchecked state, but depend on MNG_LOOSE being defined and on unshown allocation results; robustness-only, not the decisive finding.

Pointer advances past chunk[length] in FRAM/TERM/BASI/MAGN (e.g., lines 651-668, 713, 431) remain inside the length+MagickPathExtent allocation (lines 185-186) and only touch uninitialized bytes, so they are not boundary violations of the shown allocation.
Warnings emitted by the line-382/388 guard do not prevent the failure: values > MNG_MAX_OBJECTS are still clamped to the same OOB index before the sink.

verdict.summary: Decrypt path computes ilen = aes->src_len - authsize with no src_len >= authsize check; unsigned underflow (e.g., src_len=0, authsize=16) yields 0xFFFFFFF0, admitted by the ilen > 0 guard and consumed by scatterwalk_ffwd, ccp_init_data, and the GCTR block loop, causing an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). Independently, aes->iv_len is used unvalidated at L103 to derive the ctx DMA offset, underflowing for iv_len > CCP_AES_CTX_SB_COUNT*CCP_SB_BYTES and producing an out-of-bounds write at L104/L197 (CWE-787).

evidence.reason: On the decrypt branch, L61 computes `ilen = aes->src_len - authsize` with unsigned arithmetic and no check that `aes->src_len >= authsize` (authsize is restricted to {16,15,14,13,12,8,4} by the L34-45 switch, so the failure set is src_len in [0, authsize-1]). aes->src_len is an unconstrained u32 entry-point value — the fragment's own comment at L50-51 contemplates zero input lengths — so the degenerate witness src_len=0, authsize=16 yields ilen=0xFFFFFFF0. The only guard on the path, L144 `if (ilen > 0)`, admits that value; scatterwalk_ffwd then walks the source SG with a ~4 GiB offset, and the L167 `while (src.sg_wa.bytes_left)` loop (bytes_left = ilen from L148) reads AES_BLOCK_SIZE per iteration from an SG the fragment sizes at src_len bytes — out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). Absent fix: `if (aes->src_len < authsize) return -EINVAL;` before L62.

L103 computes `dm_offset = CCP_AES_CTX_SB_COUNT * CCP_SB_BYTES - aes->iv_len` with unsigned arithmetic and no validation of aes->iv_len (an unconstrained u32 entry-point value; only `if (!aes->iv)` at L21 is checked). The ctx workarea is allocated at L97-99 with the same `CCP_AES_CTX_SB_COUNT * CCP_SB_BYTES` capacity, so for witness iv_len = capacity+1 the subtraction underflows: dm_offset = 0xFFFFFFFF, and this ccp_set_dm_area copies iv_len bytes starting one byte before the ctx buffer — out-of-bounds write past the declared capacity (CWE-787), repeated at L197. Absent fix: `if (aes->iv_len > CCP_AES_CTX_SB_COUNT * CCP_SB_BYTES) return -EINVAL;` before L103.

assumptions: authsize is confined to {16,15,14,13,12,8,4} by the L34-45 switch, and aes->key_len to {16,24,32} by L24-26.
aes->iv and aes->key are non-NULL (L21, L29); aes->src_len and aes->iv_len have no shown bound.
ctx capacity is the expression CCP_AES_CTX_SB_COUNT * CCP_SB_BYTES used both in the L97-99 allocation and the L103 offset arithmetic.
scatterwalk_ffwd, ccp_init_data, ccp_set_dm_area, and the block loop process exactly the supplied offset/length under standard scatterlist/DMA semantics.
Unsigned subtraction wraps modulo 2^32 per C semantics.
limitations: Oversized aes->aad_len on the GHASH path (L118/L127) reads past the SG but no in-fragment capacity is declared to prove the out-of-range extent, so it is demoted.
Encrypt-path src_len exceeding the caller's SG extent has no in-fragment capacity to compare against.
The numeric value of CCP_AES_CTX_SB_COUNT * CCP_SB_BYTES is not shown; the iv_len boundary is expressed symbolically.
The write-side extent of p_outp/p_inp SGs is caller-provided; the read-side confirmation does not depend on it.
Caller-level invariants (e.g., a higher crypto layer requiring src_len >= authsize) are not visible in the fragment and were not assumed.

verdict.summary: When batched_input_ is true and the rt_nested_splits input list is empty, nested_splits_ holds zero elements, yet batched_ragged_input.splits(0) indexes nested_splits_[0], an unchecked std::vector operator[] access, producing a heap out-of-bounds read. The fragment never requires ragged_nested_splits_len > 0 before this access; the num_components >= 0 check runs after it and constrains a different value (size()-1), so it cannot protect the sink.

evidence.reason: splits(int) is nested_splits_[index] (unchecked operator[]), so splits(0) writes nothing but reads element 0 of nested_splits_, whose capacity is ragged_nested_splits_len (loop at lines 12-14 appends exactly that many elements; reserve at line 10 changes capacity, not size). ragged_nested_splits_len is entry-point derived (lines 3-7, OpInputList::size()) with no shown minimum, so len==0 is admitted, leaving nested_splits_ empty (loop condition 0 < 0 is false at i=0). The only guard near the sink, OP_REQUIRES(num_components >= 0) at lines 26-28, executes after line 23 and checks batched_splits_top_vec.size()-1, not the existence of element 0 (check-after-use and wrong-target drift), so the crashing path never passes through it and it cannot prevent the OOB. Absent fix: OP_REQUIRES(context, ragged_nested_splits_len > 0, ...) placed before the access. Confirmed heap out-of-bounds read: CWE-125.

assumptions: RaggedTensorVariant::splits(i) returns nested_splits_[i] via unchecked std::vector::operator[], so indexing element 0 of a zero-element vector is out of bounds (verified against ragged_tensor_variant.h at the matching revision).
OpInputList::size() returns a non-negative int; residual range of ragged_nested_splits_len is [0, input-count] with no shown lower bound.
batched_input_ is a boolean op attribute; line 16's branch shows both false and true paths exist.
limitations: Whether the op registration rejects an empty rt_nested_splits list at graph-build time is not visible in the fragment; the fragment itself imposes no minimum, and the historical fix commit be7a4de6 (added OP_REQUIRES(ragged_nested_splits_len > 0)) confirms the empty-list path was reachable at runtime.

The num_components >= 0 block (lines 24-28) resolves a different, earlier issue (invalid resize, commit b055b9c4) and is not a substitute fix for the splits(0) sink; it is not re-flagged as a separate finding because its output is unused.

No injection, crypto, or injection-type sinks exist in this fragment; severity is capped at medium because the confirmed mechanism is a localized out-of-bounds read rather than a write or code execution.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation is protected by a verbatim guard: N_big is capped to Index::max before the lossless cast (lines 21-26), the N > 0 guard excludes N == 0 before num_updates / N (lines 41, 63), rank/prefix consistency (lines 9-11, 57-62) makes the division exact, and the bad_i < 0 checks after each functor (lines 50, 68) ensure all indices were validated before indices_flat(bad_i) is read. No unconstrained entry-point value reaches an unprotected dangerous operation.

evidence.snippet:
OP_REQUIRES(
        c, N_big <= std::numeric_limits<Index>::max(),
        errors::InvalidArgument("indices has too many elements for ",
                                DataTypeString(DataTypeToEnum<Index>::v()),
                                " indexing: ", N_big, " > ",
                                std::numeric_limits<Index>::max()));
evidence.reason: Excludes N_big > Index::max, so static_cast<Index>(N_big) at line 27 is lossless and N is in [0, Index::max]; guard-identity audit passes because the same value is checked with no intervening mutation before the cast.

Excludes N == 0 from both functor paths and from num_updates / N at line 63, preventing division-by-zero and empty-range functor runs; combined with lines 21-26, N is in [1, Index::max] inside the block. This is the decisive guard for the division sink.

evidence.snippet:
OP_REQUIRES(c, bad_i < 0,
                    errors::InvalidArgument(
                        "indices", SliceDebugString(indices.shape(), bad_i),
                        " = ", indices_flat(bad_i), " is not in [0, ",
                        params->dim_size(0), "));
evidence.reason: Admits only bad_i == -1 (all indices in [0, params->dim_size(0)) under the standard functor contract) and is evaluated after the functor returns (lines 48-49) with no intervening mutation; when it fails, indices_flat(bad_i) at line 53 is indexed with bad_i in [0, N), in bounds. The identical guard covers the non-scalar path at lines 68-72.

evidence.snippet:
OP_REQUIRES(
            c, TensorShapeUtils::StartsWith(updates.shape(), indices.shape()),
            errors::InvalidArgument(
                "The shape of indices (", indices.shape().DebugString(),
                ") must be a prefix of the shape of updates (",
                updates.shape().DebugString(), "));
evidence.reason: With the rank check (lines 9-11), the prefix constraint forces updates.NumElements() = N * product(trailing dims), so num_updates / N at line 63 is integral and the updates_flat shaped view is exact (no truncation or element-count mismatch), with N > 0 guaranteed by line 41.

assumptions: indices.NumElements() and updates.NumElements() are non-negative int64 per Tensor semantics.
ScatterScalarFunctor/ScatterFunctor follow the standard contract: validate each Index against the params outer dimension before writing and return -1 or the first invalid position in [0, N).
The rank check (lines 9-11) combined with StartsWith (lines 57-62) implies updates.NumElements() = N * product(trailing dims), making num_updates / N exact.
limitations: Rank-0 params: the rank check admits params->dims() == 0 (e.g., scalar updates with rank>=1 indices and N > 0), under which params->dim_size(0) at lines 29/32/54/72 reads the dim slot of a 0-dim shape. TensorShape storage is not shown; the read stays inside the tensor object (uninitialized-value read, no demonstrated corruption), so it is kept as a hardening concern and not counted in the verdict.
Per-element validation of indices occurs inside the not-shown functor bodies; the analysis relies on the standard functor contract.
No constraints from kernel registration or shape functions outside the fragment were used.

verdict.summary: The only length check guards `length < sizeof(bh)`, but `bh` is a pointer, so the check admits buffers as small as 4/8 bytes; subsequent struct dereferences (`bh->totlen`, `bh->min_version`, `bh->hdrsize`, `bh->version`, `bh->flags`) over-read an undersized buffer before the correct `sizeof(blobheader)` check at line 33 runs.

evidence.reason: `length` is input-derived with residual range [sizeof(bh), UINT32_MAX] after the line 8 guard, where `sizeof(bh)` is the pointer size (4/8 bytes), not `sizeof(blobheader)`. A witness `length = sizeof(bh)` passes line 8 yet `bh->totlen` (and the later `bh->min_version`, `bh->hdrsize`, `bh->version`, `bh->flags`) reads fields beyond the supplied buffer — CWE-125 OOB read. Guard-Identity Audit class (2) drift: the guard bounds against pointer size while the sink consumes a `blobheader`; the absent fix is `if (length < sizeof(blobheader))` (or `sizeof(*bh)`) at line 8, and the line 33 `hdrsize != sizeof(blobheader)` check runs after the over-read.

Same insufficient guard as the line 15 sink: `length` in [sizeof(bh), sizeof(blobheader)-1] is admitted at line 8, so reading `bh->hdrsize` can exceed the buffer when `blobheader` is larger than a pointer; the correct structural bound `length < sizeof(blobheader)` is absent, making this second field read also an unconstrained CWE-125 over-read.

assumptions: `sizeof(bh)` on a pointer expression yields the pointer size (4 on ILP32, 8 on LP64) per C semantics; the fragment gives no other meaning.
`sizeof(blobheader) > sizeof(bh)` because the struct must contain at least the referenced fields `totlen` (4), `min_version` (1), `hdrsize` (2), `version` (1), `flags` (2), totaling ≥ 10 bytes.
`length` originates from externally supplied NVRAM blob data; no shown producer guarantees a larger minimum.
limitations: NULL `data` from an unshown caller is not analyzed (no NULL producer in the fragment).
Downstream use of `*dataoffset`/`*hdrflags`/`*hdrversion` is not shown, so only the in-fragment over-read is confirmed.
Exact `blobheader` layout/padding is not shown; the finding only requires the struct size to exceed a pointer size.

verdict.summary: njs_object_iterate_reverse lacks any bound on args->from/args->to in the string branches. verdict.summary: No dangerous operation in the fragment admits an unconstrained failing value. `value` reaching the reject sink at line 71 is initialized on every path (line 12 for the error-entry path, line 62 for the NJS_ERROR path), and the only array-indexed write at line 34 has an index (`ctx->index`) with no in-fragment derivation and no declared capacity, so no out-of-bounds or NULL failure is confirmable from the shown statements. evidence.reason: Sink consuming `value` on the `failed:` path. Residual range of `value` is fully constrained on both reaching paths: path A (line 13 -> goto failed at line 14) carries `value = njs_arg(args, nargs, 1)` from line 12 (`&args[1]` if nargs>=2, else the invalid-value sentinel under standard njs_arg semantics); path B (NJS_ERROR at line 57 -> goto failed at line 64) carries `value = &vm->retval` from line 62. `njs_is_memory_error` (line 58) excludes memory-error retval before line 62, and no statement between line 62 and line 71 mutates `value`, so the initialization is effective at the use (Guard-Identity Audit: no drift). Uninitialized-use failure set is empty; no CWE-457/other finding.

Least-protected memory operation: an 8-byte write into the active level array indexed by `ctx->index`. `ctx` is engine carry-in state from `vm->top_frame->function->context` (line 10); `ctx->index` is never derived, compared, or bounded anywhere in the fragment, and the capacity of the target local array (async->local assigned at line 27) is not declared or computed in the fragment. Under the CWE-787 confirmation rule requiring both a visible capacity and an in-fragment numeric derivation exceeding it, no valid out-of-bounds witness can be constructed; the candidate is demoted to notes.limitations and does not support a vulnerable verdict.

assumptions: njs_arg(args, nargs, 1) returns &args[1] when nargs > 1 and the engine's invalid-value sentinel otherwise (standard njs_arg bounds semantics, allowed under the 'standard semantics implied by call names' rule).
njs_is_error and njs_is_memory_error are pure predicates over njs_value_t, so line 13 and line 58 are evaluated before the subsequent uses of `value`.

limitations: Line 34 OOB write: failure set is real only if ctx->index can exceed the async local scope size, but neither the capacity nor any derivation of ctx->index is shown in the fragment; per the confirmation rule, this cannot be promoted to a confirmed CWE-787 finding and cannot be used to reach a vulnerable verdict.

NULL-deref candidates (`ctx->await` at line 17, `ctx->capability` at lines 49/71, `vm->top_frame` at line 10) have no NULL producer inside the fragment; NULL supplied by an unshown caller is an unconfirmable external condition.

Memory-error early return (lines 58-60) skips `njs_async_context_free`, leaking one async context per OOM only; not attacker-controllable unbounded exhaustion, so not a confirmed resource-exhaustion vulnerability.

Discarding the reject call's return status at line 71 is a robustness/status-handling concern; the path still returns NJS_ERROR, so it is fail-closed for the surrounding rejection logic and is not elevated to a finding.
When nargs <= 1, the reject call at line 71 receives the invalid-value sentinel; this is a semantic degradation, not a memory-safety flaw.

limitations: S4 `c->ci[1].stack[0] = value` (L57) is safe only if the suspended fiber's callinfo buffer keeps at least two frames; that layout invariant is not visible in the fragment, so no OOB write is confirmable from the shown code.

No if (new_str)/return-status check exists on any path to the deref (guard-insufficiency: line 67's IS_STRING type tag is a wrong-target check on the zval type, not the pointer). Reachable WDDX: <struct><var name="php_class_name"><binary>!</binary></var></struct>. Absent one-statement fix: NULL-checking new_str before ZVAL_STR or before the line 67 read. Capacity/producer line 33-36; primary CWE-476 NULL deref.

assumptions: Line 11 'stack->top == 0' guard guarantees the first wddx_stack_top call (line 20) returns a valid element; line 51 'stack->top > 1' guarantees ent2 is valid after decrement at line 52.

Standard php_base64_decode semantics: valid base64 alphabet only; invalid characters or length%4==1 yield NULL.
limitations: Storing a NULL-string zval via zend_hash_next_index_insert (line 110, varname==NULL path) or add_property_zval (line 102) may crash later inside hash/property teardown, but that teardown is outside the fragment and is not counted as an independent finding.
No loops, format strings, path/shell construction, or crypto sinks exist in the fragment; all other memory operations are guarded as inventoried in Phase 2/4.

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds read: num_bootstrap_methods is read via R_BIN_JAVA_USHORT at offset 6 without any check that sz >= 8; a short attribute (e.g., sz == 7) passes the only prior guard (attr != NULL) and reads bytes 6-7 past the end of buffer (CWE-125).

The only earlier guard, line 7 'if (attr)', constrains only attr non-NULL (wrong-target drift) and admits every failing value; the line 14 'if (offset >= sz)' guard executes after this read (check-after-use) and protects no path to this sink. Witness sz == 7 reaches buffer[6] and buffer[7], the latter out of bounds for a 7-byte region. Absent fix: a pre-read check such as 'if (offset + 2 > sz) ...' or 'if (sz < 8) ...'. Primary CWE-125 OOB read.

r_list_newf never returns NULL, so the line 20 append is not a NULL-deref candidate.
Line 6 'offset += 6;' implies r_bin_java_default_attr_new consumed the 6-byte attribute header, but that callee's internal validation is not visible here.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation with a failure set derivable from the fragment is fully guarded: i is range-checked to [0, patLen) at L15 before every pat->data[i][...] access; modulo by hilightA/hilightB is short-circuited by >0 checks (L22/L26/L37/L39/L48/L50); the volume divisor chanVolMax is clamped to >=1 (L70); the instrument index is bounded to [0, insLen) (L120); and volColor is clamped to [0,127] before indexing volColors (L159-160). Protects volColors[volColor] at L162: clamps the computed volume color to [0,127], excluding every out-of-range index that (pat->data[i][3]*127)/chanVolMax could produce.

e->song.ins has insLen entries, so the L120 guard's admitted set [0, insLen) matches the container capacity.

verdict.summary: The command-length argument parsed at line 48 (or the stored global at line 19) is an unconstrained uint; after the uint->int copy at line 66, lengths >= 0x80000000 become negative nbytes, and the clamp at line 71 only caps positive overflow, so a negative linebytes is passed as the read length to dm_i2c_read/i2c_read (lines 74/76) which fills the 16-byte stack buffer linebuf (line 68). The negative length, reinterpreted as a huge unsigned byte count by the read routine, causes an out-of-bounds stack write; the required protective statement (unsigned nbytes/linebytes or an explicit negative-length rejection) is absent.

evidence.reason: Sink writes linebytes bytes into linebuf[DISP_LINE_LEN] (capacity declared at line 68). linebytes derives from length (full uint, line 48/19) via nbytes = length (line 66, uint->int: values >= 0x80000000 become negative) and the clamp at line 71, whose admitted set is nbytes <= DISP_LINE_LEN and therefore includes every negative int; e.g. length=0x80000000 gives linebytes=INT_MIN, admitted by line 71 and reaching this sink unchanged. No guard excludes a negative length; the absent fix is the unsigned type for nbytes/linebytes (or an explicit nbytes<0 rejection). The negative value is reinterpreted as a huge unsigned byte count by the read routine, overflowing the 16-element stack buffer: CWE-787 with CWE-195 signed-to-unsigned size root.

evidence.snippet: ret = i2c_read(chip, addr, alen, linebuf, linebytes);
evidence.reason: Legacy-I2C counterpart of the same sink: linebytes is the same unconstrained residual range [-2^31, -1] U [0, DISP_LINE_LEN] admitted by the line-71 clamp, and a negative linebytes (e.g. length=0x80000000 -> INT_MIN at lines 66/71) is passed as the byte count for a read filling linebuf[DISP_LINE_LEN] (line 68), causing an out-of-bounds stack write when reinterpreted as unsigned: CWE-787 with CWE-195. The protective statement (unsigned nbytes/linebytes or negative-length check) is absent.

assumptions: linebuf at line 68 has exactly DISP_LINE_LEN elements (a small fixed compile-time constant); the clamp at line 71 uses that same constant, so positive linebytes can reach at most DISP_LINE_LEN bytes.

dm_i2c_read/i2c_read follow standard read semantics: they place len bytes into the caller's buffer, so a negative len is out-of-domain and, on conversion to a byte-count loop, becomes a huge unsigned count.
uint is 32-bit and the int conversion of values >= 0x80000000 yields a negative int (two's-complement), as the upstream fix confirms.
limitations: The exact driver behavior for a negative length is not shown in the fragment; the finding rests on the standard read-byte-count semantics and the confirmed out-of-domain argument, not on a shown driver loop.
alen on the repeat path (line 18) relies on the value previously validated by this function (lines 40-41); not treated as independently exploitable.
Large positive lengths (e.g. 0x80000000 with unsigned semantics) cause many iterations of the line-71-capped loop; this is bounded and was not flagged.

The upstream U-Boot fix changes the declaration to 'uint nbytes, linebytes;', corroborating that the fragment shown here (int nbytes, linebytes) is the vulnerable member; the verdict itself is derived from the shown statements.

verdict.summary: Every in-fragment dangerous read is fully constrained: the '*++sp' at lines 9 and 39 is reachable only from the '\\' and '^' outer cases, which exclude *sp==0, so it reads at most the in-bounds NUL (handled by 'case \0' lines 17-20 and 'else if (c == \0) len = 1' lines 42-43); the digit loop (lines 26-29) stops at the NUL; and all emitted values are bounded because c is unsigned char (0-255). No dangerous operation admits an unconstrained value.

The OOB failure set (sp[1] beyond the terminator) requires sp[0]==0 and is unreachable; guard identity holds with no assignment between line 8 and line 9. Fix PRESENT.

Read of sp[1] after a caret is reachable only from outer 'case ^' (line 37), whose admitted set is *sp == '^' (excluding 0); when '^' is the final character, sp[1] is the in-bounds terminator and 'else if (c == \0) { len = 1; }' (lines 42-43) corrects the consumed length so the value returned does not overstep the string. No shown statement mutates sp between line 37 and line 39, so guard identity holds; the OOB failure set is empty on every path. Fix PRESENT.

The digit loop's condition excludes every non-digit, including the string terminator ('\0' is not a digit), so it stops at the NUL and the maximal read index is the last digit; it never reads past the terminator and always terminates for a finite string. The post-increment at line 27 fires only after a digit was read. Fix PRESENT.

assumptions: sp points to a NUL-terminated string: the fragment itself dereferences sp and tests *sp against '\0' (lines 17, 33, 42, 50), so the NUL is an in-bounds, terminating byte.
c is unsigned char (line 4), so isgraph/isdigit receive values in 0..255 and the decimal expansion (c/100, c%10) at lines 58-62 is bounded to at most three digits.
save_string/save_char are buffer-managing appenders with standard NTB semantics; their exact capacity is not shown, so no overflow claim is made against them.
limitations: The returned len (line 65) is consumed only by unshown callers; any misuse there is not demonstrable within this fragment, and the NUL handling at lines 17-20 and 42-43 already keeps len correct for trailing '\\' and '^'.
sp == NULL or a non-NUL-terminated buffer supplied by an unshown caller cannot be derived from the fragment and is out of scope.
The internal capacity/bounds of dp managed by save_string/save_char are outside the fragment, so any failure there is unconfirmed.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the fixed variant: both pooling end indices are clamped to the input bounds (L-92, L-102), excluding the overlapping-mode one-past-the-end indices (h == input_size[1], w == input_size[2]) before they reach in_mat.col(in_offset); out_offset stays within the output column count via the sequence-bounded loops, and negative output sizes abort at the checked allocation. No dangerous operation admits an in-fragment-derivable failing value.

evidence.reason: in_mat.col(in_offset) read (L-108): in_offset = (b*input_size[1]+h)*input_size[2]+w (L-105-106) with b < input_size[0] (L-85), h <= height_end, and height_end clamped by L-92 std::min(height_end, height_max) to input_size[1]-1 (height_max at L-83), w <= width_end clamped by L-102 to input_size[2]-1. The overlapping_==true witness h == input_size[1], w == input_size[2] (last cum-seq window endpoint) is excluded by the clamps, which pass the Guard-Identity Audit (no assignment between clamp and use). Max admitted index = input_size[0]*input_size[1]*input_size[2]-1 = cols-1 for the map declared at L-57-58. Lower bound h,w >= 0 relies on standard GeneratePoolingSequence semantics (non-negative cumulative entries); a negative entry is not derivable from this fragment. Sink resolves PRESENT.

const int64_t out_offset =
              (b * output_size[1] + hs) * output_size[2] + ws;
evidence.reason: out_mat.col(out_offset) write (L-107): out_offset is bounded by hs < height_cum_seq.size()-1 (L-87) and ws < width_cum_seq.size()-1 (L-95); under standard GeneratePoolingSequence semantics each sequence has output_length+1 entries, so hs <= output_size[1]-1 and ws <= output_size[2]-1, and with b < input_size[0] (L-85) the max out_offset = output_size[0]*output_size[1]*output_size[2]-1 = cols-1 for the map declared at L-60-61. If any of output_size[0..2] is 0, the corresponding loop performs zero iterations. Sink resolves PRESENT; the sequence-length invariant is the relied-on assumption.

Decisive protective statement for the overlapping-mode OOB read: admitted set after this clamp is h <= input_size[1]-1, excluding the failure witness h == input_size[1] (and any larger cum-seq endpoint) that would otherwise place in_offset one full tensor row past the end of in_mat. Evaluated after the overlapping_ branch (L-90-91) and before the h loop (L-103); no intervening mutation of height_end or h; Guard-Identity Audit passes. Mirrored by the identical width clamp at L-102.

assumptions: GeneratePoolingSequence (L-32-35) follows its standard semantics: returns output_length+1 strictly increasing entries in [0, input_length] with the last entry equal to input_length.
tensor_in.dim_size(i) (L-16) is non-negative per TF tensor-shape contract, so input_size[i] >= 0 and floor division cannot be negative for positive pooling_ratio.
Eigen matrix maps (L-57-58, L-60-61) expose flat storage; a column index < row*col count is an in-bounds flat access.
DCHECK_GT (L-24) is compiled out in release builds, but a negative output_size causes allocate_output (L-39-43) to fail and OP_REQUIRES_OK to return before any pooling loop runs.

A negative height_start/width_start (cum-seq entry < 0) would make in_offset negative (OOB read before the buffer); this requires helper output contradicted by standard cum-seq semantics and is not derivable from the fragment.

input_size[i] = tensor_in.dim_size(i) narrowing int64 to int at L-16 could truncate dims above INT_MAX; such huge shapes are bounded by TF allocation/shape constraints outside the fragment, so oversized-dim truncation was not confirmed.
DCHECK_GT being debug-only is not itself the fix; its absence of runtime effect is neutralized by the checked allocation path for negative sizes and zero-iteration loops for zero sizes.

The loop at line 13 admits i = datalen-1 when datalen is odd; witness datalen=1, data[0]=GNUTLS_RENEGO_PROTECTION_REQUEST_MAJOR makes line 17 read data[1], one byte past the datalen-byte buffer. Guard line 77 (if (datalen % 2 != 0)) is evaluated after this use (Guard-Identity Audit class 1: check-after-use ordering drift) and protects only the later loops; the absent fix is a pre-loop parity/evenness check or a loop bound of i+1 < datalen. Mechanism: CWE-125 out-of-bounds read.

Same path as line 17: with odd datalen (witness datalen=1, data[0]=GNUTLS_FALLBACK_SCSV_MAJOR), the loop at line 13 reaches i = datalen-1 and line 30 reads data[i+1] = data[datalen], one byte past the end of data. The parity guard at line 77 runs after the loop and cannot constrain this access; absent fix is the parity/bound check placed before line 13. Mechanism: CWE-125 out-of-bounds read.

assumptions: `data` is a `datalen`-byte buffer whose valid indices are 0..datalen-1 (length contract implied by the parameter pair).
`datalen` and `data` contents are entry-point/attacker-controlled TLS ClientHello data (untrusted network input).
limitations: `server_find_pk_algos_in_ciphersuites(data, datalen, ...)` at lines 41-45 also runs before the line-77 parity check; any OOB inside that helper is not asserted because its body is not shown.
Indexing of `cipher_suites[i]`/memcpy sizes in later loops depends on helper-returned `cipher_suites_size`; that bound is not derivable in-fragment and is not asserted.
The later `data[j+1]`/`memcmp(&data[j],2)` uses (lines 93-97, 122-123) are fully protected by the line-77 parity check since `datalen` is even there; no finding is asserted for them.

verdict.summary: LZW-decoded pixel values (colour, 0..255) are used to index a colour table whose size is colour_table_size (2..256, computed at line 106) with no bounds check before the read at line 282, allowing an out-of-bounds read when colour >= colour_table_size; the clear-image path likewise indexes the table with an unvalidated background_index at line 311.

evidence.reason: colour is declared 'register unsigned char colour;' (line 16), giving it the full residual range 0..255; its only producer in the fragment is 'colour = *--stack_pos;' (line 278) from LZW-decompressed GIF data, and no shown statement constrains colour relative to colour_table_size. The colour table's capacity is colour_table_size = 2 << (flags & GIF_COLOUR_TABLE_SIZE_MASK) (line 106), i.e. 2..256 entries, and the local table is filled with exactly colour_table_size entries (loop at lines 123-140). Neighbouring guards do not protect the index: the burst clamp (lines 273-275) bounds the pixel count (wrong-target drift) and the transparency condition (lines 279-281) only decides whether to write. Witness admitted by every guard on the path: flags with GIF_COLOUR_TABLE_MASK set and low 3 bits 0 gives colour_table_size=2, and a pixel value colour=3 reads 4 bytes past the 2-entry table (up to colour values 255). The absent one-statement fix is a bound check such as 'if (colour < colour_table_size)' before the indexed read; hence CWE-125 out-of-bounds read.

In the clear-image branch (reachable via the disposal recursion gif_internal_decode_frame(gif, frame-1, true) at line 204 when frames[frame-1].disposal_method == GIF_FRAME_CLEAR), memset's fill value reads colour_table[gif->background_index]. background_index originates from the GIF header and has no shown constraint in the fragment, so its residual range is the full unsigned range, while the local-table capacity is colour_table_size (line 106) with the fill loop at lines 123-140. verdict.summary: handlerLWPolylineData writes vertices[4*vertexIndex+3] for groupCode==42 guarded only by vertexIndex<maxVertices; vertexIndex is -1 until a groupCode==10 arrives, so a DXF record with groupCode 42 before any 10 (or maxVertices==0) performs an out-of-bounds heap write at index -1; additionally 4*maxVertices overflows for maxVertices > INT_MAX/4.

evidence.reason: Sink writes at index 4*vertexIndex+3 (line 34). vertexIndex originates at -1 (line 17) and only increments on groupCode==10 (lines 25-26); groupCode and groupValue are entry-point DXF fields. The guard at line 33 admits vertexIndex=-1 for any maxVertices>=0 and lacks the required lower-bound term `vertexIndex>=0` (present for the sibling path at line 30). Witness: maxVertices=10, first vertex record is groupCode==42 -> vertexIndex=-1 -> -1<10 passes line 33 -> index 4*(-1)+3 = -1 written into the double array allocated with capacity 4*maxVertices at line 9: out-of-bounds write before the buffer (CWE-787). Absent fix: `vertexIndex>=0 &&` in the groupCode==42 guard.

Allocation size 4*maxVertices computed in signed int with only the maxVertices>0 check at line 5. maxVertices is toInt(groupValue) (line 4), fully attacker-controlled. For maxVertices=2^30 the product wraps to 0, producing an undersized/invalid allocation while the line-10 loop bound (i<maxVertices) and later writes require 4*maxVertices elements, enabling a large heap overrun; the missing protective statement is a size bound such as maxVertices<=SOMETHING before multiplying (CWE-190, secondary to CWE-787).

assumptions: toInt/toReal treat groupValue as a standard decimal integer/real parse of the DXF field.
vertices is a heap array of exactly 4*maxVertices doubles after line 9; capacity is visible at line 9.
vertexIndex is reset to -1 at line 17 on every group code 90, so -1 is reachable before any group code 10 increments it.
limitations: The line-9 integer overflow's exact runtime effect (uncaught bad_alloc vs undersized-allocation overflow) depends on the allocator's failure mode; the independent negative-index write at line 34 is fully confirmed without it.
A well-formed DXF emits 42 only after 10 per vertex, but the fragment imposes no ordering check, and an attacker-controlled file can emit 42 first; no external invariant was assumed.

verdict.summary: Attacker-controlled maxVertices (group code 90) is only checked with maxVertices>0 (line 5), so maxVertices up to INT_MAX reaches new double[4*maxVertices] (line 9). For maxVertices >= 2^30 the int multiplication 4*maxVertices wraps (e.g., to 0 at 2^30), yielding a near-zero-capacity heap allocation while the initialization loop (lines 10-14) writes indices up to 4*maxVertices-1, causing a heap buffer overflow write; the missing fix is an overflow cap on maxVertices or 64-bit/unsigned sizing before allocation.

evidence.reason: maxVertices originates from toInt(groupValue) (line 4) on entry-point DXF data and is constrained only by maxVertices>0 (line 5), leaving residual range 1..INT_MAX. The int expression 4*maxVertices overflows for maxVertices >= 2^30 (32-bit int), wrapping to 0 at exactly 2^30, so the allocation capacity no longer matches the 4*maxVertices slots the subsequent loop assumes. The guard at line 5 admits this witness and does not constrain the size quantity; the absent fix is an upper-bound check such as maxVertices <= INT_MAX/4 (or 64-bit/unsigned arithmetic) before the allocation. This is the root integer-overflow (CWE-190) that corrupts the heap size.

With the admitted witness maxVertices = 2^30, line 9 wraps 4*maxVertices to 0 so the heap object has (about) zero doubles, yet the loop at line 10 runs i from 0 to maxVertices-1 and line 14 writes index i*4+3, reaching up to 4*maxVertices-1 ≈ 2^32-1. That index exceeds the actual allocation capacity, a heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-122) reachable from unvalidated groupValue; the identical unprotected writes occur at lines 11-13. No overflow cap or size check exists anywhere in the shown fragment, so the failure set is fully admitted by the only guard (line 5).

assumptions: int is 32-bit, so INT_MAX is 2^31-1 and 4*maxVertices wraps for maxVertices >= 2^30 (common two's-complement behavior; signed overflow is UB in the standard).
toInt(groupValue) returns the full int value of the DXF field without clamping, since no clamp is shown.
new double[0] still returns a valid pointer per the standard, so the initialization loop proceeds and performs the out-of-bounds writes.
limitations: A NULL-dereference of vertices is not confirmed: the fragment contains no in-fragment producer of vertices==NULL on a path where the write guards (lines 30/33) pass.

The write branches at lines 31/34 are protected: lines 30 and 33 constrain vertexIndex to 0..maxVertices-1 at matching type/precision with no intervening mutation, so those index guards pass the Guard-Identity Audit.
If toInt were clamped to a small range or int were 64-bit, the overflow witness would not hold; neither is shown in the fragment.

verdict.summary: njs_await_fulfilled() stores the per-invocation PromiseCapability and async context in the awaited function object's shared fields (function->context / function->await, lines 42-43) with no guard. A nested/recursive activation of the same async function overwrites those fields and frees its own ctx, so the outer activation later dereferences a stale/freed ctx->capability at the resolve/reject njs_function_call (lines 58, 80) - use-after-free (fixed upstream in njs 0.7.2 by passing capability/ctx directly into njs_vmcode_interpreter).

evidence.reason: Per-invocation PromiseCapability/async-ctx records are written into the async function object's resident, reentrant fields at L42-43, taken from ctx->capability/ctx (L11) and function obtained from async->function (L22). Nothing shown binds them to the invocation or guards against overlapping activations of the same function; a nested recursive activation overwrites the same fields and frees its ctx via njs_async_context_free (L61/L83), so the outer activation's later njs_function(&ctx->capability->resolve) dereferences a freed/stale capability. Absent fix: replace L42-48 with per-invocation passing (njs_vmcode_interpreter(vm, ctx->pc, ctx->capability, ctx)) - CWE-416 use-after-free.

Confirmed sink: dereference of ctx->capability->resolve on the NJS_OK path following the unguarded shared-record store at L42-43; after a recursive activation of the same async function overwrites function->context/function->await and frees its own ctx, this dereference reads a freed/stale capability (likewise at L80 for reject). No guard on any path checks the record's validity, so the failure set is fully admitted - decisive for the VULNERABLE verdict.

assumptions: vm->top_frame->function->context (L11), ctx->await (L18), and async->function (L22) are non-NULL for a normal invocation; no NULL producer is shown in the fragment.
njs_async_context_free() frees both ctx->capability and ctx (shown at L61/L83 usage).
njs_function_call() invokes the capability's resolve/reject native function and dereferences it (standard semantics of the call names).
limitations: The exact scheduling that produces the overlapping activations (recursive async calls suspending at 'await') lives in the interpreter (njs_vmcode_interpreter, L45) outside the fragment; however, the shown store pattern at L42-43 is precisely the pattern the njs maintainers fixed as a use-after-free (commit 6a07c215, njs 0.7.2), so the mechanism is confirmed.
The NJS_ERROR memory-error path (L67-69) returns without calling njs_async_context_free(), a resource leak; noted, not a memory-corruption finding.
The top-path argument error check (L14-16) was assessed and does not protect the L58/L80 sink (wrong-target drift).

verdict.summary: Heap buffer overflow in raptor_xml_writer_start_element_common: nspace_declarations is allocated with only attribute_count+1 slots (plus declared_nspaces/xml_language) at line 15, but the attribute loop appends up to two struct nsd entries per attribute (namespace declaration + attribute). With one attribute whose namespace differs from the element's and both out of scope, entries land at indices 0, 1, and 2 while capacity is 2, writing the attribute entry past the array at line 70. A secondary out-of-bounds read occurs at line 52, where the dedup loop indexes element->attributes[j] with j up to nspace_declarations_count, which can exceed attribute_count.

evidence.reason: Heap OOB write (CWE-787): capacity is nspace_max_count = element->attribute_count+1 at line 15, allocated at lines 21-22. The attribute loop (line 40) appends up to two entries per attribute: the namespace declaration at lines 58-64 and this unconditional attribute entry. With attribute_count=1, element->name->nspace out of scope (line 28 true) and attributes[0]->nspace out of scope and != name nspace (line 45 true, dedup at 51-55 leaves declare_me=1), nspace_declarations_count reaches 2, so this write targets index 2 of a 2-element array. No guard constrains nspace_declarations_count < nspace_max_count. Absent fix: size as attribute_count*2+1 (+declared_nspaces+xml_language) or a bounds check before the append.

Out-of-bounds read (CWE-125): the dedup loop bound j < nspace_declarations_count (line 51) lets j reach nspace_declarations_count-1, which the attribute loop raises to up to 1+2*attribute_count and thus beyond attribute_count-1. With attribute_count=2 and count=3 (element name declaration plus first attribute's namespace and attribute entries), j=2 reads element->attributes[2], outside the attribute_count-element attributes array indexed elsewhere as attributes[i] (lines 42, 59, 71). Absent fix: compare element->attributes[i]->nspace instead of element->attributes[j]->nspace, or bound j by attribute_count.

assumptions: The vulnerable append path requires nstack non-NULL, which every write under nstack's guard satisfies at lines 14, 28, 39, 44, 81, and 108.
element->attribute_count equals the length of element->attributes as used by the loop at line 40.
raptor_namespace_format_as_xml / raptor_qname_format_as_xml return NULL on failure and the fragment checks those results (lines 32, 61, 73).
limitations: Integer overflow of nspace_max_count (int) near INT_MAX would need attribute_count near INT_MAX and is not required for the demonstrated small-count witness.
The xml_language buffer sizing relative to raptor_xml_escape_string behavior (lines 111-122) depends on the unshown helper and was not used for the verdict.
Signed/unsigned conversions between int nspace_max_count (line 15) and the size_t count are harmless for the admitted witness and not relied on.

verdict.summary: The inode-in-ICB length iinfo->i_lenAlloc reaches page-cache sinks with no upper-bound guard: memcpy at lines 34-35 copies i_lenAlloc bytes into a PAGE_SIZE page (OOB write for i_lenAlloc > PAGE_SIZE), and memset at lines 32-33 uses PAGE_SIZE - i_lenAlloc, which underflows to a huge length while the base pointer is already past the page. The only i_lenAlloc check (line 9) excludes only zero.

evidence.reason: iinfo->i_lenAlloc is unsigned with residual range {1..UINT_MAX} after the line 9 guard `if (!iinfo->i_lenAlloc)`, which admits every nonzero value and is the only guard on the field. With no check constraining it to the dest capacity PAGE_SIZE (the page produced at line 26 by find_or_create_page, NULL-checked at line 27), i_lenAlloc=4097 copies 4097 bytes into a 4096-byte page: OOB write (CWE-787). The absent one-statement fix is an upper-bound check `if (iinfo->i_lenAlloc > PAGE_SIZE) return -EIO;` before line 30.

The same unbounded i_lenAlloc is used both as a page offset and in `PAGE_SIZE - iinfo->i_lenAlloc`, computed in unsigned arithmetic. For the line 9-admitted witness i_lenAlloc=4097, the length underflows to a huge value (CWE-190 corrupting the size) and the base kaddr + i_lenAlloc points past the end of the PAGE_SIZE page from line 26, producing an OOB write (CWE-787). No guard between line 9 and line 32 constrains i_lenAlloc's upper bound.

assumptions: iinfo->i_lenAlloc and iinfo->i_lenEAttr are unsigned 32-bit fields of struct udf_inode_info whose values derive from the on-disk UDF in-ICB layout; their declarations are outside the shown fragment.
The page returned by find_or_create_page at line 26 has capacity PAGE_SIZE, and kaddr at line 31 maps its full extent.
The failure set is i_lenAlloc > PAGE_SIZE for the compiler's PAGE_SIZE constant; the analysis uses PAGE_SIZE (typically 4096) as the capacity named in the fragment.
limitations: The capacity of iinfo->i_data (UDF_EXTENDED_AD_IN_ICB_SIZE) is not declared in the fragment, so the i_data-addressed memset at lines 41-42, the error-path memcpy at line 59, and the i_data source read at line 34 are not independently confirmable OOB and are excluded from the verdict.

The fragment does not show the caller or the ICB parser that assigns i_lenAlloc; a caller that pre-validated i_lenAlloc <= PAGE_SIZE could not trigger the bug, but no such invariant is shown and none is assumed.
No loops exist in the fragment, so Phase 3 loop analysis is vacuous.

With i_lenAlloc = 4097, PAGE_SIZE - i_lenAlloc underflows to a huge unsigned size and memcpy copies 4097 bytes into a 4096-byte page, producing a heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).

With disk-derived iinfo->i_lenAlloc = 4097 (admitted by the line 9 fall-through and by lines 27/30), PAGE_SIZE - iinfo->i_lenAlloc wraps in unsigned arithmetic to a huge size, so the memset writes far beyond the page: CWE-787. Absent fix: validation that iinfo->i_lenAlloc <= PAGE_SIZE before this use.

assumptions: iinfo->i_lenAlloc, iinfo->i_lenEAttr, and inode->i_size are populated from on-disk UDF inode (ICB) metadata, i.e., entry-point input; no uploader in the fragment bounds them.
find_or_create_page (line 26) returns a page whose capacity is PAGE_SIZE, corroborated by the fragment's own use of PAGE_SIZE as the page size at line 33.
memset/memcpy follow standard kernel semantics (dest must hold the full count; unsigned size arithmetic wraps).
limitations: S3 (memset of iinfo->i_data at lines 41-42) and S4 (restore memcpy at line 59) also consume unconstrained lengths, but iinfo->i_data's capacity is not declared in the fragment, and S4 additionally requires filemap_fdatawrite() to fail; they are demoted rather than independently confirmed.
The source read at line 34 (iinfo->i_data + iinfo->i_lenEAttr) could read out of bounds for large i_lenEAttr/i_lenAlloc, but no source-buffer capacity is shown, so CWE-125 is not claimed.
No loops exist in the fragment, so Phase 3 loop-bound issues are vacuous.

`kiocb_set_rw_flags()` nonzero return is fully handled by the return at line 17 (status-tracked).

Helper bodies (`io_file_get_flags`, `iocb_flags`, `kiocb_set_rw_flags`, `io_file_supports_nowait`, `io_req_ffs_set`) are not shown; their internal behavior beyond the standard semantics asserted above is out of scope.

sysfs store buffers are treated as entry-point input per sysfs/kernfs semantics, but no unconstrained value reaches a sink because of the shown guard.
limitations: The body of dlpar_add_slot is not shown; only that its return status is checked, so its internal behavior is not evaluated.
No loops are present in the fragment, so loop-bound analysis is not applicable.

evidence.reason: Decisive capacity guard: per-row allocation = MagickMax(bytes_per_line, image->columns+256UL) >= bytes_per_line computed at line 449, so the whole buffer holds rows*bytes_per_line = length bytes (line 450); every row loop (p=pixels+(image->rows-y-1)*bytes_per_line at 617/661/708/755/811/856) reads <= bytes_per_line per row, bounding max offset to length-1 and excluding any out-of-bounds read.
Fail-closed status check: a short read (count != length) throws before any row loop consumes the pixel buffer, excluding partial-fill input from reaching the conversion sinks.

Guard-identity-compliant stride fix for RLE: DecodeImage writes exactly image->columns*image->rows bytes (extent at 482-483), and this sets the case-8 row stride to image->columns so the row reads match the decode extent exactly; excludes any stride/capacity mismatch for RLE4/RLE8.

Loop-bound evidence: with image->columns >= 1 (width<=0 thrown at 325), the case-1 loop admits x <= columns-8 and bit <= 7, so SetPixelIndex indexes x+bit <= columns-1, never reaching past the columns-wide index cache; degenerate columns (e.g., 1-7) are covered by the columns%8 remainder loop.

assumptions: 64-bit size_t arithmetic: with width <= 2^31-1 (signed 32-bit read at 154 plus width<=0 check at 325) and rows <= 2^31 (height read at 155, zero-check at 327), bytes_per_line (<= 4*2^31) * rows (<= 2^31) < 2^64, so length does not wrap.
AcquireVirtualMemory/SetImageExtent return failure paths are shown and are fail-closed (NULL check at 458/479, status==MagickFalse return at 385).
Colormap paths only run for PseudoClass (bpp < 16, line 367), so image->colors <= 1<<bpp <= 256.
limitations: DecodeImage's body is not shown; only its extent (columns*rows) and status check are visible, and the allocated buffer is >= that extent.

On 32-bit size_t builds, image->columns*bits_per_pixel and bytes_per_line*rows could wrap for extreme dimensions; SetImageExtent/Allocation overflow checks and the length/8 vs blob-size check likely fail closed, so this is hardening-level and not confirmed by the fragment.
MagickAbsoluteValue of INT_MIN height and shifts by 32 in the mask-scan loops are undefined-behavior corners with no exploitable consequence derivable from the shown code.
file_size/blob-size mismatch is only warned (317-324), which is informational, not a security sink.
