verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation in the fragment is protected by a verifiable guard: TIFFScanlineSize() result is rejected when <=0 before the size_t promotion and allocations; bits_per_sample and samples_per_pixel are range-capped before buffer-size arithmetic; rows_per_strip is clamped; all allocations and libtiff read calls are NULL/status checked. No in-fragment derivation admits a value that exceeds a shown capacity, so no confirmed vulnerability.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement. scanline_size is assigned at line 592 from TIFFScanlineSize(tiff) (entry-point-derived, ssize_t, full domain) and this guard executes before every later use: the (MagickSizeType) cast at line 600, AcquireVirtualMemory at line 601, and ResetMagickMemory at line 605. It excludes the entire failure set (every value <= 0), so a negative/huge scanline_size cannot be promoted to a massive size_t nor distort the 1.5*number_pixels sizing. Guard-identity audit passes: no assignment or transformation occurs between the check and the uses (no drift).

Protective validation of entry-point bits_per_sample (uint16, full domain at line 162). Admitted set is [1,32] plus exactly {64} when sample_format==SAMPLEFORMAT_IEEEFP; excluded are 0 and 33..65535 (and 64 for non-float). The same value is consumed unchanged at lines 595-596 (pow(2.0,ceil(log(bits_per_sample)/log(2.0))) <= 64) and at line 422 (palette colors = 2^bits <= 65536), with no intervening write, so the guard fully constrains the buffer-size arithmetic that follows.

Protective cap on entry-point samples_per_pixel (uint16, line 162): admitted set is [0,32] (MaxPixelChannels==32 at line 4), excluding >=33. This bounds every dependent size factor in the fragment, including 4*(samples_per_pixel+1) used for strip_extent (line 730) and tile_extent (line 825), the samples loops at lines 739 and 832, and number_pixels at lines 595-596. Same value, no drift.

Protected sink. number_pixels here is fully constrained before use: scanline_size >= 1 (guard at 593) and <= 1.5*number_pixels (guard at 598), bits_per_sample in [1,32] or {IEEEFP,64} (guard at 171-172), samples_per_pixel <= 32 (guard at 177), rows_per_strip <= image->rows (clamp at 568-569), and image->columns/rows <= 2^32-1 so the size_t products at lines 595-596 and 605 cannot wrap on a 64-bit size_t. The allocation failure is handled at line 602, so line 605 is unreachable with an invalid size. Buffer consumers (TIFFReadPixels at line 676, strip/tile/generic loops) read at most scanline_size/TIFFStripSize/TIFFTileSize/columns*rows bytes, all within the corresponding guarded capacities.

assumptions: libtiff tag contracts hold as documented: TIFFTAG_COLORMAP returns 1<<bits_per_sample entries per channel, TIFFTAG_EXTRASAMPLES returns an array of exactly extra_samples entries in sample_info, WHITEPOINT returns >=2 floats and PRIMARYCHROMATICITIES >=6 floats.
Analysis assumes a 64-bit size_t platform, on which image->columns*image->rows (each <= 2^32-1) and number_pixels*sizeof(uint32) cannot wrap; this is consistent with the fragment's own guards.
AcquireVirtualMemory/AcquireQuantumMemory return NULL on failure and are always NULL-checked in the fragment.
limitations: Zero TileWidth/TileLength values could in principle make the x+=columns / y+=rows loops non-terminating (lines 849-860); rejection of such values depends on unshown libtiff semantics and HeapOverflowSanityCheck behavior, so this is demoted from a confirmed finding.

On a hypothetical 32-bit size_t build, rows*TIFFTileRowSize(tiff) (line 825) or columns*rows (line 921) could wrap; the in-fragment HeapOverflowSanityCheck guards only rows, so a platform-specific overflow is not derivable strictly from the shown code.
TIFFReadRGBAImage failure is checked only for return value -1 (line 928); other failure-return conventions of that unshown callee are not treated as confirmed.
row_per_strip == 0 (malformed ROWSPERSTRIP tag) handling of rows_remaining (size_t decrement at line 784) depends on unshown libtiff strip-size computation and is not confirmed harmful in-fragment.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the patched hfsplus_block_allocate: every page pointer is used only after an IS_ERR() check, all bitmap reads/writes are bounded by curr < end with end <= pptr + PAGE_CACHE_BITS/32, the found start is validated with start >= size, len is clamped with min(size - start, len), and the full-u32 write loop exits via the len < 32 -> last gate at the word containing the last allocatable bit. No dangerous operation admits an unconstrained value.

evidence.reason: Guard-identity-sound IS_ERR check placed immediately after read_mapping_page (17) and before the first kmap/deref (22, 32); the same check re-guards every later page re-read (63, 114), so the ERR_PTR failure set of read_mapping_page never reaches kmap() or any *curr access on any path.

Excludes every found position start = offset + (curr - pptr)*32 + i (78) with start >= size; start is consumed unchanged by the clamp at line 84 and the accounting at line 135, so no check-then-use or type drift; this protects the write phase from ever allocating at/above the bitmap bound.

Clamps the requested length to the exact remaining bit range size - start, so the write phase can never mark bits at or beyond size; combined with the len < 32 gate it bounds every full-u32 write to words strictly inside the region.

Stops the while (curr < end) write loop (98) at the word overlapping bit (size-1), so *curr++ = cpu_to_be32(0xffffffff) (106) and the final *curr = cpu_to_be32(n) (132) never touch words past the allocation region, even though the write-phase advance sets end to a full page (120).

Bounds the scan-phase page advance (58) so the while(1) loop (44) terminates at the bitmap bound; the offset >= size break precedes each page re-read (61), preventing scanning beyond the bitmap and ensuring the 'bitmap full' path (73-75) is reached.

assumptions: PAGE_CACHE_BITS is the per-page bit capacity (upstream PAGE_SIZE*8), so PAGE_CACHE_BITS/32 is one page's u32 word count and end = pptr + PAGE_CACHE_BITS/32 is the last full page word.
read_mapping_page returns an ERR_PTR on failure and never NULL, so IS_ERR(page) fully guards the subsequent kmap/deref.
limitations: The write-phase advance (lines 111-120) has no offset >= size break (unlike the scan phase at 59); safety there rests on len <= size - start clamping, which was verified to stop writes at the final region word.

For a crafted volume with size >= 0xFFFF8000 blocks and a fully-set >=512 MiB bitmap, the u32 advance offset += PAGE_CACHE_BITS at line 58 could in theory wrap and make the scan loop non-terminating; this is not fixed upstream and depends on unshown caller/file-size facts, so it is not confirmed as a reachable in-fragment failure.
No call site for hfsplus_block_allocate is shown, so provenance of size/offset/*max is classified as internal-helper parameters; all conclusions are drawn from in-fragment constraints only.

verdict.summary: The BMP reader fragment carries protective statements for every dangerous operation: signed width reads rejected at width<=0 (L332), height!=0 (L334), colors capped to 2^bpp<=256 (L342-382), exact count checks on colormap and pixel reads (L428, L472), per-row pixel capacity with +256 RLE slack (L463-464/484-485), DecodeImage status check (L491), bounded scanline loops, and the offset_bits repeat guard for loop termination (L448). No admitted value reaches an unprotected sink.

evidence.reason: Protective guard for every width-derived sink: it excludes the full failure set {0, negative} of the entry-point width (L127/128 short or L153/154 signed long) before columns=MagickAbsoluteValue(width) (L369) and SetImageExtent (L391). Admitted set is [1,32767] (OS/2) or [1,2^31-1] (Windows), so all scanline loop bounds (L629, L673, L720, L766, L825, L869) index within [0,columns-1] and bytes_per_line stays positive. No assignment or cast intervenes between check and use, so the guard passes the identity audit.

Capacity statement for the pixel buffer used by every conversion loop: each row is max(bytes_per_line, columns+256) bytes, so the RLE decoder (L489) has the +256 slack and each recomputed row stride (L712, L758, L818, L858) is bounded by the allocated per-row size; the same guard appears at L484-485 for the RLE branch. Allocation failure is fail-closed at L465/L486.

Return-status guard on the file-to-buffer copy: a short read (count != length, e.g. truncated file after the loose length/8 check at L458) throws before any conversion loop consumes the buffer, so no partially-filled buffer reaches the pixel sinks.

Return-status guard on the colormap read: colors is capped at 2^bits_per_pixel <= 256 by L342-344 and normalized from 0 at L382-383, the buffer is 4*colors bytes (L413-414), and the exact-count check fails closed, so the subsequent colormap[i] writes (L437-439, loop bound i < colors at L435) stay inside the allocated colormap.

Termination/robustness guard on the multi-frame do-while loop: it excludes re-seeking to a frame offset already processed (the seek at L451 would otherwise re-read the same header forever), and together with *magick='\0' (L947) and the EOF short-read break (L954) the loop always terminates on malformed input.

assumptions: Natural 64-bit size_t/ssize_t platform, matching the declared ssize_t width/height provenance and MagickOffsetType arithmetic.

Standard callee semantics for ReadBlob (returns actual byte count), AcquireVirtualMemory/AcquireQuantumMemory (NULL on failure), DecodeImage (writes within the passed extent and returns status), QueueAuthenticPixels (NULL on failure), IsValidColormapIndex (bounds-checked).
colors for PseudoClass images is bounded to <= 256 by the visible checks at L342-344 combined with the zero-default at L382-383.
limitations: On a 32-bit size_t build, image->columns*bits_per_pixel (L456) can wrap; the fragment's other guards (allocation NULL checks L465/L486, count checks L472) make this a robustness concern rather than a demonstrated in-fragment corruption, so it is not the verdict driver.

The mask-shift loops (L553-614) can evaluate an out-of-range shift for attacker-chosen masks; this is undefined behavior, not a memory-safety sink with a derivable failing value, and no downstream operation is shown to consume a corrupted value.
The pair counterpart is not shown; the verdict rests on the protective statements visible in this fragment passing the Guard-Identity Audit.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the patched side of the pair. The strict `>` guard admits `p > line` and excludes exactly `p == line`, leaving an empty intersection with the failure set; no statement between lines 218 and 220 re-assigns `p` (Guard-Identity pass, no drift). This one comparison operator is the added fix that neutralizes the OOB read.

assumptions: p, incl_regmatch.startp[0], and incl_regmatch.endp[0] are pointers into `line` because vim_regexec is called on `line` (lines 105, 315, 347), bounding all later pointer arithmetic to the line buffer.
IObuff is an IOSIZE-byte buffer as used by STRNCPY at lines 419 and 457 and vim_snprintf(IObuff, IOSIZE, ...) at line 290.

`STRNCPY(IObuff, aux, i)` at line 419 relies on the comment's assertion `IOSIZE > compl_length` (line 418); `ins_compl_len()`'s domain is not bounded by shown code, and a length ≥ IOSIZE requires an unshown completion state that cannot be derived from the fragment.

The `IObuff[i-1]`/`IObuff[i-2]` reads (lines 442–451) assume `i >= ins_compl_len() >= 1` and a non-whitespace word start via skipwhite; the degenerate `i == 0` case needs `ins_compl_len() == 0`, which no shown statement produces.

verdict.summary: OP_JMPUW computes the jump offset a as (uint32_t)((pc - irep->iseq) + (int16_t)a) at line 302 and uses it at line 322 as pc = irep->iseq + a with no runtime bounds check against irep->ilen. A negative sum (operand -1 at the first instruction) wraps to a = 0xFFFFFFFF, and the restore path sets a directly from the stored break value; only the debug-only mrb_assert at line 308 and the ensure-handler range test at line 314 (skipped when ch == NULL) exist, so the next instruction fetch reads out of bounds.

evidence.reason: Sink is pointer arithmetic on mrb_code* with index a of type uint32_t (declared line 11). a is set unconstrained at line 302 ((uint32_t)((pc - irep->iseq) + (int16_t)a)) and at line 307 ((uint32_t)mrb_integer(target)); the only apparent guards do not constrain it: line 308 is a debug-only mrb_assert (no-op in release builds, and a >= 0 is tautological for unsigned), and line 314 compares a only against the ensure handler [begin,end) range and is skipped when catch_handler_find returns NULL. Degenerate witness derived in-fragment: JMPUW at pc - irep->iseq == 0 with operand -1 yields a = 0xFFFFFFFF (unsigned wrap, CWE-195/CWE-125), or operand ilen - d + 1 yields a = ilen + 1; both are admitted on the main path (ch == NULL) and on the restore path (assert disabled) and cause an out-of-bounds instruction fetch after line 322. Absent fix: a runtime bounds check such as 'if (a >= irep->ilen)' before the pc assignment.

assumptions: irep->ilen is the number of instructions in the current irep, so the valid program-counter range is [irep->iseq, irep->iseq + irep->ilen).
mrb_assert is a debug-only assertion macro that compiles to a no-op in release builds (no MRB_DEBUG), so it is not a runtime protective statement.
Bytecode operands (including the OP_JMPUW signed offset) and the restored break value are attacker-controlled when untrusted .mrb bytecode is loaded (mrb_load_irep/mrb_load_nstring).
a is declared uint32_t (line 11), so the conversion at line 302 from a negative signed sum yields a large unsigned value.
limitations: Other reads in the fragment (pool/sym string lengths at OP_STRING/OP_SYMBOL/OP_ERR, syms[b], L935 catch-handler target, generic regs[a] register indexing) have their capacity validated outside the shown fragment (irep loader/compiler), so they are not confirmed here.
OP_ENTER register writes assume the callee frame nregs covers len and argc; that invariant is not shown in the fragment.

If the paired member of this pair is the version that adds the line-308 assert, the same out-of-bounds pc read still exists on the main path, so this fragment cannot be the fully fixed member under release-build semantics.
